sourceDefinition: (T, S, M, Msb, K) and A_ilayohi , (M, K,) aor. , (T, Msb, K,) inf. n. A^a*anN , (T, S, Msb, K,) He [gave ear or] listened to it, (T, S, M, Msb, K,) or him: (T, S, M, K: *) or it signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (M,) he listened to it, or him, pleased, or being pleased. (M, K.) It is said in a trad., (T,) maA A^a*ina A@ll~`hi li$aYo'K linabiY~K yatagan~aY bAlqurA=ni (T, S) God hath not listened to anything [in a manner] like his listening [to a prophet chanting the Kur-án ]. (T.) And in the Kur [lxxxiv. 2 and 5], waA^a*inato lirab~ihA And shall listen to its Lord, (M, Bd, Jel,) and obey; (Jel;) i. e., shall submit to the influence of his power as one listens to the commander and submits to him. (Bd.) And you say, A^a*ina lil~ahowi He listened and inclined to sport, or play. (M.) ― -b2- [Hence, perhaps,] A^a*ina liraAy^iHapi AlT~aEaAmi (assumed tropical:) He desired eagerly, or longed for, the food, [perceiving its odour, ] (ISh, K,) and inclined to it. (ISh, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also, app.,] A^a*ina lahu fiY Al$~aY' , (S, M, K,) or fiY A^amori ka*aA , (T,) or fiY ka*aA , (Msb,) aor. , (T, K,) inf. n. A_i*onN , (T, S, M, K,) or this is a simple subst., (Msb,) and A^a*iynN , (K,) [as though originally signifying He gave ear to him in respect of such a thing; and then] he permitted him, allowed him, or gave him permission or leave, to do the thing, or such a thing. (M, Msb, K.) [See also A_i*onN , below.] You say, A^a*inotu liloEabodi fay Alt~ijaArapi [ I gave permission, or leave, to the slave to traffic ]. (Msb.) ― -b4- A^a*ina lahu Ealayohi He took, or got, permission, or leave, for him from him. (M.) You say, Aiy*ano liY EalaY AlA^amiyri (S, TA) Take thou, or get thou, permission for me from the commander, or governor, or prince. (TA.) El-A'azz Ibn-'AbdAllah says, wa A_in~iY A_i*aA Dan~a AlA^amiyru bA_i*onihi Ealay AlA_i*ni mino nafosiY A_i*A $iy^otN qaAdirN [ And verily I, when the prince is niggardly of his permission, am able to take permission of myself when I will ]. (TA.) And a poet says, qulotu libaw~aAbK ladayohi daAruhaA tiy^o*ano faA_in~iY Hayow^uhaA wajaAruhaA [ I said to a door-keeper, near by whom was her house, take thou, or get thou, permission for me to enter, for I am her husband's father, and her neighbour ]: meaning, says Aboo-Jaafar, litaA^o*ano ; for the suppression of the l is allowable in poetry, and the pronunciation with kesr to the t is accord. to the dial. of him who says A^anota tiEolamu . (S.) ― -b5- A^a*ina biAl$~aY'i , (S, * M, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, M, K,) inf. n. A_i*onN and A^a*anN and A^a*aAnN and A^a*aAnapN , (M, K,) He knew the thing; knew of it; had knowledge of it; became informed, or apprized, of it. (S, M, Msb, K.) sourceDefinition: , (S, M, K,) inf. n. taA^o*iynN , (K,) He wrung, or twisted, ( Earaka ,) his (a boy's, S) ear: (S, K:) or he struck, ( Daraba , TA,) or struck with his finger, or fillipped, ( naqara , M, TA,) his ear. (M, TA.) [See also A^a*anahu .] They say, (in a prov., TA in art. jwz ,) likul~i jaAbihK jawozapN vum~a yuw^o*~anu , (M, TA,) i. e. For every one that comes to water is a single watering for his family and his cattle; then his ear is struck, to apprize him that he has nothing more to receive from them: (TA in the present art., and the like is said in the same in art. jwz :) or, (assumed tropical:) then he is repelled from the water: (TA in art. jwz :) [for A^*~nhu signifies also] ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) He repelled him, (IAar, T, M, K,) namely, a man, (IAar, T, M,) from drinking, (K,) and did not give him to drink. (M, K.) You say also, A^a*~inuwA Ean~iY A^uwalahaA , [in which the pronoun appears, from the context, to relate to camels,] (assumed tropical:) Send ye away from me the first ones of them. (En-Nadr, T.) -A2- A^*~n Aln~aEola , (inf. n. as above, S,) He put to the sandal what is termed A^u*unN , q. v. infrà: (S, M, K:) and in like manner one says with respect to other things. (S, K.) -A3- A^*~n , (M, K,) inf. n. as above, (K,) also signifies He made known, or notified, a thing ( bi$aYo'K ) much; (M, K; *) he proclaimed, or made proclamation; syn. naAdaY : (Jel in vii. 42, and Bd and Jel in xii. 70 and xxii. 28:) Sb says that some of the Arabs make A^a*~ana and ↓ A=*ana to be syn.: but some say that the former signifies he called out publickly; and the latter, i. q. A^aEolama [ he made to know, &c.: see 4]. (M, TA.) It is said in the Kur [xxii. 28], waA^a*~ino fiY Aln~aAsi biAlHaj~i (M) And proclaim thou, among the people, the pilgrimage. (Bd, Jel.) ― -b2- Also, (S, K,) or A^*~n biAlS~alaApi , (Msb,) inf. n. as above, (M, K,) or A^a*aAnN , (S,) or both, (TA,) or the latter is [properly speaking] a simple subst. [used as an inf. n.], as in the instances of wad~aEa wadaAE~aA and sal~ama salaAmFA and kal~ama kalaAmFA &c., (Msb,) He called to prayer; (M, K;) he notified, or made known, or proclaimed, [i. e., chanted, from the miy^o*anap ,] the time of prayer; (S, * Msb, * TA;) and ↓ A=*ana signifies the same, (K,) inf. n. A_iy*aAnN . (TA.) IB says, the phrase A^a*~ana AlEaSoru , with the verb in the act. form, [a phrase commonly obtaining in the present day,] is wrong; the correct expression being A^u*~ina biAlEaSori [ The time of the prayer of afternoon was proclaimed, i. e., chanted ], with the verb in the pass. form, and with the preposition to connect it with its subject. (Msb.) ― -b3- You say also, A^a*~ana biA_irosaAli A_ibilihi He spoke of sending away his camels. (En-Nadr, T.)

And AstA^*n fiY Ald~uxuwli Elyh , and, elliptically, AstA^*n Elyh , He asked, or demanded, permission, or leave, to go in to him. ]

sourceDefinition: [is held by some to be an inf. n., like ↓ A^a*ayinN : (see 1:) by others, to be] a simple subst.; (Msb;) signifying Permission; leave; or concession of liberty, to do a thing: and sometimes command: and likewise will; (Msb, TA;) as in the phrase biA_i*oni A@ll~`hi by the will of God: (Msb:) or, accord. to El-Harállee, the withdrawal, or removal, of prevention or prohibition, and the giving of power or ability, in respect of being and creation: or, accord. to Ibn-El-Kemál, the rescission of prohibition, and concession of freedom of action, to him who has been prohibited by law: or, accord. to Er-Rághib, the notification of the allowance or permission of a thing, and of indulgence in respect of it; as in A_il~aA liyuTaAEa biA_i*oni A@ll~`hi , [in the Kur iv. 67,] meaning [ but that he may be obeyed ] by the will of God, and [also] by his command: (TA:) or, as explained in the Ksh, facilitation; an explanation founded upon the opinion that the actions of men are by their own effective power, but facilitated by God; and in this sense, Esh-Shiháb regards it as a metaphor, or a non-metaphorical trope: (MF:) and accommodation; syn. tawofiyqN ; (Hr in explanation of a clause of iii. 139 of the Kur [which see below];) but Es-Semeen says that this requires consideration. (TA.) ― -b2- Also Knowledge; syn. EilomN ; (T, M, K;) and so ↓ A^a*iynN ; (M, K;) as in the saying faEalahu biA_i*oniY (T, * M, K) and ↓ biA^a*iynY (M, K) [ He did it with my knowledge ]: or A_i*onN has a more particular signification than EilomN , being scarcely ever, or never, used save of that [ knowledge ] wherein is will, conjoined with command or not conjoined therewith; for in the saying [in the Kur iii. 139, referred to above,] wamaA kaAna linafosK A^ano tamuwta A_il~aA biA_i*oni A@ll~`hi [ And it is not for a soul to die save with the knowledge of God ], it is known that there are will and command; and in the saying [in the Kur ii. 96], wamaA humo biD~aAriyna bihi mino A^aHadK A_il~aA bA_i*oni A@ll~`hi [ But they do not injure thereby any one save with the knowledge of God ], there is will in one respect, for there is no difference of opinion as to the fact that God hath made to exist in man a faculty wherein is the power of injuring another: (Er-Rághib:) but Es-Semeen says that this plea is adduced by Er-Rághib because of his inclining to the persuasion of the Moatezileh. (TA.) You say also, faEalotu ka*aA biA_i*onihi meaning I did thus by his command. (T.)

definition: and ↓ A^u*onN , (S, M, Msb, K,) the latter a contraction of the former, [which is the more common,] (Msb,) [The ear;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ A^u*onN , (S, M, Msb, K,) the latter a contraction of the former, [which is the more common,] (Msb,) [The ear; ] one of the organs of sense; (M, TA;) well known: (M:) of the fem. gender: (S, M, Msb, K:) as also ↓ A^a*iynN : (K:) pl. A=*aAnN , (S, M, Msb, K,) its only pl. form: (M:) dim. ↓ A^u*ayonapN ; but when used as a proper name of a man, A^u*ayonu , though A^u*ayonapu has been heard. (S.) You say, jaA='a naA$ir~aA A^u*unayohi [ He came spreading, or, as we say, pricking up, his ears: meaning] (tropical:) he came in a state of covetousness, or eagerness. (T, K, TA. [See also na$ara .]) And wajadotu fulaAnFA laA bisFA A^u*unayohi (tropical:) I found such a one feigning himself inattentive, or heedless. (T, TA.) And labisotu A^u*unaY~a lahu (tropical:) I turned away from him, avoided him, or shunned him: or I feigned myself inattentive, or heedless, to him. (K, TA. [See also labisa .]) ― -b2- (tropical:) A man who listens to what is said to him: (M, K, TA:) or a man who hears the speech of every one: (S:) or who relies upon what is said to him; as also waAbiSapu Als~amoEi : (M in art. wbS :) applied as an epithet to one and to a pl. number, (S, M, K,) alike, (S, M,) and to two, and to a woman; not being pluralized nor dualized [nor having the fem. form given to it]: (IB:) you say rajulN A^N*onN (AZ, S, M) and A^u*onN , and rijaAlN A^u*unN and A^u*onN [&c.]: (AZ, M:) and sometimes it is applied to a man as a name of evil import. (M.) It is said in the Kur [ix. 61], wayaquwluwna huwa A^u*unN qulo A^u*unu xayorK lakumo (T, M) And they say, “He is one who hears and believes everything that is said to him:” as though, by reason of the excess of his listening, he were altogether the organ of hearing; like as a spy is termed EayonN ; or A^u*un is here from A^a*ina “he listened,” and is like A^unufN and $ululN in its derivation: (Bd:) for among the hypocrites was he who found fault with the Prophet, saying, “If anything be told him from me, I swear to him, and he receives it from me, because he is an A^u*un :” (M:) therefore he is commanded to answer, Say, “A hearer of good for you.” (T, M, Bd.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) A sincere, or faithful, adviser of a people, who counsels to obedience: (Msb:) a man's intimate, and special, or particular, friend. (TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A certain appertenance of the heart; (M;) [i. e. either auricle thereof;] A^u*unaA Alqalobi signifying two appendages ( zanamataAni ) in the upper part of the heart: (K:) and (tropical:) of a naSol [or arrow-head or the like; i. e. either wing thereof]: and (tropical:) of an arrow; A=*aAnu Als~ahomi signifying the feathers of the arrow, as AHn says, when they are attached thereon; and *uw valaAvi A=*aAnK [ a thing having three such feathers ] meaning an arrow: all so called by way of comparison: (M:) and (assumed tropical:) of a sandal; (S, M, K;) i. e. the part thereof that surrounds the qibaAl [q. v.]: (M:) or A^u*unaA Aln~aEoli signifies the two parts, [or loops, ] of the sandal, to which are tied the EaDudaAni of the $iraAk , [or two branches of the thong that is attached to another thong between two of the toes, which two branches, however, sometimes pass through the A^u*unaAni , encompassing the heel, ] behind the narrow part ( xaSor ) of the sole. (AO in an anonymous MS in my possession. See also xaSorN .) ― -b5- (tropical:) A handle, (M,) or [ a loopshaped, or an ear-shaped, handle, such as is termed ] Eurowap , (T, K,) of anything; (M, K) as, for instance, (M,) of a kuwz [or mug]; (T, M;) and of a dalow [or bucket]: so called by way of comparison: and in all cases fem.: (M:) pl. as above. (T.) ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) What becomes sharp, or pointed, and then falls off, or out, of the plants called Earofaj and vumaAm when they put forth their xuwS [q. v.], or when their xwS become perfect; because it has the shape of an ear. (AHn, M.)

sourceDefinition: A making known; a notification; an announcement. (T, S, Mgh.) [See 4.] So in the Kur [ix. 3], wa A^a*aAnN mina A@ll~`hi warasuwlihi A_ilaY Aln~aAsi [ And a notification, or an announcement, from God and his apostle to men, or the people ]. (M, K.) (TA.) [This (which is chanted in the mosque) consists of the words of the former A^a*aAn with the addition of qado qaAmati AlS~alaAho pronounced twice after HaYa EalaY AlfalaAHo .] ― -b4- AlA^a*aAnaAni signifies The A^a*aAni [ more commonly so called ] and the A_iqaAmap . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ A^ufoqN (S, K) A side; meaning a lateral, or an outward or adjacent, part or portion; or a part, region, quarter, or tract, considered with respect to its collocation or juxtaposition or direction, or considered as belonging to a whole; or a remote side; syn. naAHiyapN ; (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K;) and a border, or an extremity; (JK;) of a land, or of the earth; and of the sky, or heavens: (JK, Mgh, Msb:) [or the horizon, or part next to the horizon, of the sky and of the earth; ] or what appears of the sides ( Aln~awaAHiY ) of the celestial sphere, (K, TA,) and of the borders, or extremities, of the earth: (TA:) or the place whence blows the south wind, and the north wind, and the west wind, and the east wind: (K, * TA:) pl. A=faAqN : (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K:) and the sing. also is used as a pl.; like fulokN , as is said in the Nh: (MF:) thus in the verse of El-'Abbás, in praise of the Prophet: A^anota lam~a wulidota A^a$oraqati AlA^aro DuwaDaA='a to binuwrika AlA^ufuqu [ When thou wast born, the earth became bright, and the tracts of the horizon, or the regions, shone with thy light ]: or, as some say, AlAfq is made fem. by him as meaning Aln~aAHiyapu . (TA.) The phrase Hiyna yagiybu AlA^ufuqu means When the redness, or whiteness, in the A^ufuq [or horizon ] disappears. (Mgh.) ― -b2- Also, in like manner, The side, or lateral part, of a tent: (JK:) or the part between the [ two ] anterior [ pieces of wood called the ] zir~aAni , in the [ fore part called the ] riwaAq , of a tent: (K:) and the sides, or lateral parts, of a tent of the kind belonging to the Arabs of the desert. (TA.) -A2- A^ufuqN is also said to be a pl. of A^afiyqN ; but this is disallowed by Lh. (TA.) -A3- See also A=fiqN .

(TA.)

definition: is a pronoun, denoting the speaker, [ I, masc.
sourceDefinition: is a pronoun, denoting the speaker, [ I, masc. and fem.,] in the language of some of the Arabs: they say, A^ano faEalotu [ I did ], with the n quiescent: but most of them pronounce it [↓ A^ana ] with fet-h when conjoined with a following word; (Mughnee, K;) saying, A^ana faEalotu : (TA:) and [↓ A^anaA ] with A in a case of pause: (Mughnee, K:) and some pronounce it with A also when it is conjoined with a following word; saying, A^anaA faEalotu ; [as we generally find it written in books;] but this is of a bad dialect: (TA:) [this last assertion, however, requires consideration; for the dial. here said to be bad is that of Temeem, accord. to what here follows:] the Basrees hold that the pronoun consists of the ' and the n , and that the [final] A is redundant, because it is suppressed in a case of conjunction with a following word; but the Koofees hold that the pronoun is composed of all the three letters, because the A is preserved in a case of conjunction with a following word in the dial. of Temeem. (Marginal note in a copy of the Mughnee.) [Accord. to Az,] it is best to say ↓ A^anaA in a case of pause; and ↓ A^ana in a case of conjunction with a following word, as in A^ana faEalotu *aAka [ I did that ]; but some of the Arabs say, faEalotu *aAka ↓ A^anaA ; and some make the n quiescent in a case of this kind, though this is rare, saying, A^ano qulotu *aAka [ I said that ]; and Kudá'ah prolong the former A , saying, qulotuhu ↓ A=na . (T.) [Accord. to J,] ↓ A^anaA is a pronoun denoting the speaker alone, and is made to end invariably with fet-h to distinguish it from the particle A^ano which renders the aor. mansoob; the final A being for the purpose of showing what is the vowel in a case of pause; but when it occurs in the middle [or beginning] of a sentence, it is dropped, except in a bad dialect. (S.) [Accord. to ISd,] ↓ A^ana is a noun denoting the speaker; and in a case of pause, you add A at the end, [saying ↓ A^anaA ,] to denote quiescence; (M;) [or] it is better to do this, though it is not always done: (TA:) but it is said, on the authority of Ktr, that there are five dial. vars. of this word; namely, faEalotu ↓ A^ana , and ↓ A^anaA , and ↓ A=na , and A^anN , and ↓ A^anahN , all mentioned by IJ; but there is some weakness in this: IJ says that the h in ↓ A^anahN may be a substitute for the A in A^anaA , because the latter is the more usual, and the former is rare; or it may be added to show what is the vowel, like the h , and be like the h in kitaAbiyaho and HisaAbiyahN . (M.) For the dual, as well as the pl., only naHonu is used. sourceDefinition: ]: (Mughnee, K: *) and in the phrase, balaganiY A^ano qado kaAna ka*aA wka*aA [ It has come to my knowledge, or been related to me, or been told to me, or it came to my knowledge, &c., that ( the case is this:) such and such things have been ]; a phrase of this kind, in which A^ano occurs with a verb, not being approved without qado , unless you say, balaganiY A^an~ahu kaAna ka*aA waka*aA : (Lth, T:) [for] when the contracted A^ano has for its predicate a verbal proposition, of which the verb is neither imperfectly inflected, like layosa and EasaY , nor expressive of a prayer or an imprecation, it is separated from the verb, according to the more approved usage, by qado , or the prefix sa , or sawofa , or a negative, as laA &c., or lawo : (I 'Ak pp. 100 and 101:) but when its predicate is a nominal proposition, it requires not a separation; so that you say, Ealimotu A^ano ziayodN qaAy^imN [ I knew that ( the case was this: ) Zeyd was standing ]; (I 'Ak p. 100;) and balaganiY A^ano zaydN xaArijN [ It has come to my knowledge, or been related to me, or been told to me, &c., that ( the case is this:) Zeyd is going, or coming, out, or forth ]; (TA;) except in the case of a negation, as in the saying in the Kur [xi. 17], wA^ano laA A_ilha A_il~aA huwa [ And that ( the case is this:) there is no deity but He ]. (I 'Ak p. 100.) Thus used, it is originally triliteral, and is also what is termed maSodariy~ap ; [ Ealima A^ano , in the first of the exs. above, for instance, meaning Ealima A^an~ahu , i. e. Ealima A^an~a Al$~aA^ona , which is equivalent to Ealima kawona Al$~aA^oni ;] and governs the subject in the accus. case, and the predicate in the nom. case: and its subject must be a pronoun, suppressed, [as in the exs. given above, where it means Al$~aA^oni , and in a verse cited before, commencing A^ano taqoraA=ni , accord. to A'boo-'Alee,] or expressed; the latter, accord. to the more correct opinion, being allowable only by poetic license: and its predicate must be a proposition, unless the subject is expressed, in which case it may be either a single word or a proposition; both of which kinds occur in the following saying [of a poet]: biA^anoka rabiyEN wgayovN mariyEN waA^anoka hunaAka takuwna Alv~imaAlaA [he is speaking of persons coming as guests to him whom he addresses, when their provisions are exhausted, and the horizon is dust-coloured, and the north wind is blowing, (as is shown by the citation of the verse immediately preceding, in the T,) and he says, They know that thou art like rain that produces spring-herbage, and like plenteous rain, and that thou, there, art the aider and the manager of the affairs of people ]. (Mughnee. [In the T, for rabiyEN , I find Al~arbiyEu ; and for waA^anoka , I there find waqidomFA : but the reading in the Mughnee is that which is the more known.]) [J says,] A^ano is sometimes a contraction of A^an~a and does not govern [anything]: you say, balaganiY A^anN zayodN xaArijN [explained above]; and it is said in the Kur [vii. 41], wanuwduwA A^ano tilokumu Aljan~apu [ And it shall be proclaimed to them that ( the case is this:) that is Paradise ]: (S:) [here, however, A^anp is regarded by some as an explicative, as will be seen below:] but in saying this, J means that it does not govern as to the letter; for virtually it does govern; its subject being meant to be understood; the virtual meaning being A^an~ahu tilokumu Aljan~apu . (IB.) [In another place, J says,] You may make the contracted A^ano to govern or not, as you please. (S.) Aboo-Tálib the Grammarian mentions an assertion that the Arabs make it to govern; as in the saying [of a poet, describing a beautiful bosom], kaA^ano va*oyayohi Huq~aAni [ As though its two breasts were two small round boxes ]: but [the reading commonly known is kaA^ano vadoyaAhu Huq~aAni (this latter reading is given in De Sacy's Anthol. Gram. Ar. p. 104 of the Ar. text; and both are given in the S;) kaA^ano here meaning kaA^an~ahu ; and] Fr says, We have not heard the Arabs use the contracted form and make it to govern except with a pronoun, in which case the desinential syntax is not apparent. (T.) The author of the K says in the B that you say, Ealimotu A^ano zyodFA lamunoTaliqN [ I knew that Zeyd was indeed going away ], with l when it is made to govern; and Ealimotu A^ano zayodN munoTaliqN [ I knew that ( the case was this:) Zeyd was going away ], without l when it is made to have no government. (TA. [But in the latter ex. it governs the subject, which is understood, as in other exs. before given.]) [See an ex. in a verse ending with the phrase wakaA^ano qadi cited voce qad , where kaA^ano is for kaA^an~ahu , meaning kaA^an~a Al$~A^na , and a verb is understood after qd . And see also A^an~a , below.]― -b2- Thirdly, it is an explicative, (Mughnee, K,) meaning A^ayo (S, M, and so in some copies of the K,) or [rather] used in the manner of A^ayo ; (Mughnee, and so in some copies of the K;) [meaning qaAy^ilFA , or qaAy^iliyna ; or yaquwlu , or yaquwluwna ; or some other form of the verb qaAla ; i. e. Saying ; &c.;] as in the saying [in the Kur xxiii. 27], faA^awoHayonaA A_ilayohi A^ani ASonaEi Aloquloka [ And we revealed, or spake by revelation, unto him, saying, Make thou the ark ]; (Mughnee, K) and [in the Kur vii. 41,] wanuwduwA A^ano tilokumu Alojan~apu [ And it shall be proclaimed to them, being said, That is Paradise ]; or in these two instances it may be regarded as what is termed maSodariy~ap , by supposing the preposition [ bi ] understood before it, so that in the former instance it is the biliteral, because it is put before the imperative, and in the second it is the contraction of A^an~a because it is put before a nominal proposition; (Mughnee;) and [in the Kur xxxviii. 5,] waAnoTalaqa AlomalaA^u minohumo A^ani Amo$uwA (S, M, Mughnee) i. e. [ And the chief persons of them ] broke forth, or launched forth, with their tongues, or in speech, [saying,] Go ye on, or continue ye, in your course of action &c. (Mughnee.) For this usage of A^ano certain conditions are requisite : first, that it be preceded by a proposition : secondly, that it be followed by a proposition; so that you may not say, *akarotu EasojadFA A^ano *ahabFA , but you must say A^aYN in this case, or must omit the explicative : thirdly, that the preceding proposition convey the meaning of Alqawolu , as in the exs. above; in the last of which, AnTlq has the meaning assigned to it above; not that of walking or going away : fourthly, that there be not in the preceding proposition the letters of Alqawolu ; so that one may not say, qulotu lahu A^ani AfoEalo ; or, if there be in it those letters, that the word which they compose shall be interpreted by another word; as in the saying, in the Kur [v, 117], maA qulotu lahumo A_il~aA maA A^amarotaniY bihi A^ani AEobuduwA All~`ha which may mean, as Z says, I have not commanded them [aught save that which Thou commandedst me, saying, Worship ye God ]; (Mughnee;) in which instance Fr says that it is an explicative : (T :) fifthly, that there be not a preposition immediately before it; for if you say, katabotu A_ilayohi biA^ani AfoEalo ka*aA , it is what is termed maSodariy~ap [as we have before shown]. (Mughnee.) When it may be regarded as an explicative and is followed by an aor. with lA as in A^a$arotu A_ilayohi A^ano laA tafoEal ka*aA , it may be marfooa, [namely, the aor.,] on the supposition that lA is a negative ; or mejzoom, on the supposition that it is a prohibitive; and in both cases An is an explicative ; [so that the meaning is, I made a sign to him, as though saying, Thou wilt not do such a thing, in the former case ; or, in the latter, Do not thou such a thing ; ] or mansoob, on the supposition that lA is a negative and that An is what is termed maSodariy~ap : but if lA is wanting, it may not be mejzoom, but may be marfooa [if we use An as an explicative] or mansoob [if An be what is termed maSodariy~ap ]. (Mughnee.)― -b3- Fourthly, it is redundant, as a corroborative, (Mughnee, K,) like whatever else is redundant : and thus it is in four cases : one of these, which is the most common, being when it occurs after lam~aA denoting time; [and this is mentioned in the M ; ] as in the saying [in the Kur xxix. 32], walm~aA A^ano jaA='a to rusulunaA luwTFA [ And when our apostles came to Lot ]: (Mughnee:) [or,] accord. to J, (TA,) it is sometimes a connective to lam~aA ; as in the saying in the Kur [xii. 96], falam~aA A^ano jaA='a Aloba$iyru [ And when that (like as we say, " now that,") the announcer of good tidings came ] : and sometimes it is redundant ; as in the saying in the Kur [viii. 34], wamaA lahumo A^ano laA yuEa*ibahumu All~`hu [as though it might be rendered But what reason have they, God should not punish them? ] : (S, TA:) but IB says that the connective is redundant ; and [that An is not redundant in the latter instance, for] if it were redundant in this verse of the Kur it would not render the [aor.] verb mansoob. (TA. [The author of the Mughnee, like IB, disallows that An is redundant in a case of this kind, which Kh asserts it to be ; and says that fiY is under- stood before it.]) The second case is when it occurs between lawN and a verb signifying swearing, the latter being expressed; as in this verse: faA^uqosimu A^ano lawi A@lotaqayonaA waA^anotumu lakaAna lanaA yawomN mina Al$~ar~i muZolimu [ And I swear, had we and you met, there had been to us a dark day of evil ]: and when that verb is omitted; as in the following ex.: A^amaA waA@ll~`hi A^ano lawo kunota Hur~iA wamaA biA@loHuiriA^anota walaA AlEatiyqi [ Verily, or now surely, by God, if thou wert freeborn; but thou art not the freeborn nor the emancipated ]: so say Sb and others: Ibn-'Os- foor holds it to be a particle employed to connect the complement of the oath with the oath; but this is rendered improbable by the fact that it is in most cases omitted, and such particles are not. (Mughnee.) The third case, which is extr., is when it occurs between the k [of comparison] and the noun governed by it in the genitive case; as in the saying, wayawomFA tuwaAfiynaA biwajohK muqas~amK kaA^anN ZaboyapK taEoTuw A_ilaY waAriqi Als~alamo [ And on a day thou comest to us with a beautiful face, like a doe-gazelle raising her head towards the goodly green-leaved tree of the selem kind ], accord. to the reading of him who makes Tbypo to be governed in the genitive case [instead of the accus. or the nom.; for if we read it in the accus. or the nom., A^ano is a contraction of A^an~a ; in the former case, Zbyp being its subject, and its predicate being suppressed; and in the latter case, the meaning being kaA^an~ahaA ZaboyapN , so that the subject of An is suppressed]. (Mughnee.) The fourth case is when it occurs after A_i*aA ; as in the following ex.: faA^umohluhu Hat~aY A_*aA A^ano kaA^an~ahu muEaATiY yadK fiy luj~api AlmaA='i gaAmiru [ And I leave him alone until when he is as though he were a giver of a hand to be laid hold upon, in the fathomless deep of the water immerged ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b4- [Fifthly,] among other meanings which have been assigned to it, (Mughnee,) it has a conditional meaning, like A_inN : (Mughnee, K:) so the Koofees hold; and it seems to be most probably correct, for several reasons: first, because both these forms occur, accord. to different readings, in several instances, in one passage of the Kur; as in [ii. 282,] A^ano taDil~N A_iHodaAhumaA [ If one of them twain (namely, women,) err ]; &c.: secondly, because [the prefix] fa often occurs after it; as in a verse commencing with A^abaA xuraA$apa [as cited voce A^am~aA , accord. to some who hold that A^m~aA in that verse is a compound of the conditional A^ano and the redundant maA ; and as in the Kur ii. 282, where the words quoted above are immediately followed by fatu*ak~ira A_iHodaAhumaA A@loA^uxoraY ]: thirdly, because it is conjoined with A_inN [which forms a part of the compound A_ik~aA ] in this ex.: A_im~aA A^aqamota waA^am~aA A^anota murotaHilFA faA@ll~`hu yakolaA^u maA taA^otiY wamaA ta*aru [ If thou remain, and if thou be going away ( A^am~aA meaning A^ano kunota , as syn. with A_ino kunota ), may God guard thee ( yakolaA^u being marfooa because of the f ) as long as thou doest and as long as thou leavest undone ]: thus related, with kesr to the former An [in A_in~aA ] and with fet-h to the latter [in A^am~aA ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b5- [Sixthly,] it is a negative, like A_ino : (Mughnee, K:) so, as some say, in [the Kur iii. 66,] A^anE yuw^otaY A^aHadN mivola maA A^uwtiytumo [meaning accord. to them Not any one is given the like of that scripture which ye have been given ]: but it is said [by others] that the meaning is, [taken with what precedes it,] And believe not ye that ( biA^ano ) any one is given the like of that scripture which ye have been given, except it be given to him who followeth your religion; and that the phrase “ say thou, Verily the direction is the direction of God, ” is parenthetic. (Mughnee.) ― -b6- [Seventhly,] it is syn. with A_i*o , (AZ, T, Mughnee, K, [in Freytag's Lex., from the K, A_i*o qiyla , but qyl in the K relates to what there follows,]) as some say, in [the Kur l. 2,] balo EajibuwA A^anN jaA='ahumo muno*irNminohumo [ Verily they wonder because a warner from among themselves hath come unto them ]; (Mughnee, K;) and in other instances; but correctly, in all these instances, An is what is termed maSodariy~ap , and li denoting cause is understood before it. (Mughnee.) [See also A^am~aA and A_im~aA .] ― -b7- [Eighthly,] it is syn. with liy^al~A , accord. to some, in [the Kur iv. last verse,] yubay~inu A@ll~`huA^ano taDil~uwA [ God explaineth to you (the ordinances of your religion, Jel), lest ye should err, or in order that ye may not err ]; (Mughnee, K;) and in the saying, nazalotumo manozila AlA^aDoyaAfi min~aA faEaj~alonaA AlqiraY A^ano ta$otimuwnaA [ Ye became, or have become, in the condition of our guests; so we hastened, or have hastened, the entertainment, lest ye should revile us, or in order that ye should not revile us ]: (Mughnee:) but correctly, in such a case [likewise], An is what is termed maSodariy~ap , and the original wording is karaAhapa A^ano taDil~uwA [ from a motive of dislike that ye should err ], (Mughnee, K,) and maxaAfapa A^ano ta$otimuwnaA [ from a motive of fear that ye should revile us ]: so say the Basrees: some say, extravagantly, that l is meant to be understood before it, and Al~a*iY after it. (Mughnee.) ― -b8- [Ninthly,] it occurs in the sense of Al~a*iY ; as in the saying, zayodN A^aEoqalu minN A^ano yako*ib [ Zeyd is more reasonable than he who lies; which is equivalent to saying, Zeyd is too reasonable to lie: but respecting its usage in a phrase of this kind, and respecting the form of the aor. after it in such a case, see mino ]. (Kull p. 78.) ― -b9- By a peculiarity of pronunciation termed EanoEatapN , the tribe of Temeem say Eano instead of A^anN . (M.)

(Mughnee.) (Mughnee.) ― -b4- [Fifthly,] among other meanings which have been assigned to it, (Mughnee,) it has a conditional meaning, like A_inN : (Mughnee, K:) so the Koofees hold; and it seems to be most probably correct, for several reasons: first, because both these forms occur, accord. to different readings, in several instances, in one passage of the Kur; as in [ii. 282,] A^ano taDil~N A_iHodaAhumaA [ If one of them twain (namely, women,) err ]; &c.: secondly, because [the prefix] fa often occurs after it; as in a verse commencing with A^abaA xuraA$apa [as cited voce A^am~aA , accord. to some who hold that A^m~aA in that verse is a compound of the conditional A^ano and the redundant maA ; and as in the Kur ii. 282, where the words quoted above are immediately followed by fatu*ak~ira A_iHodaAhumaA A@loA^uxoraY ]: thirdly, because it is conjoined with A_inN [which forms a part of the compound A_ik~aA ] in this ex.: A_im~aA A^aqamota waA^am~aA A^anota murotaHilFA faA@ll~`hu yakolaA^u maA taA^otiY wamaA ta*aru [ If thou remain, and if thou be going away ( A^am~aA meaning A^ano kunota , as syn. with A_ino kunota ), may God guard thee ( yakolaA^u being marfooa because of the f ) as long as thou doest and as long as thou leavest undone ]: thus related, with kesr to the former An [in A_in~aA ] and with fet-h to the latter [in A^am~aA ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b5- [Sixthly,] it is a negative, like A_ino : (Mughnee, K:) so, as some say, in [the Kur iii. 66,] A^anE yuw^otaY A^aHadN mivola maA A^uwtiytumo [meaning accord. to them Not any one is given the like of that scripture which ye have been given ]: but it is said [by others] that the meaning is, [taken with what precedes it,] And believe not ye that ( biA^ano ) any one is given the like of that scripture which ye have been given, except it be given to him who followeth your religion; and that the phrase “ say thou, Verily the direction is the direction of God, ” is parenthetic. (Mughnee.) ― -b6- [Seventhly,] it is syn. with A_i*o , (AZ, T, Mughnee, K, [in Freytag's Lex., from the K, A_i*o qiyla , but qyl in the K relates to what there follows,]) as some say, in [the Kur l. 2,] balo EajibuwA A^anN jaA='ahumo muno*irNminohumo [ Verily they wonder because a warner from among themselves hath come unto them ]; (Mughnee, K;) and in other instances; but correctly, in all these instances, An is what is termed maSodariy~ap , and li denoting cause is understood before it. (Mughnee.) [See also A^am~aA and A_im~aA .] ― -b7- [Eighthly,] it is syn. with liy^al~A , accord. to some, in [the Kur iv. last verse,] yubay~inu A@ll~`huA^ano taDil~uwA [ God explaineth to you (the ordinances of your religion, Jel), lest ye should err, or in order that ye may not err ]; (Mughnee, K;) and in the saying, nazalotumo manozila AlA^aDoyaAfi min~aA faEaj~alonaA AlqiraY A^ano ta$otimuwnaA [ Ye became, or have become, in the condition of our guests; so we hastened, or have hastened, the entertainment, lest ye should revile us, or in order that ye should not revile us ]: (Mughnee:) but correctly, in such a case [likewise], An is what is termed maSodariy~ap , and the original wording is karaAhapa A^ano taDil~uwA [ from a motive of dislike that ye should err ], (Mughnee, K,) and maxaAfapa A^ano ta$otimuwnaA [ from a motive of fear that ye should revile us ]: so say the Basrees: some say, extravagantly, that l is meant to be understood before it, and Al~a*iY after it. (Mughnee.) ― -b8- [Ninthly,] it occurs in the sense of Al~a*iY ; as in the saying, zayodN A^aEoqalu minN A^ano yako*ib [ Zeyd is more reasonable than he who lies; which is equivalent to saying, Zeyd is too reasonable to lie: but respecting its usage in a phrase of this kind, and respecting the form of the aor. after it in such a case, see mino ]. (Kull p. 78.) ― -b9- By a peculiarity of pronunciation termed EanoEatapN , the tribe of Temeem say Eano instead of A^anN . (M.)

sourceDefinition: is used in various ways: first, as a conditional particle, (S, M, Msb, Mughnee, K,) denoting the happening of the second of two events in consequence of the happening of the first, (S, Msb, *) whether the second be immediate or deferred, and whether the condition be affirmative or negative; (Msb;) [and as such it is followed by a mejzoom aor., or by a pret. having the signification of an aor.;] as in the saying, [ A_ino tafoEalN A^foEalN If thou do such a thing, I will do it; and] A_ino taA^otiniY A=tika [ If thou come to me, I will come to thee ]; and A_inN jiy^otaniY A^akoramotuka [ If thou come to me, I will treat thee with honour ]; (S;) and A_ino faEalota faEalotu [ If thou do, I will do ] for which the tribe of Teiyi say, as IJ relates on the authority of Ktr, hino faEalota faEalotu ; (M;) and A_ino daxalot Ald~aAra A^awN [ If thou stand, I will stand ]; and A_ino daxaloti Ald~aAra A^awo lamo tadoxuliY Ald~aArD faA^anoti TaAlqN [ If thou enter the house, or if thou enter not the house, thou shalt be divorced ]; (Msb;) and [in the Kur viii. 39,] A_ino yanotahuwA yugofarN lahumo maA qad salafa [ If they desist, what hath already past shall be forgiven them ]; and [in verse 19 of the same ch.,] waA_ino taEuwduwA naEudo [ But if ye return to attacking the Apostle, we will return to assisting him]. (Mughnee, K.) [On the difference between it and A_i*A , see the latter.] When either it or A_i*aA is immediately followed by a noun in the nom. case, the said noun is governed in that case by a verb necessarily suppressed, of which it is the agent; as in the saying, in the Kur [ix. 6], waA_ino A^aHadN mina A@lomu$orikiyna A@stajaAraka ; the complete phrase being waA_ini AsotajaAraka A^aHadN mina A@lomu$orikiyna A@sotajaAraka [ And if any one of the believers in a plurality of gods demand protection of thee, (if) he demand protection of thee ]: so accord. to the generality of the grammarians. (I 'Ak p. 123.) Sometimes it is conjoined with the negative laA , and the ignorant may imagine it to be the exceptive A_il~aA ; as in [the saying in the Kur ix. 40,] A_il~aA tanoSuruwhu faqad naSarahu A@ll~`hu [ If ye will not aid him, certainly God did aid him ]; and [in the next preceding verse,] A_il~aA tanofiruwA yuEa*~ibokumo [ If ye will not go forth to war, He will punish you ]. (Mughnee, K. *) It is sometimes used to denote one's feigning himself ignorant; as when you say to one who asks, “ Is thy child in the house? ” and thou hast knowledge thereof, A_ino kaAna fiY Ald~aAri A^aEolamotuka bihi [ If he be in the house, I will inform thee thereof ]. (Msb.) And to denote one's putting the knowing in the predicament of the ignorant, in order to incite to the doing or continuing an action; as when you say, A_inN kunota A@buniY faA^aTiEoniY [ If thou be my son, obey me ]; as though you said, “ Thou knowest that thou art my son, and it is incumbent on the son to obey the father, and thou art not obedient; therefore do what thou art commanded to do. ” (Msb.) And sometimes it is divested of the conditional meaning, and becomes syn. with law ; as in the saying, Sal~i waA_inN Eajazota Eani AlqiyaAm [ Pray thou though thou be unable to stand; ] i. e. pray thou whether thou be able to stand or unable to do so; and in the saying, A^akorimN ziyodFA waA_ino qaEada i. e. [ Treat thou Zeyd with honour ] though he be sitting; or, whether he sit or not. (Msb.) [ A_im~aA as a compound of the conditional A_inN and the redundant maA , see in an art. of which AmA is the heading.] ― -b2- [Secondly,] it is a negative, (S, Mughnee, K,) syn. with maA ; (S;) and is put before a nominal proposition; (Mughnee, K;) as in the saying [in the Kur lxvii. 20], A_ini A@lokaAfiruwna A_il~aA fiY guruwrK [ The unbelievers are not in aught save in a deception ]; (S, Mughnee, K;) and before a verbal proposition; as in [the Kur ix. 108,] A_ino A^aradonaA A_il~aA A@loHusonaY [ We desired not, or meant not, aught save that which is best ]. (Mughnee, K.) The assertion of some, that the negative A_inN does not occur except where it is followed by A_il~aA , as in the instances cited above, or by lam~aA , with tesh-deed, which is syn. therewith, as, accord. to a reading of some of the Seven [Readers], in the saying [in the Kur lxxxvi. 4], A_ino kul~u nafosK lam~aA EalayohaA HaAfiZN , i. e., maA kul~u nafosK A_il~aA EalayohaA HaAfiZN [ There is not any soul but over it is a guardian ], is refuted by the sayings in the Kur [x. 69 and lxxii. 26], A_ino Eindakumo mino suloTaAnK bih`*aA [meaning, accord. to the Jel., Ye have no proof of this that ye say], and A_ino A^adoriyA^aqariybN maA tuwEaduwna [ I know not whether that with which ye are threatened be nigh ]. (Mughnee, K. *) The conditional and the negative both occur in the saying in the Kur [xxxv. 39], walay^ino zaAlataA A_ino A^amosakahumaA mino A^aHadK mino baEodihi [ And I swear that, if they should quit their place, not any one should withhold them after Him ]: the former is conditional; and the latter is negative, and is [part of] the complement of the oath which is denoted by the l prefixed to the former; the complement of the condition being necessarily suppressed. (Mughnee.) When it is put before a nominal proposition, it has no government, accord. to Sb and Fr; but Ks and Mbr allow its governing in the manner of layosa ; and Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr reads, [in the Kur vii. 193,] A_ini A@l~a*iyna tadoEuwna mino duwni A@ll~`hi EibaAdFA A^amovaAlakumN [ Those whom ye invoke beside God, or others than God, are not men like you ]: also, the people of El-'Áliyeh have been heard to say, A_inN A^aHadN xayorFAmino A^aHdK A_il~aA biAlEaAfiyapi [ Any one is not better than any other one, except by means of health, or soundness ]; and A_ino *`lika naAfiEaka walaA DaAr~aka [ That is not profitable to thee nor injurious to thee ]: as an ex. of its occurrence without government, which is mostly the case, the saying of some, qaAy^mN ↓ A_in~a may be explained as originally A_inN A^anaA qaAy^imN [ I am not standing ]; the A^ of A^anaA being elided for no reason in itself, and the n of A_inN being incorporated into the n of A^anaA , and the A of this latter being elided in its conjunction with the following word; but A_in~a qaAy^imFA has also been heard. (Mughnee.) Sometimes it occurs [as a negative] in the complement of an oath: you say, waA@ll~`hi A_inN faEalotu , meaning maA faEalotu [ By God, I did not ]. (S.) ― -b3- [Thirdly,] it is a contraction of A_in~a , and is put before a nominal and before a verbal proposition. (Mughnee, K.) In the former case, it is made to govern and is made to have no government: (S, * K:) [i. e.] in this case, it is allowable to make it govern; contr. to the opinion of the Koofees: (Mughnee:) Lth says that he who uses the contracted form of A_in~a uses the nom. case with it, except that some of the people of El-Hijáz use the accus. case with it: (T:) thus it is said, accord. to one reading, [in the Kur xi. 113,] A_ino kul~aA lamaA layuwaf~iyan~ahumN rab~uka A^aEomaAlahumN [ Verily all of them, thy Lord will indeed fully render them the recompense of their works ]: (T, Mughnee:) Fr says, We have not heard the Arabs use the contracted form and make it to govern, unless with a pronoun, in which case the desinential syntax is not apparent; and he adds that in the instance cited above, they make kul~A to be governed in the accus. case by lywf~yn~hm ; as though the phrase were layuwaf~iyan~ahumo kul~aA ; and that kul~u would be proper; for you say, A_ino zayodN laqaAy^imN [ Verily Zeyd is standing ]: (T:) the ex. given by Sb is, A_ino EamorFA lamunTaliqN [ Verily 'Amr is going away ]. (Mughnee.) But it is [most] frequently made to have no government; as in the saying [in the Kur xliii. 34 accord. to one reading], waA_ino kul~u *`lika lamaA mataAEu A@loHayaApi A@ld~unoyaA [ And verily all that is the furniture of the present life ]; and, accord. to the reading of Hafs, [and of 'Ásim and Kh, in the Kur xx. 66, respecting which see A_in~a ,] A_ino h`*aAni lasaAHiraAni [ Verily these two are enchanters ]; &c. (Mughnee.) When it is put before a verbal proposition, it is necessarily made to have no government: (Mughnee, K:) and in most cases the verb is a preterite and of the kind called naAsix [which effects a change of the grammatical form or of the meaning in a nominal proposition before which it is placed]; as in the saying [in the Kur ii. 138], waA_ino kaAnatN lakabiyrapF [ And verily it was a great matter ]; and [in the Kur xvii. 75,] waA_ino kaAduwA layafotinuwnaka [ And verily they were near to seducing thee ]; (Mughnee;) in which last ex. AZ says, it means laqado , i. e. without doubt; and so in the same ch. vv. 78 and 108: (T:) less frequently it is an aor. of a verb of this kind; as in the saying [in the Kur xxvi. 186], waA_ino naZun~uka lamina A@lokaA*ibyna [ And verily we think thee to be of the number of the liars ]: and both these kinds of expression may be taken as exs. to be imitated: less frequently than this it is a preterite of a verb not of the kind termed nasx ; as in the saying [of a poet], $al~atN yamiynuka A_inN qatalota lamusolimFA [ May thy right arm, or hand, dry up, or become unsound! verily thou hast slain a Muslim ]; but this may not be taken as an ex. to be imitated; contr. to the opinion of Akh; for he allows the phrase, A_ino qiAma laA^anaA [ Verily I stood ], and A_inN qaEada lA^anota [ Verily thou sattest ]: and less frequently than this it is an aor. of a verb not of the kind termed nAsx ; as in the saying, A_ino yaziynuka lanafosuka waA_inN ya$iynuka lahiyahN [ Verily thy soul is that which beautifies thee, and it is that which deforms thee ]; and this, by common consent, may not be taken as an ex. to be imitated. (Mughnee.) Wherever you find A_inN with la after it, decide that it is originally A_in~a ; (Mughnee, K;) as in the exs. above: but respecting this l there is a difference of opinion: see this letter. (Mughnee.) J says, (TA,) A_inN is sometimes a contraction of A_in~a , and this must have l put before its predicate, to compensate for what is elided, of the doubled letter; as in the saying in the Kur [lxxxvi. 4, accord. to him who reads lamaA instead of lam~aA ], A_ino kul~u nafosK lamaA EalayohaA HaAfiZN [ Verily every soul hath over it a guardian ]; and in the saying, A_inN zaydN laA^axuwka [ Verily Zeyd is thy brother ]; in order that it may not be confounded with A_inN which is syn. with the negative maA : (S, TA:) but IB says, l is here introduced to distinguish between negation and affirmation, and this A_ino has neither subject nor predicate; so J's saying that the l is put before its predicate is without meaning: and this l is sometimes introduced with the objective complement of a verb; as in A_ino Darabotu lazayodFA [ Verily I struck, or beat, Zeyd ]; and with the agent; as in A_ino qaAma lazayodN [ Verily Zeyd stood ]. (TA.) When the contracted A_ino governs, this l is not necessary; so you may say, A_ino zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Verily Zeyd is standing ]; because in this case it cannot be confounded with the negative; for the negative does not render the subject mansoob and the predicate marfooa: and when it does not govern, if the meaning is apparent, the l is not needed; as in wanaHonu A^ubaApu AlD~ayomi mino A=li maAlikK waA_ino maAlikN kaAnato kiraAma AlmaEaAdini [ And we are persons who refuse to submit to injury, of the family of Málik: and verily the family of Málik are generous in respect of their origins ]; kaAnato being here for lakaAnatN . (I 'Ak p. 99.) ― -b4- [Fourthly,] it is redundant, (S, Mughnee, K,) occurring with maA ; as in the saying, maA A_ino yaquwmu zayodN [ Zeyd does not stand ]; (S;) and in the saying [of a poet], kaA A_ino A^atayota bi$oY'K A^anota takorahuhu [ Thou didst not a thing which thou dislikest ]. (Mughnee, K: in the CK Aatotu .) It is mostly thus used after the negative mA , when put before a verbal proposition; as above; or before a nominal proposition; as in the saying, manaAyaAnaA wadawolapu A=xariynaA wamaA A_ino Tib~unaA jbunN wl`kinN [ And our habit is not cowardice; but our destinies and the good fortune of others caused our being defeated]: and in this case it prevents the government of mA , as in this verse: but in the saying, baniY gudaAnapa maA A_ino A^anotumu *ahabFA walaA SariyfFA wal`kinN A^anotumu Alxazafu [ Sons of Ghudáneh, ye are not indeed gold, nor silver, or pure silver, but ye are pottery ], accord. to him who relates it thus, saying *hbFA and SryfFA , in the accus. case, it is explained as a negative, corroborative of mA : (Mughnee:) and accord. to J, (TA,) the negatives maA and A_inN are sometimes thus combined for corroboration; as in the saying of the rájiz, (El-Aghlab El-'Ijlee, TA,) A^akovara minohu qirapF waqaAraA maA A_inN raA^ayonaA malik~aA A^agaAraA [ We have not indeed seen a king who has made a hostile incursion possessing more numerous sheep, or goats, and camels, than he ]; (S, TA;) but IB says that An is here redundant, not a negative. (TA.) Sometimes it is redundant after the conjunct noun maA ; as in the saying, yurajiY~ AlmaroA_u maA A_inN laA yaraAhu wataEoriDu duwna A^adonaAhu AlxuTuwbu [ Man hopes for that which he will not see; for calamities intervene as obstacles in the way to what is nearest thereof ]. (Mughnee.) And after the maA termed maSodariy~ap , (Mughnee,) [i. e.,] after the adverbial maA [which is of the kind termed mSdry~p ]; (TA;) as in the saying (of Maaloot El-Kurey'ee, cited by Sb, TA), waraj~i AlfataY liloxayori maA A_ino raA^ayotahu Ealay Als~in~i xayorFA laAyazaAlu yaziydu [ And hope thou that the youth is destined for good as long as thou hast seen him not ceasing to increase in good with age ]. (Mughnee.) And after the inceptive A^alaA ; as in the saying, A^alaA A_ino saraY layoliY fbit~u kay^iybaA A^uHaA*iru A^ano tanoA^aY Aln~awaY bigaDuwbaA [ Now he journeyed on, or during, that my night, and I passed the night in an evil state, broken in spirit by grief, being fearful that the distance to which he was going with Ghadoob (a woman so named) would become far ]. (Mughnee.) And before the meddeh denoting disapproval: [for] Sb heard a man, on its being said to him, “ Wilt thou go forth if the desert become plentiful in herbage? ” reply, A^aA^anaA A_iniyhN [ What, I, indeed? ] disapproving that he should think otherwise than that. (Mughnee. [See also art. AnY .]) ― -b5- [Fifthly,] it is syn. with qado : so it is said to be in the saying [in the Kur lxxxvii. 9], A_ino nafaEati A@l*~ikoraY [ Admonition hath profited ], (T, Mughnee, K,) by IAar (T) and by Ktr: (Mughnee:) and Abu-l-' Abbás relates that the Arabs say, A_inN nafaEati A@l*~ikoraY meaning qadoqaAma zayodN [ Zeyd has stood ]; and he adds, that Ks states his having heard them say so, and having thought that it expressed a condition, but that he asked them, and they answered that they meant qadoqaAma zayodN , and not maA qaAma zayodN . (T.) [So too, accord. to the K, in all the exs. cited in the next sentence as from the Mughnee; but this is evidently a mistake, occasioned by an accidental omission.] ― -b6- [Sixthly,] it is asserted also by the Koofees, that it is syn. with A_i*o , in the following exs.: in the Kur [v. 62], waA@t~aquwA A@ll~`ha A_inN kunotumo muw^ominiyna [ And fear ye God, because ye are believers: and so, accord. to AZ, as is said in the T, in a similar instance in the Kur ii. 278: and in the same, iv. 62]: and [in the Kur xlviii. 27,] latado xulun~a A@lmasojida A@loHaraAma A_ino $aA='a A=miniyna [ Ye shall assuredly enter the sacred mosque, because God hath willed, in security ]: and in like instances, when the verb therein expresses what is held sure to happen or to have happened: and in the saying, A^atagoDabu A_inN A^udonaA qutayobapa Huz~ataA jihaArFA walamo tagoDabo liqatoli A@boni HaAzimi [ Art thou angry because the ears of Kuteybeh have been cut, openly, or publicly, and wast not angry for the slaughter of Ibn-Házim? ]: (Mughnee:) but in all these instances [it is sufficiently obvious that] An may be otherwise explained. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b7- [Seventhly,] it is sometimes syn. with A_i*aA ; as in the Kur [ix. 23], laA tat~axi*uwA A=baA='akumo waA_ixowaAnakumo A^awoliyaA='a A_ini A@sotaHab~uwA A@lokuforaEalaY A@loA_iymaAni [ Take not ye your fathers and your brethren as friends when they love unbelief above belief ]; and in the same [xxxiii. 49], waA@moraA^apF muw^ominapF A_ino wahabato nafosahaA liln~abiY~ [ And a believing woman when she giveth herself to the Prophet ]: so says AZ. (T.) ― -b8- [Eighthly,] it is used for A_im~aA , (Mughnee and K, voce A_im~aA ,) distinct from A_im~aA which is a compound of the conditional A_inN and the redundant maA . (Mughnee ibid.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce A_im~aA in the present work, commencing with the words saqatohu Alr~awaAEidu .]

rawSourceText: is used in various ways: first, as a conditional particle, (S, M, Msb, Mughnee, K,) denoting the happening of the second of two events in consequence of the happening of the first, (S, Msb, *) whether the second be immediate or deferred, and whether the condition be affirmative or negative; (Msb;) [and as such it is followed by a mejzoom aor., or by a pret. having the signification of an aor.;] as in the saying, [ A_ino tafoEalN A^foEalN If thou do such a thing, I will do it; and] A_ino taA^otiniY A=tika [ If thou come to me, I will come to thee ]; and A_inN jiy^otaniY A^akoramotuka [ If thou come to me, I will treat thee with honour ]; (S;) and A_ino faEalota faEalotu [ If thou do, I will do ] for which the tribe of Teiyi say, as IJ relates on the authority of Ktr, hino faEalota faEalotu ; (M;) and A_ino daxalot Ald~aAra A^awN [ If thou stand, I will stand ]; and A_ino daxaloti Ald~aAra A^awo lamo tadoxuliY Ald~aArD faA^anoti TaAlqN [ If thou enter the house, or if thou enter not the house, thou shalt be divorced ]; (Msb;) and [in the Kur viii. 39,] A_ino yanotahuwA yugofarN lahumo maA qad salafa [ If they desist, what hath already past shall be forgiven them ]; and [in verse 19 of the same ch.,] waA_ino taEuwduwA naEudo [ But if ye return to attacking the Apostle, we will return to assisting him]. (Mughnee, K.) [On the difference between it and A_i*A , see the latter.] When either it or A_i*aA is immediately followed by a noun in the nom. case, the said noun is governed in that case by a verb necessarily suppressed, of which it is the agent; as in the saying, in the Kur [ix. 6], waA_ino A^aHadN mina A@lomu$orikiyna A@stajaAraka ; the complete phrase being waA_ini AsotajaAraka A^aHadN mina A@lomu$orikiyna A@sotajaAraka [ And if any one of the believers in a plurality of gods demand protection of thee, (if) he demand protection of thee ]: so accord. to the generality of the grammarians. (I 'Ak p. 123.) Sometimes it is conjoined with the negative laA , and the ignorant may imagine it to be the exceptive A_il~aA ; as in [the saying in the Kur ix. 40,] A_il~aA tanoSuruwhu faqad naSarahu A@ll~`hu [ If ye will not aid him, certainly God did aid him ]; and [in the next preceding verse,] A_il~aA tanofiruwA yuEa*~ibokumo [ If ye will not go forth to war, He will punish you ]. (Mughnee, K. *) It is sometimes used to denote one's feigning himself ignorant; as when you say to one who asks, “ Is thy child in the house? ” and thou hast knowledge thereof, A_ino kaAna fiY Ald~aAri A^aEolamotuka bihi [ If he be in the house, I will inform thee thereof ]. (Msb.) And to denote one's putting the knowing in the predicament of the ignorant, in order to incite to the doing or continuing an action; as when you say, A_inN kunota A@buniY faA^aTiEoniY [ If thou be my son, obey me ]; as though you said, “ Thou knowest that thou art my son, and it is incumbent on the son to obey the father, and thou art not obedient; therefore do what thou art commanded to do. ” (Msb.) And sometimes it is divested of the conditional meaning, and becomes syn. with law ; as in the saying, Sal~i waA_inN Eajazota Eani AlqiyaAm [ Pray thou though thou be unable to stand; ] i. e. pray thou whether thou be able to stand or unable to do so; and in the saying, A^akorimN ziyodFA waA_ino qaEada i. e. [ Treat thou Zeyd with honour ] though he be sitting; or, whether he sit or not. (Msb.) [ A_im~aA as a compound of the conditional A_inN and the redundant maA , see in an art. of which AmA is the heading.] ― -b2- [Secondly,] it is a negative, (S, Mughnee, K,) syn. with maA ; (S;) and is put before a nominal proposition; (Mughnee, K;) as in the saying [in the Kur lxvii. 20], A_ini A@lokaAfiruwna A_il~aA fiY guruwrK [ The unbelievers are not in aught save in a deception ]; (S, Mughnee, K;) and before a verbal proposition; as in [the Kur ix. 108,] A_ino A^aradonaA A_il~aA A@loHusonaY [ We desired not, or meant not, aught save that which is best ]. (Mughnee, K.) The assertion of some, that the negative A_inN does not occur except where it is followed by A_il~aA , as in the instances cited above, or by lam~aA , with tesh-deed, which is syn. therewith, as, accord. to a reading of some of the Seven [Readers], in the saying [in the Kur lxxxvi. 4], A_ino kul~u nafosK lam~aA EalayohaA HaAfiZN , i. e., maA kul~u nafosK A_il~aA EalayohaA HaAfiZN [ There is not any soul but over it is a guardian ], is refuted by the sayings in the Kur [x. 69 and lxxii. 26], A_ino Eindakumo mino suloTaAnK bih`*aA [meaning, accord. to the Jel., Ye have no proof of this that ye say], and A_ino A^adoriyA^aqariybN maA tuwEaduwna [ I know not whether that with which ye are threatened be nigh ]. (Mughnee, K. *) The conditional and the negative both occur in the saying in the Kur [xxxv. 39], walay^ino zaAlataA A_ino A^amosakahumaA mino A^aHadK mino baEodihi [ And I swear that, if they should quit their place, not any one should withhold them after Him ]: the former is conditional; and the latter is negative, and is [part of] the complement of the oath which is denoted by the l prefixed to the former; the complement of the condition being necessarily suppressed. (Mughnee.) When it is put before a nominal proposition, it has no government, accord. to Sb and Fr; but Ks and Mbr allow its governing in the manner of layosa ; and Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr reads, [in the Kur vii. 193,] A_ini A@l~a*iyna tadoEuwna mino duwni A@ll~`hi EibaAdFA A^amovaAlakumN [ Those whom ye invoke beside God, or others than God, are not men like you ]: also, the people of El-'Áliyeh have been heard to say, A_inN A^aHadN xayorFAmino A^aHdK A_il~aA biAlEaAfiyapi [ Any one is not better than any other one, except by means of health, or soundness ]; and A_ino *`lika naAfiEaka walaA DaAr~aka [ That is not profitable to thee nor injurious to thee ]: as an ex. of its occurrence without government, which is mostly the case, the saying of some, qaAy^mN ↓ A_in~a may be explained as originally A_inN A^anaA qaAy^imN [ I am not standing ]; the A^ of A^anaA being elided for no reason in itself, and the n of A_inN being incorporated into the n of A^anaA , and the A of this latter being elided in its conjunction with the following word; but A_in~a qaAy^imFA has also been heard. (Mughnee.) Sometimes it occurs [as a negative] in the complement of an oath: you say, waA@ll~`hi A_inN faEalotu , meaning maA faEalotu [ By God, I did not ]. (S.) ― -b3- [Thirdly,] it is a contraction of A_in~a , and is put before a nominal and before a verbal proposition. (Mughnee, K.) In the former case, it is made to govern and is made to have no government: (S, * K:) [i. e.] in this case, it is allowable to make it govern; contr. to the opinion of the Koofees: (Mughnee:) Lth says that he who uses the contracted form of A_in~a uses the nom. case with it, except that some of the people of El-Hijáz use the accus. case with it: (T:) thus it is said, accord. to one reading, [in the Kur xi. 113,] A_ino kul~aA lamaA layuwaf~iyan~ahumN rab~uka A^aEomaAlahumN [ Verily all of them, thy Lord will indeed fully render them the recompense of their works ]: (T, Mughnee:) Fr says, We have not heard the Arabs use the contracted form and make it to govern, unless with a pronoun, in which case the desinential syntax is not apparent; and he adds that in the instance cited above, they make kul~A to be governed in the accus. case by lywf~yn~hm ; as though the phrase were layuwaf~iyan~ahumo kul~aA ; and that kul~u would be proper; for you say, A_ino zayodN laqaAy^imN [ Verily Zeyd is standing ]: (T:) the ex. given by Sb is, A_ino EamorFA lamunTaliqN [ Verily 'Amr is going away ]. (Mughnee.) But it is [most] frequently made to have no government; as in the saying [in the Kur xliii. 34 accord. to one reading], waA_ino kul~u *`lika lamaA mataAEu A@loHayaApi A@ld~unoyaA [ And verily all that is the furniture of the present life ]; and, accord. to the reading of Hafs, [and of 'Ásim and Kh, in the Kur xx. 66, respecting which see A_in~a ,] A_ino h`*aAni lasaAHiraAni [ Verily these two are enchanters ]; &c. (Mughnee.) When it is put before a verbal proposition, it is necessarily made to have no government: (Mughnee, K:) and in most cases the verb is a preterite and of the kind called naAsix [which effects a change of the grammatical form or of the meaning in a nominal proposition before which it is placed]; as in the saying [in the Kur ii. 138], waA_ino kaAnatN lakabiyrapF [ And verily it was a great matter ]; and [in the Kur xvii. 75,] waA_ino kaAduwA layafotinuwnaka [ And verily they were near to seducing thee ]; (Mughnee;) in which last ex. AZ says, it means laqado , i. e. without doubt; and so in the same ch. vv. 78 and 108: (T:) less frequently it is an aor. of a verb of this kind; as in the saying [in the Kur xxvi. 186], waA_ino naZun~uka lamina A@lokaA*ibyna [ And verily we think thee to be of the number of the liars ]: and both these kinds of expression may be taken as exs. to be imitated: less frequently than this it is a preterite of a verb not of the kind termed nasx ; as in the saying [of a poet], $al~atN yamiynuka A_inN qatalota lamusolimFA [ May thy right arm, or hand, dry up, or become unsound! verily thou hast slain a Muslim ]; but this may not be taken as an ex. to be imitated; contr. to the opinion of Akh; for he allows the phrase, A_ino qiAma laA^anaA [ Verily I stood ], and A_inN qaEada lA^anota [ Verily thou sattest ]: and less frequently than this it is an aor. of a verb not of the kind termed nAsx ; as in the saying, A_ino yaziynuka lanafosuka waA_inN ya$iynuka lahiyahN [ Verily thy soul is that which beautifies thee, and it is that which deforms thee ]; and this, by common consent, may not be taken as an ex. to be imitated. (Mughnee.) Wherever you find A_inN with la after it, decide that it is originally A_in~a ; (Mughnee, K;) as in the exs. above: but respecting this l there is a difference of opinion: see this letter. (Mughnee.) J says, (TA,) A_inN is sometimes a contraction of A_in~a , and this must have l put before its predicate, to compensate for what is elided, of the doubled letter; as in the saying in the Kur [lxxxvi. 4, accord. to him who reads lamaA instead of lam~aA ], A_ino kul~u nafosK lamaA EalayohaA HaAfiZN [ Verily every soul hath over it a guardian ]; and in the saying, A_inN zaydN laA^axuwka [ Verily Zeyd is thy brother ]; in order that it may not be confounded with A_inN which is syn. with the negative maA : (S, TA:) but IB says, l is here introduced to distinguish between negation and affirmation, and this A_ino has neither subject nor predicate; so J's saying that the l is put before its predicate is without meaning: and this l is sometimes introduced with the objective complement of a verb; as in A_ino Darabotu lazayodFA [ Verily I struck, or beat, Zeyd ]; and with the agent; as in A_ino qaAma lazayodN [ Verily Zeyd stood ]. (TA.) When the contracted A_ino governs, this l is not necessary; so you may say, A_ino zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Verily Zeyd is standing ]; because in this case it cannot be confounded with the negative; for the negative does not render the subject mansoob and the predicate marfooa: and when it does not govern, if the meaning is apparent, the l is not needed; as in wanaHonu A^ubaApu AlD~ayomi mino A=li maAlikK waA_ino maAlikN kaAnato kiraAma AlmaEaAdini [ And we are persons who refuse to submit to injury, of the family of Málik: and verily the family of Málik are generous in respect of their origins ]; kaAnato being here for lakaAnatN . (I 'Ak p. 99.) ― -b4- [Fourthly,] it is redundant, (S, Mughnee, K,) occurring with maA ; as in the saying, maA A_ino yaquwmu zayodN [ Zeyd does not stand ]; (S;) and in the saying [of a poet], kaA A_ino A^atayota bi$oY'K A^anota takorahuhu [ Thou didst not a thing which thou dislikest ]. (Mughnee, K: in the CK Aatotu .) It is mostly thus used after the negative mA , when put before a verbal proposition; as above; or before a nominal proposition; as in the saying, manaAyaAnaA wadawolapu A=xariynaA wamaA A_ino Tib~unaA jbunN wl`kinN [ And our habit is not cowardice; but our destinies and the good fortune of others caused our being defeated]: and in this case it prevents the government of mA , as in this verse: but in the saying, baniY gudaAnapa maA A_ino A^anotumu *ahabFA walaA SariyfFA wal`kinN A^anotumu Alxazafu [ Sons of Ghudáneh, ye are not indeed gold, nor silver, or pure silver, but ye are pottery ], accord. to him who relates it thus, saying *hbFA and SryfFA , in the accus. case, it is explained as a negative, corroborative of mA : (Mughnee:) and accord. to J, (TA,) the negatives maA and A_inN are sometimes thus combined for corroboration; as in the saying of the rájiz, (El-Aghlab El-'Ijlee, TA,) A^akovara minohu qirapF waqaAraA maA A_inN raA^ayonaA malik~aA A^agaAraA [ We have not indeed seen a king who has made a hostile incursion possessing more numerous sheep, or goats, and camels, than he ]; (S, TA;) but IB says that An is here redundant, not a negative. (TA.) Sometimes it is redundant after the conjunct noun maA ; as in the saying, yurajiY~ AlmaroA_u maA A_inN laA yaraAhu wataEoriDu duwna A^adonaAhu AlxuTuwbu [ Man hopes for that which he will not see; for calamities intervene as obstacles in the way to what is nearest thereof ]. (Mughnee.) And after the maA termed maSodariy~ap , (Mughnee,) [i. e.,] after the adverbial maA [which is of the kind termed mSdry~p ]; (TA;) as in the saying (of Maaloot El-Kurey'ee, cited by Sb, TA), waraj~i AlfataY liloxayori maA A_ino raA^ayotahu Ealay Als~in~i xayorFA laAyazaAlu yaziydu [ And hope thou that the youth is destined for good as long as thou hast seen him not ceasing to increase in good with age ]. (Mughnee.) And after the inceptive A^alaA ; as in the saying, A^alaA A_ino saraY layoliY fbit~u kay^iybaA A^uHaA*iru A^ano tanoA^aY Aln~awaY bigaDuwbaA [ Now he journeyed on, or during, that my night, and I passed the night in an evil state, broken in spirit by grief, being fearful that the distance to which he was going with Ghadoob (a woman so named) would become far ]. (Mughnee.) And before the meddeh denoting disapproval: [for] Sb heard a man, on its being said to him, “ Wilt thou go forth if the desert become plentiful in herbage? ” reply, A^aA^anaA A_iniyhN [ What, I, indeed? ] disapproving that he should think otherwise than that. (Mughnee. [See also art. AnY .]) ― -b5- [Fifthly,] it is syn. with qado : so it is said to be in the saying [in the Kur lxxxvii. 9], A_ino nafaEati A@l*~ikoraY [ Admonition hath profited ], (T, Mughnee, K,) by IAar (T) and by Ktr: (Mughnee:) and Abu-l-' Abbás relates that the Arabs say, A_inN nafaEati A@l*~ikoraY meaning qadoqaAma zayodN [ Zeyd has stood ]; and he adds, that Ks states his having heard them say so, and having thought that it expressed a condition, but that he asked them, and they answered that they meant qadoqaAma zayodN , and not maA qaAma zayodN . (T.) [So too, accord. to the K, in all the exs. cited in the next sentence as from the Mughnee; but this is evidently a mistake, occasioned by an accidental omission.] ― -b6- [Sixthly,] it is asserted also by the Koofees, that it is syn. with A_i*o , in the following exs.: in the Kur [v. 62], waA@t~aquwA A@ll~`ha A_inN kunotumo muw^ominiyna [ And fear ye God, because ye are believers: and so, accord. to AZ, as is said in the T, in a similar instance in the Kur ii. 278: and in the same, iv. 62]: and [in the Kur xlviii. 27,] latado xulun~a A@lmasojida A@loHaraAma A_ino $aA='a A=miniyna [ Ye shall assuredly enter the sacred mosque, because God hath willed, in security ]: and in like instances, when the verb therein expresses what is held sure to happen or to have happened: and in the saying, A^atagoDabu A_inN A^udonaA qutayobapa Huz~ataA jihaArFA walamo tagoDabo liqatoli A@boni HaAzimi [ Art thou angry because the ears of Kuteybeh have been cut, openly, or publicly, and wast not angry for the slaughter of Ibn-Házim? ]: (Mughnee:) but in all these instances [it is sufficiently obvious that] An may be otherwise explained. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b7- [Seventhly,] it is sometimes syn. with A_i*aA ; as in the Kur [ix. 23], laA tat~axi*uwA A=baA='akumo waA_ixowaAnakumo A^awoliyaA='a A_ini A@sotaHab~uwA A@lokuforaEalaY A@loA_iymaAni [ Take not ye your fathers and your brethren as friends when they love unbelief above belief ]; and in the same [xxxiii. 49], waA@moraA^apF muw^ominapF A_ino wahabato nafosahaA liln~abiY~ [ And a believing woman when she giveth herself to the Prophet ]: so says AZ. (T.) ― -b8- [Eighthly,] it is used for A_im~aA , (Mughnee and K, voce A_im~aA ,) distinct from A_im~aA which is a compound of the conditional A_inN and the redundant maA . (Mughnee ibid.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce A_im~aA in the present work, commencing with the words saqatohu Alr~awaAEidu .]

definition: is one of the particles which annul the quality of the inchoative;
sourceDefinition: is one of the particles which annul the quality of the inchoative; and is originally A_in~a ; therefore Sb has not mentioned it among those particles [as distinct from A_in~a , from which, however, it is distinguished in meaning]: (I 'Ak p. 90:) it is a corroborative particle; (I 'Ak, Mughnee;) a particle governing the subject in the accus. case and the predicate in the nom. case, (S, I 'Ak, Mughnee, K,) combining with what follows it to form an equivalent to an inf. n., (S,) [for,] accord. to the most correct opinion, it is a conjunct particle, which, together with its two objects of government, is explained by means of an inf. n. (Mughnee.) If the predicate is derived, the inf. n. by means of which it is explained is of the same radical letters; so that the implied meaning of balaganiy A^an~aka tanoTaliqu [ It has come to my knowledge, or been related to me, or been told to me, or it came to my knowledge, &c., that thou goest away ], or A^an~aka munoTaliqN [ that thou art going away ], is balaganiy AlAinoTilaAqu [or rather A@noTilaAquka thy going away has come to my knowledge, &c.]; and hence, the implied meaning of balaganiY A^an~aka fiy Ald~aAri [ It has come to my knowledge, &c., that thou art in the house ] is balaganiY A@sotiqoraAruka fiy Ald~aAri [ thy remaining in the house has come to my knowledge, &c.], because thea predicate is properly a word suppressed from Aistaqar~a or musotaqir~N : and if the predicate is underived, the implied meaning is explained by the word kawoni ; so that the implied meaning of balaganiY A^an~a h`*A zayodN [ It has come to my knowledge, &c., that this is Zeyd ] is balaganiY kawonuhu zayodFA [ his being Zeyd has come to my knowledge, &c.]; for the relation of every predicate expressed by an underived word to its subject may be denoted by a word signifying “ being; ” so that you say, h`*aA zayodN and, if you will, h`*aA kaAy^inN zayodFA ; both signifying the same. (Mughnee.) There are cases in which either A^an~a or A_in~a may be used: [see the latter, in twelve places:] other cases in which only the former may be used: and others in which only the latter. (I 'Ak p. 91.) The former only may be used when the implied meaning is to be explained by an inf. n. (I 'Ak, K.) Such is the case when it occurs in the place of a noun governed by a verb in the nom. case; as in yuEojibuniY A^an~aka qaAy^imN [ It pleases me that thou art standing ], i. e. qiyaAmuka [ thy standing pleases me]: or in the place of a noun governed by a verb in the accus. case; as in Earafotu A^at~aka qaAy^imN [ I knew that thou wast standing ], i. e. qiyaAmaka [ thy standing ]: or in the place of a noun governed in the gen. case by a particle; as in Eajibotu mino A^an~aka qaAy^imN [ I wondered that thou wast standing ], i. e. mino qiyaAmka [ at, or by reason of, thy standing ]: (I 'Ak p. 91:) [and sometimes a preposition is understood; as in laA $ak~a A^an~ahu ka*aA , for laA $ak~a fiY A^an~ahu ka*aA There is no doubt that it is thus, i. e. laA $~k~a fiY kawonihi ka*aA There is no doubt of its being thus: ] and A^an~a must be used after lawo ; as in lawo A^an~aka qaAy^imN laqumotu [ If that thou wert standing, I had stood, or would have stood, i. e. lawo vabata qiyaAmuka , or lawo qiyaAmuka vaAbitN , accord. to different opinions, both meaning if thy standing were a fact: see I 'Ak pp. 305 and 306]. (K.) Sometimes its A^ is changed into E ; so that you say, Ealimotu Ean~aka munoTaliqN [meaning I knew that thou wast going away ]. (M.) ― -b2- With k prefixed to it, it is a particle of comparison, (S, * M, TA,) [still] governing the subject in the accus. case and the predicate in the nom. case: (TA:) you say, kaA^an~a zayodFA EamorNw [It is as though Zeyd were 'Amr ], meaning that Zeyd is like 'Amr; as though you said, A_in~a zayodFA kaAy^inN kaEamorKw [ verily, Zeyd is like 'Amr ]: [it is to be accounted for by an ellipsis: or] the k is taken away from the middle of this proposition, and put at its commencement, and then the kesreh of A_in~a necessarily becomes changed to a fet-hah, because A_in~a cannot be preceded by a preposition, for it never occurs but at the commencement [of a proposition]. (IJ, M.) Sometimes, kaA^an~a denotes denial; as in the saying, kaA^an~aka A^amiyrunaA fataA^omuranaA [ As though thou wert our commander so that thou shouldst command us ], meaning thou art not our commander [ that thou shouldst command us ]. (TA.) It also denotes wishing; as in the saying, kaA^on~aka biy qado qulotu Al$~iEora faA^ujiydahu , meaning Would that I had poetized, or versified, so that I might do it well: (TA:) [an elliptical form of speech, of which the implied meaning seems to be, would that I were as though thou sawest me that I had poetized, &c.; or the like: for] you say [also], kaA^an~iY bika meaning kaA^an~iY A^aboSuru bika [It is as though I saw thee ]; i. e. I know from what I witness of thy condition to-day how thy condition will be tomorrow; so that it is as though I saw thee in that condition: (Har p. 126: [see also bi ; near the end of the paragraph:]) [thus,] kaA^an~a also denotes knowing; and also thinking; [the former as in the saying immediately preceding, and] as when you say, kaA^an~a A@ll~`ha yafoEalu maA ya$aA='u [ I know, or rather it appears, as though seen, that God does what He wills ]; and [the latter as when you say,] kaA^an~aka xaArijN [ I think, or rather it seems, that Thou art going forth ]. (TA.) ― -b3- [When it has The affixed pronoun of the first person, sing. Or Pl., you say, A^an~iY and A^an~aniY , and A^an~aA and A^an~anaA : and When it has also the k of comparison prefixed to It,] you say, kaA^an~iY and kaA^an~aniY , [and kaA^an~aA and kaA^an~anaA ,] like as you say, l`kin~iY and l`kin~aniY [&c.]. (S.) ― -b4- As A^an~a is a derivative from A_in~a , it is correctly asserted by Z that A^an~amaA imports restriction, like ↓ A_in~amaA ; both of which occur in the saying in the Kur [xxi. 108], yuwHaY A_ilaY~a A^an~amaA ↓ qulo A_in~amaA A_il`hukumo A_il`hF waAHidN [ Say thou, It is only revealed to me that your God is only one God ]: the former is for the restricting of the quality to the qualified; and the latter, for the reverse: (Mughnee, K:) i. e. the former is for the restricting of the revelation to the declaration of the unity; and the latter, for the restricting of “ your God ” to unity: (Marginal note in a copy of the Mughnee:) but these words of the Kur do not imply that nothing save the unity was revealed to the Prophet; for the restriction is limited to the case of the discourse with the believers in a plurality of gods; so that the meaning is, there has not been revealed to me [aught], respecting the godhead, except the unity; not the attribution of any associate to God. (Mughnee.) [ A^an~amaA , however, does not always import restriction; nor does always even ↓ A_in~amaA : in each of these, mA is what is termed kaAf~apN ; i. e., it restricts the particle to which it is affixed from exercising any government; and sometimes has no effect upon the signification of that particle: (see art. maA ; and see A_in~amaA , below, voce A_in~a :) thus, for instance, in the Kur viii. 28, waA@EolamuwA A^an~amaA A^amowaAlukumo fitonapF means And know ye that your possessions and your children are a trial; not that they are only a trial. (IAar.) ― -b5- A^an~a is someTimes contracted into A^ano ; (S, Mughnee;) and in This case, it governs in the manner already exPlained, voce A^ano . (meaning, maketh you to know that they will believe when it cometh? i. e. ye do not know that: Jel:) Maybe, when it cometh, they will not believe ]: (S, M, Mughnee, K:) thus accord. to this reading: (Mughnee, K:) and Ubeí here reads laEal~ahaA . (S.) A^an~a and laA^an~a and lawo A^an~a are all syn. with Eal~a and laEal~a ; and A^an~iY and A^an~aniY , and laA^an~iY and lA^an~aniY , and luwo A^an~iY and lawo A^an~iniY , with Eal~iY and laEal~iY . (K voce laEal~a .) ― -b7- It is also syn. with A^ajalo [ Yes, or yea; or it is as thou sayest ]. (M, TA.) [See also A_in~a as exemplified by a verse commencing with wayaqulona and by a saying of Ibn-Ez-Zubeyr.]
