rawSourceText: is one of the particles which annul the quality of the inchoative; and is originally A_in~a ; therefore Sb has not mentioned it among those particles [as distinct from A_in~a , from which, however, it is distinguished in meaning]: (I 'Ak p. 90:) it is a corroborative particle; (I 'Ak, Mughnee;) a particle governing the subject in the accus. case and the predicate in the nom. case, (S, I 'Ak, Mughnee, K,) combining with what follows it to form an equivalent to an inf. n., (S,) [for,] accord. to the most correct opinion, it is a conjunct particle, which, together with its two objects of government, is explained by means of an inf. n. (Mughnee.) If the predicate is derived, the inf. n. by means of which it is explained is of the same radical letters; so that the implied meaning of balaganiy A^an~aka tanoTaliqu [ It has come to my knowledge, or been related to me, or been told to me, or it came to my knowledge, &c., that thou goest away ], or A^an~aka munoTaliqN [ that thou art going away ], is balaganiy AlAinoTilaAqu [or rather A@noTilaAquka thy going away has come to my knowledge, &c.]; and hence, the implied meaning of balaganiY A^an~aka fiy Ald~aAri [ It has come to my knowledge, &c., that thou art in the house ] is balaganiY A@sotiqoraAruka fiy Ald~aAri [ thy remaining in the house has come to my knowledge, &c.], because thea predicate is properly a word suppressed from Aistaqar~a or musotaqir~N : and if the predicate is underived, the implied meaning is explained by the word kawoni ; so that the implied meaning of balaganiY A^an~a h`*A zayodN [ It has come to my knowledge, &c., that this is Zeyd ] is balaganiY kawonuhu zayodFA [ his being Zeyd has come to my knowledge, &c.]; for the relation of every predicate expressed by an underived word to its subject may be denoted by a word signifying “ being; ” so that you say, h`*aA zayodN and, if you will, h`*aA kaAy^inN zayodFA ; both signifying the same. (Mughnee.) There are cases in which either A^an~a or A_in~a may be used: [see the latter, in twelve places:] other cases in which only the former may be used: and others in which only the latter. (I 'Ak p. 91.) The former only may be used when the implied meaning is to be explained by an inf. n. (I 'Ak, K.) Such is the case when it occurs in the place of a noun governed by a verb in the nom. case; as in yuEojibuniY A^an~aka qaAy^imN [ It pleases me that thou art standing ], i. e. qiyaAmuka [ thy standing pleases me]: or in the place of a noun governed by a verb in the accus. case; as in Earafotu A^at~aka qaAy^imN [ I knew that thou wast standing ], i. e. qiyaAmaka [ thy standing ]: or in the place of a noun governed in the gen. case by a particle; as in Eajibotu mino A^an~aka qaAy^imN [ I wondered that thou wast standing ], i. e. mino qiyaAmka [ at, or by reason of, thy standing ]: (I 'Ak p. 91:) [and sometimes a preposition is understood; as in laA $ak~a A^an~ahu ka*aA , for laA $ak~a fiY A^an~ahu ka*aA There is no doubt that it is thus, i. e. laA $~k~a fiY kawonihi ka*aA There is no doubt of its being thus: ] and A^an~a must be used after lawo ; as in lawo A^an~aka qaAy^imN laqumotu [ If that thou wert standing, I had stood, or would have stood, i. e. lawo vabata qiyaAmuka , or lawo qiyaAmuka vaAbitN , accord. to different opinions, both meaning if thy standing were a fact: see I 'Ak pp. 305 and 306]. (K.) Sometimes its A^ is changed into E ; so that you say, Ealimotu Ean~aka munoTaliqN [meaning I knew that thou wast going away ]. (M.) ― -b2- With k prefixed to it, it is a particle of comparison, (S, * M, TA,) [still] governing the subject in the accus. case and the predicate in the nom. case: (TA:) you say, kaA^an~a zayodFA EamorNw [It is as though Zeyd were 'Amr ], meaning that Zeyd is like 'Amr; as though you said, A_in~a zayodFA kaAy^inN kaEamorKw [ verily, Zeyd is like 'Amr ]: [it is to be accounted for by an ellipsis: or] the k is taken away from the middle of this proposition, and put at its commencement, and then the kesreh of A_in~a necessarily becomes changed to a fet-hah, because A_in~a cannot be preceded by a preposition, for it never occurs but at the commencement [of a proposition]. (IJ, M.) Sometimes, kaA^an~a denotes denial; as in the saying, kaA^an~aka A^amiyrunaA fataA^omuranaA [ As though thou wert our commander so that thou shouldst command us ], meaning thou art not our commander [ that thou shouldst command us ]. (TA.) It also denotes wishing; as in the saying, kaA^on~aka biy qado qulotu Al$~iEora faA^ujiydahu , meaning Would that I had poetized, or versified, so that I might do it well: (TA:) [an elliptical form of speech, of which the implied meaning seems to be, would that I were as though thou sawest me that I had poetized, &c.; or the like: for] you say [also], kaA^an~iY bika meaning kaA^an~iY A^aboSuru bika [It is as though I saw thee ]; i. e. I know from what I witness of thy condition to-day how thy condition will be tomorrow; so that it is as though I saw thee in that condition: (Har p. 126: [see also bi ; near the end of the paragraph:]) [thus,] kaA^an~a also denotes knowing; and also thinking; [the former as in the saying immediately preceding, and] as when you say, kaA^an~a A@ll~`ha yafoEalu maA ya$aA='u [ I know, or rather it appears, as though seen, that God does what He wills ]; and [the latter as when you say,] kaA^an~aka xaArijN [ I think, or rather it seems, that Thou art going forth ]. sourceDefinition: is one of the particles which annul the quality of the inchoative, like A^an~a , of which it is the original: (I 'Ak p. 90:) it is a corroborative particle, (I 'Ak, Mughnee,) corroborating the predicate; (S, K;) governing the subject in the accus. case and the predicate in the nom. case; (S, I 'Ak, Mughnee, K;) [and may generally be rendered by Verily, or certainly, or the like; exactly agreeing with the Greek ὃτι , as used in Luke vii. 16 and in many other passages in the New Testament; though it often seems to be nothing more than a sign of inception, which can hardly be rendered at all in English; unless in pronunciation, by laying a stress upon the predicate, or upon the copula;] as in the saying, A_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Verily, or certainly, Zeyd is standing; or simply, Zeyd is standing, if we lay a stress upon standing, or upon is]. (I 'Ak p. 90.) But sometimes it governs both the subject and the predicate in the accus. case; as in the saying, A_i*aA A@$otad~a junoHu All~ayoli falotaA^oti walotakunN xuTaAka xifaAfFA A_in~a Hur~aAsanaA A^usodaA [ When the darkness of night becomes, or shall become, intense, then do thou come, and let thy steps be light: verily our guardians are lions ]; (Mughnee, K; [but in the latter, for A@$otad~a , we find A@sowad~a , so that the meaning is, when the first portion of the night becomes, or shall become, black, &c.;]) and as in a trad. in which it is said, An~a qaEora jahan~ama saboEiyna xariyfFA [ Verily the bottom of Hell is a distance of seventy years of journeying]: (Mughnee, K:) the verse, however, is explained by the supposition that it presents a denotative of state [in the last word, which is equivalent to $ijoEaAnFA or the like], and that the predicate is suppressed, the meaning being, taloqaAhumo A^usodFA [ thou wilt find them lions ]; and the trad. by the supposition that qaEora is an inf. n., and saboEiyna is an adverbial noun, so that the meaning is, the reaching the bottom of hell is [to be accomplished in no less time than] in seventy years. (Mughnee.) And sometimes the inchoative [of a proposition] after it is in the nom. case, and its subject is what is termed Damiyru $aA^onK , suppressed; as in the saying of Mohammad, A_in~a mino A^a$ad~i Aln~aAsi Ea*aAbFA yawoma Alqiy`mapi AlmuSaw~iruwna [ Verily, ( the case is this:) of the men most severely to be punished, on the day of resurrection, are the makers of images ], originally A_in~ahu , i. e. A_in~a Al$~aA^ona ; (Mughnee, K; *) and as in the saying in the Kur [xx. 66], A_in~a h`*aAni lasaAHiraAni , [accord. to some,] as will be seen in what follows. (TA.) ― -b2- Of the two particles A_in~a and ↓ A^an~a , in certain cases only the former may be used; and in certain other cases either of them may be used. (I' Ak p. 91.) The former must be used when it occurs inceptively, (Kh, T, I' Ak p. 92, Mughnee, K,) having nothing before it upon which it is syntactically dependent, (Kh, T,) with respect to the wording or the meaning; (K;) as in A_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Verily Zeyd is standing ]. (I' Ak, K.) It is used after A^alaA , (I' Ak, K,) the inceptive particle, (I' Ak,) or the particle which is employed to give notice [of something about to be said]; (K;) as in A^alaA A_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Now surely Zeyd is standing ]. (I' Ak K.) And when it occurs at the commencement of the complement of a conjunct noun; (I' Ak, K; *) as in jaA='a Al~a*iY A_in~ahu qaAy^imN [ He who is standing came ]; (I' Ak;) and in the Kur [xxviii. 76], waA=tayonaAhu mina A@lokunuwri maA A_in~a mafaAtiHahu latanuwo'u biA@loEuSobapi A^uwliY Alquw~api [ And we gave him, of treasures, that whereof the keys would weigh down the company of men possessed of strength ]. (I' Ak, * K, * TA.) And in the complement of an oath, (I' Ak, K,) when its predicate has la , (I' Ak,) or whether its subject or its predicate has la or has it not; (K;) as in waA@ll~`hi A_in~a zayodFA laqaAy^imN [ By Allah, verily Zeyd is standing ], (I' Ak,) and A_in~ahu qaAy^imN : or, as some say, when you do not employ the l , the particle is with fet-h; as in qaAy^imN ↓ waA@ll~`hi A^an~aka [I swear by Allah that thou art standing ]; mentioned by Ks as thus heard by him from the Arabs: (TA:) but respecting this case we shall have to speak hereafter. (I' Ak.) And when it occurs after the word qawolN or a derivative thereof, in repeating the saying to which that word relates; (Fr, T, I' Ak, * K; *) as in the saying [in the Kur iv. 156], waqawolihimo A_in~aA qatalonaA A@lomasiyHa [ And their saying, Verily we have slain the Messiah ]; (Fr, T;) and qulotu A_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ I said, Verily Zeyd is standing ]; (I' Ak;) and [in the Kur v. 115,] qaAla A@ll~`hu A_in~Y mun~z~iluhaA Ealayokumo [ God said, Verily I will cause it to descend unto you ]; accord. to the dial. of him who does not pronounce it with fet-h: (K:) but when it occurs in explaining what is said, you use ↓ A^an~a ; as in the saying, qado qulotu laka kalaAmFA HasanFA A^an~a A^abaAka $ariyfN waA^an~aka EaAqilN [ I have said to thee a good saying; that thy father is noble and that thou art intelligent ]; (Fr, T;) or when the word signifying “ saying ” is used as meaning “ thinking; ” as in A^ataquwlu A^an~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Dost thou say that Zeyd is standing? ], meaning A^ataZun~u [ Dost thou think? ]. (I' Ak.) Also, when it occurs in a phrase denotative of state; (I' Ak;) [i. e.,] after the w denotative of state; (K;) as in zurotuhu waA_in~iY *uwA^amalK [ I visited him, I verily having hope, or expectation ]; (I' Ak;) and in jaA='a ziyodN wa A_in~a yadahu EalaY raA^osihi [ Zeyd came, he verily having his hand upon his head ]. (K.) And when it occurs in a phrase which is the predicate of a proper (as opposed to an ideal) substantive; (I' Ak, K; *) as in zayodN A_in~ahu qaAy^imN [ Zeyd, verily he is standing ], (I' Ak,) or *aAhibN [ going away ]; contr. to the assertion of Fr. (K.) And when it occurs before the l which suspends the grammatical government of a verb of the mind, preceding it, with respect to its objective complements; (I' Ak, K; *) as in Ealimotu A_in~a zayodFA laqaAy^imN [ I knew Zeyd verily was standing ]; (I' Ak;) and in [the Kur lxiii. 1,] waA@ll~`hu yaEolamu A_in~aka larasuwluhu [ And God knoweth thou verily art his apostle ]: (K:) but if the l is not in its predicate, you say, ↓ A^an~a ; as in Ealimotu A^an~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ I knew that Zeyd was standing ]. (I' Ak.) And in the like of the saying in the Kur [ii. 171], waA_in~a A@l~a*iyna A@xotalafuwA fiY A@lokitaAbi lafiY $aqaAqK baEiydK [ And verily they who differ among themselves respecting the book are in an opposition remote from the truth]; because of the l [of inception] which occurs after it, in lafiY : (Ks, A 'Obeyd:) the l of inception which occurs before the predicate of A_in~a should properly commence the sentence; so that A_in~a zayodFA laqaAy^imN [ Verily Zeyd is standing ] should properly be laA_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN ; but as the l is a corroborative and A_in~a is a corroborative, they dislike putting two particles of the same meaning together, and therefore they put the l later, transferring it to the predicate: Mbr allows its being put before the predicate of ↓ A^an~a ; and thus it occurs in an unusual reading of the saying [in the Kur xxv. 22], A_il~aA A^an~ahumo layaA^okuluwna A@lT~aEaAma [ But they ate food ]; but this is explained by the supposition that the l is here redundant: (I' Ak p. 95:) this is the reading of Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr: others read, A_il~aA A_in~ahumo layaA^okuluna AlT~aEaAma [ but verily they ate food ]: and A_in~a [as well as ↓ A^an~a ] is used after the exceptive A_il~aA when it is not followed by the l [of inception]. (TA.) Also, When it occurs after Hayovu ; as in Aijoliso Hayovu A_in~a zayodFA jaAlisN [ Sit thou where Zeyd is sitting ]. (I' Ak p. 92, and k) And after Hat~aY ; as in mariDa zayodN Hat~aY A_in~ahumo laA yarojuwnahu [ Zeyd has fallen sick, so that verily they have no hope for him : whereas after a particle governing the gen. case, [i. e. a preposition,] you say, ↓ A^an~a . (IHsh in De Sacy's Anthol. Gr. Ar. P. 76.) ― -b3- Either of these two forms may be used after A_i*aA denoting a thing's happening suddenly, or unexpectedly; as in xarajotu faA_i*aA A_in~a zayodFAqaAy^imN [ I went forth, and lo, verily Zeyd was standing ], and zayodFA qaAy^imN ↓ faA_i*aA A^an~a [ and lo, or at that present time, Zeyd's standing ]; in which latter case, A^an~a with its complement is [properly] an inchoative, and its enunciative is A_i*aA ; the implied meaning being, and at that present time was the standing of Zeyd: or it may be that the enunciative is suppressed, and that the implied meaning is, [ and lo, or at that present time, ] the standing of Zeyd was an event come to pass. (I' Ak p. 93.) Also, when occurring in the complement of an oath, if its enunciative is without l : (I' Ak:) [see exs. given above:] or, as some say, only ↓ A^an~a is used in this case. (TA.) Also, when occurring after fa denoting the complement of a condition; as in mano yaA^otiniY faA_in~ahu mukoramN [ He who cometh to me, verily he shall be treated with honour ], and mukoramN ↓ A^an~ahu ; in which latter case, A^an~a with its complement is an inchoative, and the enunciative is suppressed; the implied meaning being, honourable treatment of him shall be an event come to pass: or it may be an enunciative to an inchoative suppressed; the implied meaning being, his recompense shall be honourable treatment. (I' Ak p. 94.) Also, when occurring after an inchoative having the meaning of a saying, its enunciative being a saying, and the sayer being one; as in xayoru Alqawoli A_in~Y A^aHomadu [ The best saying is, Verily I praise God], and A^aHomadu ↓ A^an~iY ; in which latter case, A^an~a with its complement is an enunciative of xayoru ; the implied meaning being, the best saying is the praising of God [or my praising of God]. (I' Ak ubi suprà.) You also say, lab~ayoka A_in~a AlHamodalaka [ At thy service ! Verily praise belongeth to Thee! O God]; commencing [with A_in~a ] a new proposition: and sometimes one says, ↓ A^an~a ; meaning biA^an~a AlHamoda laka [ because praise belongeth to Thee ]. (Msb.) ― -b4- The cases in which A_in may not be used in the place of A^an~a have been mentioned above, voce A^an~a . ― -b5- [When it has the affixed pronoun of the first person, sing. or pl.,] you say, A_in~iY and A_in~aniY , (S,) and A_in~aA and A_in~anaA , (TA,) like as you say l`kin~iY and l`kin~iniY [&c.]. (S.) A_in~a as a contraction of A_in~a A^anaA has been mentioned above, as occurring in the phrase A_in~a qaAy^imN , voce A_ino , q. v. ― -b6- Accord. to the grammarians, (T,) A_in~amaA is a compound of A_in~a and maA , (T, S,) which latter prevents the former's having any government: (T:) it imports restriction; like A^an~amaA , which see above, voce A^an~a , in three places: (Mughnee, K:) [i. e.] it imports the restriction of that which it precedes to that which follows it; as in A_in~amaA zayodN munoTaliqN [ Zeyd is only going away ], and A_in~amaA yanoTaliqu zayodN [ Only Zeyd goes away ]: (Bd in ii. 10:) [in other words,] it is used to particularize, or specify, or distinguish a thing from other things: (S:) it affirms a thing in relation to that which is mentioned after it, and denies it in relation to other things; (T, S;) as in the saying in the Kur [ix. 60], A_in~amaA A@lS~adaqaAtu lilofuqaraA='i [ The contributions levied for pious uses are only, or but, for the poor ]: (S:) but El- Ámidee and AHei say that it does not import restriction, but only corroboration of an affirmation, because it is a compound of the corroborative A_in~a and the redundant maA which restrains the former from exercising government, and that it has no application to denote negation implied in restriction, as is shown by the trad., A_in~amaA Al~iribaA fiY Aln~asiyoy^api [which must mean, Verily usury is in the delay of payment ], for usury is in other things beside that here mentioned, as ribaA AlfDoli [or profit obtained by the superior value of a thing received over that of a thing given], by common consent: (Kull p. 76:) some say that it necessarily imports restriction: J says what has been cited above from the S: some say that it has an overt signification in denoting restriction, and is susceptible of the meaning of corroboration: some say the reverse of this: El-Ámidee says that if it were [properly] restrictive, its occurrence in another sense would be at variance with the original import; but to this it may be replied, that if it were [properly] corroborative, its occurrence in another sense would be at variance with the original import: it [therefore] seems that it is susceptible of both these meanings, bearing one or the other according as this or that suits the place. (Msb.) A_in~amaA is to be distinguished from A_in~a with the conjunct [noun] maA , which does not restrain it from governing [though its government with this is not apparent, and which is written separately]; as in A_in~a maA Einoka HasanN meaning Verily what is with thee is good, and in A_in~a maA faEalota HasanN meaning Verily thy deed is good. (I' Ak pp. 97 and 98.) ― -b7- A_in~a is sometimes contracted into A_inN ; (S, Mughnee, K;) and in this case, it is made to govern and is made to have no government: (S:) it is seldom made to govern in this case; often made to have no government: the Koofees say that it is not contracted; (Mughnee, K;) and that when one says, A_ino zayodN lamunoTaliqN [the meaning is virtually Verily Zeyd is going away, but] A_inN is a negative and the l is syn. with A_il~A ; but this assertion is refuted by the fact that some make it to govern when contracted, as in exs. cited above, voce A_ino , q. v. (Mughnee.) ― -b8- It is also syn. with naEamN [ Even so; yes; yea ]; (Mughnee, K;) contr. to the opinion of AO. (Mughnee.) [See also A^an~a , last sentence.] Those who affirm it to have this meaning cite as an ex. the following verse (Mughnee, K *) of 'Obeyd-Allah Ibn-Keys-er-Rukeiyát: (S, * TA:) ka waqado kabirota faqulotu A_in~aho wayaqulona $ayobN qado EalaA [ And they say, (namely, the women,) Hoariness hath come upon thee, and thou hast become old: and I say, Even so, or yes, or yea ]: (Mughnee, K:) but this has been rebutted by the saying, We do not concede that the h is here added to denote the pause, but assert that it is a pronoun, governed by A_in~a in the accus. case, and the predicate is suppressed; the meaning being, A_in~ahu ka*`lika [ Verily it, i. e. the case, is thus ]. (Mughnee.) [J says,] The meaning is, A_n~ahu qado kaAna kamaA taqulona [ Verily it, i. e. the case, hath been as ye say ]: A 'Obeyd says, This is a curtailment of the speech of the Arabs; the pronoun being deemed sufficient because the meaning is known: and as to the saying of Akh, that it signifies naEamo , he only means thereby that it may be so rendered, not that it is originally applied to that signification: he says that the h is here added to denote the pause. (S.) There is, however, a good ex. of A_in~a in the sense of naEamo in the saying of Ibn-Ez-Zubeyr, to him who said to him, “May God curse a she camel which carried me to thee,” A_in~a waraAkibahaA , i. e. Even so, or yes, or yea; and may God curse her rider: for the suppression of both the subject and the predicate is not allowable. (Mughnee.) And hence, accord. to Mbr, the saying in the Kur [xx. 66], as thus read, A_in~a h`*Ani lasaAHiraAni [meaning, if so, Yes, these two are enchanters ]. (Mughnee.) [But this phrase has given rise to much discussion, related in the Mughnee and other works. The following is a brief abstract of what has been said respecting it by several of the leading authorities.] A booIs-hák says that the people of El-Medeeneh and El-Koofeh read as above, except 'Ásim, who is reported to have read, A_inN h`*aAni , without tesh-deed, and so is Kh; [so too is Hafs, as is said above, voce A_ino ;] and that AA read A_in~a h`*yoni , the former word with teshdeed, and the latter in the accus. case: that the argument for A_in~a h`*aAni , with teshdeed and the nom. case, [or rather what is identical in form with the nom. case,] is, that it is of the dial. of Kináneh, in which the dual is formed by the termination An in the nom. and accus. and gen. cases alike, as also in the dial. of Benu-l-Hárith Ibn-Kaab: but that the old grammarians say that h is here suppressed; the meaning being, A_in~ahu h`*aAni : (T:) this last assertion, however, is weak; for what is applied to the purpose of corroboration should not be suppressed, and the instances of its suppression which have been heard are deviations from general usage, except in the case of A^an~a , with fet-h, contracted into A^ano : (Mughnee:) Aboo-Is-hák then adds, that some say, A_in~a is here syn. with naEamo : this last opinion he holds to be the best; the meaning being, naEamo h`*aAni lahumaA saAHiraAni [ Yes, these two, verily they are two enchanters: for this is not a case in which the l (which is the l of inception) can be regarded as transferred from its proper place, at the commencement of the sentence or proposition, as it is in some instances mentioned in the former half of this paragraph: but it is said in the Mughnee that this explanation is invalidated by the fact that the combining of the corroborative l and the suppression of the inchoative is like the combining of two things inconsistent, or incompatible; as is also the opinion that the l is redundant, because the redundant l prefixed to the enunciative is peculiar to poetry]: next in point of goodness, in the opinion of A booIs-hák, is, that it is of the dial. of Kináneh and Benu-l-Hárith Ibn-Kaab: the reading of AA he does not allow, because it is at variance with the written text: but he approves the reading of 'Ásim and Kh. (T.) -A2- A_in~a also occurs as a verb: it is the third person pl. fem. of the pret. from AlA^ayonu , syn. with Alt~aEabu ; or from A=na syn. with qaruba : or the third person sing. masc. of the pret. passive from AlA^anyinu , in the dial. of those who, for rud~a and Hub~a , say rid~a and Hib~a , likening these verbs to qiyla and biyEa : or the sing. masc. of the imperative from the same: or the pl. fem. of the imperative from AlA^ayonu ; or from A=na syn. with qaruba : or the sing. fem. of the corroborated form of the imperative from waA^aY , syn. with waEada . (Mughnee.) A^anaA , signifying I: see A^ano , in seven places.

rawSourceText: is one of the particles which annul the quality of the inchoative, like A^an~a , of which it is the original: (I 'Ak p. 90:) it is a corroborative particle, (I 'Ak, Mughnee,) corroborating the predicate; (S, K;) governing the subject in the accus. case and the predicate in the nom. case; (S, I 'Ak, Mughnee, K;) [and may generally be rendered by Verily, or certainly, or the like; exactly agreeing with the Greek ὃτι , as used in Luke vii. 16 and in many other passages in the New Testament; though it often seems to be nothing more than a sign of inception, which can hardly be rendered at all in English; unless in pronunciation, by laying a stress upon the predicate, or upon the copula;] as in the saying, A_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Verily, or certainly, Zeyd is standing; or simply, Zeyd is standing, if we lay a stress upon standing, or upon is]. (I 'Ak p. 90.) But sometimes it governs both the subject and the predicate in the accus. case; as in the saying, A_i*aA A@$otad~a junoHu All~ayoli falotaA^oti walotakunN xuTaAka xifaAfFA A_in~a Hur~aAsanaA A^usodaA [ When the darkness of night becomes, or shall become, intense, then do thou come, and let thy steps be light: verily our guardians are lions ]; (Mughnee, K; [but in the latter, for A@$otad~a , we find A@sowad~a , so that the meaning is, when the first portion of the night becomes, or shall become, black, &c.;]) and as in a trad. in which it is said, An~a qaEora jahan~ama saboEiyna xariyfFA [ Verily the bottom of Hell is a distance of seventy years of journeying]: (Mughnee, K:) the verse, however, is explained by the supposition that it presents a denotative of state [in the last word, which is equivalent to $ijoEaAnFA or the like], and that the predicate is suppressed, the meaning being, taloqaAhumo A^usodFA [ thou wilt find them lions ]; and the trad. by the supposition that qaEora is an inf. n., and saboEiyna is an adverbial noun, so that the meaning is, the reaching the bottom of hell is [to be accomplished in no less time than] in seventy years. (Mughnee.) And sometimes the inchoative [of a proposition] after it is in the nom. case, and its subject is what is termed Damiyru $aA^onK , suppressed; as in the saying of Mohammad, A_in~a mino A^a$ad~i Aln~aAsi Ea*aAbFA yawoma Alqiy`mapi AlmuSaw~iruwna [ Verily, ( the case is this:) of the men most severely to be punished, on the day of resurrection, are the makers of images ], originally A_in~ahu , i. e. A_in~a Al$~aA^ona ; (Mughnee, K; *) and as in the saying in the Kur [xx. 66], A_in~a h`*aAni lasaAHiraAni , [accord. to some,] as will be seen in what follows. (TA.) ― -b2- Of the two particles A_in~a and ↓ A^an~a , in certain cases only the former may be used; and in certain other cases either of them may be used. (I' Ak p. 91.) The former must be used when it occurs inceptively, (Kh, T, I' Ak p. 92, Mughnee, K,) having nothing before it upon which it is syntactically dependent, (Kh, T,) with respect to the wording or the meaning; (K;) as in A_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Verily Zeyd is standing ]. (I' Ak, K.) It is used after A^alaA , (I' Ak, K,) the inceptive particle, (I' Ak,) or the particle which is employed to give notice [of something about to be said]; (K;) as in A^alaA A_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Now surely Zeyd is standing ]. (I' Ak K.) And when it occurs at the commencement of the complement of a conjunct noun; (I' Ak, K; *) as in jaA='a Al~a*iY A_in~ahu qaAy^imN [ He who is standing came ]; (I' Ak;) and in the Kur [xxviii. 76], waA=tayonaAhu mina A@lokunuwri maA A_in~a mafaAtiHahu latanuwo'u biA@loEuSobapi A^uwliY Alquw~api [ And we gave him, of treasures, that whereof the keys would weigh down the company of men possessed of strength ]. (I' Ak, * K, * TA.) And in the complement of an oath, (I' Ak, K,) when its predicate has la , (I' Ak,) or whether its subject or its predicate has la or has it not; (K;) as in waA@ll~`hi A_in~a zayodFA laqaAy^imN [ By Allah, verily Zeyd is standing ], (I' Ak,) and A_in~ahu qaAy^imN : or, as some say, when you do not employ the l , the particle is with fet-h; as in qaAy^imN ↓ waA@ll~`hi A^an~aka [I swear by Allah that thou art standing ]; mentioned by Ks as thus heard by him from the Arabs: (TA:) but respecting this case we shall have to speak hereafter. (I' Ak.) And when it occurs after the word qawolN or a derivative thereof, in repeating the saying to which that word relates; (Fr, T, I' Ak, * K; *) as in the saying [in the Kur iv. 156], waqawolihimo A_in~aA qatalonaA A@lomasiyHa [ And their saying, Verily we have slain the Messiah ]; (Fr, T;) and qulotu A_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ I said, Verily Zeyd is standing ]; (I' Ak;) and [in the Kur v. 115,] qaAla A@ll~`hu A_in~Y mun~z~iluhaA Ealayokumo [ God said, Verily I will cause it to descend unto you ]; accord. to the dial. of him who does not pronounce it with fet-h: (K:) but when it occurs in explaining what is said, you use ↓ A^an~a ; as in the saying, qado qulotu laka kalaAmFA HasanFA A^an~a A^abaAka $ariyfN waA^an~aka EaAqilN [ I have said to thee a good saying; that thy father is noble and that thou art intelligent ]; (Fr, T;) or when the word signifying “ saying ” is used as meaning “ thinking; ” as in A^ataquwlu A^an~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ Dost thou say that Zeyd is standing? ], meaning A^ataZun~u [ Dost thou think? ]. (I' Ak.) Also, when it occurs in a phrase denotative of state; (I' Ak;) [i. e.,] after the w denotative of state; (K;) as in zurotuhu waA_in~iY *uwA^amalK [ I visited him, I verily having hope, or expectation ]; (I' Ak;) and in jaA='a ziyodN wa A_in~a yadahu EalaY raA^osihi [ Zeyd came, he verily having his hand upon his head ]. (K.) And when it occurs in a phrase which is the predicate of a proper (as opposed to an ideal) substantive; (I' Ak, K; *) as in zayodN A_in~ahu qaAy^imN [ Zeyd, verily he is standing ], (I' Ak,) or *aAhibN [ going away ]; contr. to the assertion of Fr. (K.) And when it occurs before the l which suspends the grammatical government of a verb of the mind, preceding it, with respect to its objective complements; (I' Ak, K; *) as in Ealimotu A_in~a zayodFA laqaAy^imN [ I knew Zeyd verily was standing ]; (I' Ak;) and in [the Kur lxiii. 1,] waA@ll~`hu yaEolamu A_in~aka larasuwluhu [ And God knoweth thou verily art his apostle ]: (K:) but if the l is not in its predicate, you say, ↓ A^an~a ; as in Ealimotu A^an~a zayodFA qaAy^imN [ I knew that Zeyd was standing ]. (I' Ak.) And in the like of the saying in the Kur [ii. 171], waA_in~a A@l~a*iyna A@xotalafuwA fiY A@lokitaAbi lafiY $aqaAqK baEiydK [ And verily they who differ among themselves respecting the book are in an opposition remote from the truth]; because of the l [of inception] which occurs after it, in lafiY : (Ks, A 'Obeyd:) the l of inception which occurs before the predicate of A_in~a should properly commence the sentence; so that A_in~a zayodFA laqaAy^imN [ Verily Zeyd is standing ] should properly be laA_in~a zayodFA qaAy^imN ; but as the l is a corroborative and A_in~a is a corroborative, they dislike putting two particles of the same meaning together, and therefore they put the l later, transferring it to the predicate: Mbr allows its being put before the predicate of ↓ A^an~a ; and thus it occurs in an unusual reading of the saying [in the Kur xxv. 22], A_il~aA A^an~ahumo layaA^okuluwna A@lT~aEaAma [ But they ate food ]; but this is explained by the supposition that the l is here redundant: (I' Ak p. 95:) this is the reading of Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr: others read, A_il~aA A_in~ahumo layaA^okuluna AlT~aEaAma [ but verily they ate food ]: and A_in~a [as well as ↓ A^an~a ] is used after the exceptive A_il~aA when it is not followed by the l [of inception]. (TA.) Also, When it occurs after Hayovu ; as in Aijoliso Hayovu A_in~a zayodFA jaAlisN [ Sit thou where Zeyd is sitting ]. (I' Ak p. 92, and k) And after Hat~aY ; as in mariDa zayodN Hat~aY A_in~ahumo laA yarojuwnahu [ Zeyd has fallen sick, so that verily they have no hope for him : whereas after a particle governing the gen. case, [i. e. a preposition,] you say, ↓ A^an~a . (IHsh in De Sacy's Anthol. Gr. Ar. (I' Ak p. 93.) Also, when occurring in the complement of an oath, if its enunciative is without l : (I' Ak:) [see exs. given above:] or, as some say, only ↓ A^an~a is used in this case. (TA.) (I' Ak pp. 97 and 98.) ― -b7- A_in~a is sometimes contracted into A_inN ; (S, Mughnee, K;) and in this case, it is made to govern and is made to have no government: (S:) it is seldom made to govern in this case; often made to have no government: the Koofees say that it is not contracted; (Mughnee, K;) and that when one says, A_ino zayodN lamunoTaliqN [the meaning is virtually Verily Zeyd is going away, but] A_inN is a negative and the l is syn. with A_il~A ; but this assertion is refuted by the fact that some make it to govern when contracted, as in exs. cited above, voce A_ino , q. v. (Mughnee.) ― -b8- It is also syn. with naEamN [ Even so; yes; yea ]; (Mughnee, K;) contr. to the opinion of AO. (Mughnee.) [See also A^an~a , last sentence.] Those who affirm it to have this meaning cite as an ex. the following verse (Mughnee, K *) of 'Obeyd-Allah Ibn-Keys-er-Rukeiyát: (S, * TA:) ka waqado kabirota faqulotu A_in~aho wayaqulona $ayobN qado EalaA [ And they say, (namely, the women,) Hoariness hath come upon thee, and thou hast become old: and I say, Even so, or yes, or yea ]: (Mughnee, K:) but this has been rebutted by the saying, We do not concede that the h is here added to denote the pause, but assert that it is a pronoun, governed by A_in~a in the accus. case, and the predicate is suppressed; the meaning being, A_in~ahu ka*`lika [ Verily it, i. e. the case, is thus ]. (Mughnee.) [J says,] The meaning is, A_n~ahu qado kaAna kamaA taqulona [ Verily it, i. e. the case, hath been as ye say ]: A 'Obeyd says, This is a curtailment of the speech of the Arabs; the pronoun being deemed sufficient because the meaning is known: and as to the saying of Akh, that it signifies naEamo , he only means thereby that it may be so rendered, not that it is originally applied to that signification: he says that the h is here added to denote the pause. (S.) There is, however, a good ex. of A_in~a in the sense of naEamo in the saying of Ibn-Ez-Zubeyr, to him who said to him, “May God curse a she camel which carried me to thee,” A_in~a waraAkibahaA , i. e. Even so, or yes, or yea; and may God curse her rider: for the suppression of both the subject and the predicate is not allowable. (Mughnee.) And hence, accord. to Mbr, the saying in the Kur [xx. 66], as thus read, A_in~a h`*Ani lasaAHiraAni [meaning, if so, Yes, these two are enchanters ]. (Mughnee.) [But this phrase has given rise to much discussion, related in the Mughnee and other works. The following is a brief abstract of what has been said respecting it by several of the leading authorities.] A booIs-hák says that the people of El-Medeeneh and El-Koofeh read as above, except 'Ásim, who is reported to have read, A_inN h`*aAni , without tesh-deed, and so is Kh; [so too is Hafs, as is said above, voce A_ino ;] and that AA read A_in~a h`*yoni , the former word with teshdeed, and the latter in the accus. case: that the argument for A_in~a h`*aAni , with teshdeed and the nom. case, [or rather what is identical in form with the nom. case,] is, that it is of the dial. of Kináneh, in which the dual is formed by the termination An in the nom. and accus. and gen. cases alike, as also in the dial. of Benu-l-Hárith Ibn-Kaab: but that the old grammarians say that h is here suppressed; the meaning being, A_in~ahu h`*aAni : (T:) this last assertion, however, is weak; for what is applied to the purpose of corroboration should not be suppressed, and the instances of its suppression which have been heard are deviations from general usage, except in the case of A^an~a , with fet-h, contracted into A^ano : (Mughnee:) Aboo-Is-hák then adds, that some say, A_in~a is here syn. with naEamo : this last opinion he holds to be the best; the meaning being, naEamo h`*aAni lahumaA saAHiraAni [ Yes, these two, verily they are two enchanters: for this is not a case in which the l (which is the l of inception) can be regarded as transferred from its proper place, at the commencement of the sentence or proposition, as it is in some instances mentioned in the former half of this paragraph: but it is said in the Mughnee that this explanation is invalidated by the fact that the combining of the corroborative l and the suppression of the inchoative is like the combining of two things inconsistent, or incompatible; as is also the opinion that the l is redundant, because the redundant l prefixed to the enunciative is peculiar to poetry]: next in point of goodness, in the opinion of A booIs-hák, is, that it is of the dial. of Kináneh and Benu-l-Hárith Ibn-Kaab: the reading of AA he does not allow, because it is at variance with the written text: but he approves the reading of 'Ásim and Kh. (T.) -A2- A_in~a also occurs as a verb: it is the third person pl. fem. of the pret. from AlA^ayonu , syn. with Alt~aEabu ; or from A=na syn. with qaruba : or the third person sing. masc. of the pret. passive from AlA^anyinu , in the dial. of those who, for rud~a and Hub~a , say rid~a and Hib~a , likening these verbs to qiyla and biyEa : or the sing. masc. of the imperative from the same: or the pl. fem. of the imperative from AlA^ayonu ; or from A=na syn. with qaruba : or the sing. fem. of the corroborated form of the imperative from waA^aY , syn. with waEada . (Mughnee.) A^anaA , signifying I: see A^ano , in seven places.

definition: , occurring in a trad.
sourceDefinition: , occurring in a trad., (S, Mgh, K, &c., in the first and last in art. mA^n , and in the second in the present art.,) where it is said, A_in~a Tuwla AlS~alaApi waqiSara AlxuTobapi may^in~apN mino fiqohi Alr~ajuli , (S, Mgh, TA, &c.,) is of the measure mafEilapN waqiSara AlxuTobapi may^in~apN mino fiqohi Alr~ajuli , [originally maA^oninapN ,] from A_in~a , (S, Z in the Fáïk, IAth, Mgh, K,) the corroborative particle; (Z, IAth, Mgh;) like maEosaApN from EasaY ; (S, K;) but not regularly derived from A_in~a , because a word may not be so derived from a particle; or it may be said that this is so derived after the particle has been made a noun; (Z, IAth;) or neither of these modes of derivation is regular: (MF:) the meaning is, [ Verily the longness of the prayer and the shortness of the oration from the pulpit are (together)] a proper ground for one's saying, Verily the man is a person of knowledge or intelligence: (Z, * Mgh, K in art. mA^n :) this is the proper signification: accord. to AO, the meaning is, a thing whereby one learns the knowledge, or intelligence, of the man: (Mgh:) or it means a thing suitable to, (S, Mgh,) and whereby one knows, (S,) the knowledge, or intelligence, of the man: (S, Mgh:) or a sign (As, S, K) of the knowledge, or intelligence, of the man; and suitable thereto: (As, S:) or an evidence thereof: (M:) or an indication, or a symptom, thereof; everything that indicates a thing being said to be may^in~apN lahu : [so that may^in~apN lika*aA may be well rendered a thing that occasions one's knowing, or inferring, or suspecting, such a thing; and in like manner, a person that occasions one's doing so: or, more properly, a thing, &c., in which such a thing is usually known to take place, or have place, or be, or exist, like maZin~apN :] one of the strangest of the things said of it is, that the ' is a substitute for the Z of maZin~apN : (IAth:) this seems to have been the opinion of Lh: (Az, L:) accord. to AA, it is syn. with A=yapN [ a sign, &c.]. (TA.) As says (S, * K, TA, all in art. mA^n ) that the word is thus, with teshdeed to the n , in the trad. and in a verse of poetry, as these are related; (S, TA;) but correctly, in his opinion, it should be may^iynapN of the measure faEiylapN , (S, K, * TA,) unless it be from A_in~a , as first stated above: (S, TA:) AZ used to say that it is may^it~apN , with t , (S, K, * TA,) meaning a thing (lit. a place ) meet, fit, or proper, or worthy or deserving, and the like; of the measure mafoEilapN , [originally maA^otitapN ,] from A^at~ahu meaning “he overcame him with an argument or the like:” (S, K, TA:) but some say that it is of the measure faEil~apN , from maA^ana meaning AiHotamala : see art. mA^n . (K in that art.) You say also, huwa may^in~apN liloxayori , from A_in~a , He is a person fit, or proper, for one's saying of him, Verily he is good; and in like manner, maEosaApN , from EasaY , as meaning “a person fit, or proper, for one's saying of him, May-be he will do good.” (A, TA.) And A_in~ahu lamay^in~apN A^ano yakuwna ka*aA Verily it is meet, fit, or proper, for one's saying of it, Verily it is thus; or is worthy, or deserving, of one's saying &c.: or verily it is a thing meet, fit, or proper, for one's saying &c.; or is a thing worthy, or deserving, of one's saying &c.: of the measure mafoEilapN , from A_in~a . (K in the present art.) And A_in~ahu lamay^in~apN A^ano yafoEala *aAka Verily he is meet, fit, or proper, for doing that; or is worthy, or deserving, of doing that: or verily he is a person meet, fit, or proper, for doing that; or is a person worthy, or deserving, of doing that: and in like manner you say of two, and of more, and of a female: but may^in~apN may be of the measure faEil~apN [from mA^n ], i. e. a triliteral-radical word. (M.) ― -b2- You also say, A^ataAhu Ealay may^n~ap *aAka , meaning He came to him at the time, or season, [or fit or proper time, ] of that; and at the first thereof. (M.)

definition: , with the h quiescent, is a word used in chiding, or checking;
sourceDefinition: , with the h quiescent, is a word used in chiding, or checking; meaning Hasobuka [ Sufficient for thee is such a thing; &c.]. (ISd, K.) ― -b2- A_iyhFA signifies, (S, K,) as also Ayha , (K,) a command to be silent, (S, K,) and to abstain; (S, TA;) i. e. Be silent; and abstain, or desist: (TA:) both are used in chiding, or checking: and hiyha is used in the place of A_iyha . (Lth, TA.) You say [also,] A_iyhFA Ean~aA Be silent, and abstain from [ troubling ] us. (S, TA.) And A_iyhaA Ean~iY A@loA=na Abstain thou from [ Troubling ] me now. (AZ, TA.) ― -b3- A_iyhFA also occurs as meaning I hold that to be true, and approve it. (IAth, TA.) -A2- A_iyhi , as also A_iyha and A_iyhK , is a word denoting a desire, or demand, for one to add, or to give, or do, more; (Lth, K;) and a desire for one to speak: (K:) it (i. e. A_iyhi ) is an imperative verbal noun, (S,) indecl., with kesr for its termination: (K:) you say to a man, when you desire, or demand, his telling or saying more of a [certain] story or subject of discourse, or his doing more of a [certain] deed, A_iyhi , with kesr. to the h ; (S;) [i. e. Tell me, or say, more of this; say on; go on, or proceed, with this; or do more of this; ] and A@foEalo A_iyhi [ Go on, or proceed, with this; do it ]; (AZ;) and for A_iyhi , you say, hiyhi : (Lth:) but when you make no interruption after it, you pronounce it with tenween, (ISk, S, K,) and say A_iyhK , (ISk, S,) which means Had~ivonaA [i. e. Tell us, or relate to us, something ]; (Ks, Lh, (ISk, * S; *) and for this one says hiyhK , by substitution of one letter for another: (Ks, Lh:) or it means zido [i. e. tell, or say, or do, something more ]; and haAti [i. e. give, or relate, something ]; (Har p. 592;) and takal~ama [i. e. speak ]. (Idem p. 419.) In the following saying of Dhu-r-Rummeh, waqafonaA wa qulonaA A_iyhi Eano A^um~i saAlimK wa maA baAlu takoliymi Ald~iyaAri AlbalaAqiEi [ We stopped, and we said, Tell us some tidings: inform us ( A^axobiriynaA being app. understood) respecting Umm-Sálim: but what is the case (meaning what is the use) of speaking to the vacant dwellings? ], he has used the word without tenween, though making no interruption after it, because he intended a pause. (ISk, S.) Ibn-Es-Seree says, When you say, A_iyhi yaA rajulu , you only command him to tell you more of the subject of discourse known to you and him, as though you said, haAti AlHadiyva [ Give, or relate, the story, or narrative, O man ]: but if you say, A_iyhK , with tenween, it is as though you said, haAti HadiyvFA m~aA [ Give, or relate, some story or narrative ], because the tenween renders indeterminate: and Dhu-rRummeh meant the tenween, but omitted it through necessity. (S.) As says that Dhu-rRummeh has committed a mistake; the expression of the Arabs being only A_iyhK [in a case of this kind]: ISd says, the truth is, that it is without tenween when determinate, and with tenween when indeterminate; and that Dhu-r-Rummeh asks the ruins to tell him more of a known story, as though he said, Relate to us the story, or tell us the tidings: (TA:) Aboo-Bekr Ibn-Es-Sarráj says, citing this verse, that Ayh is not known in a case of this kind without tenween in any of the dialects; meaning that it is never conjoined with a following word unless it be with tenween. (IB, TA.)

definition: i. q. A^aSolN [The root, basis, or foundation; or the origin, or source; or the most essential part, or very essence; of a thing]. (K.) ― -b2- And [hence, app.,] The inward, or intrinsic, state or...
sourceDefinition: i. q. A^aSolN [The root, basis, or foundation; or the origin, or source; or the most essential part, or very essence; of a thing]. (K.) ― -b2- And [hence, app.,] The inward, or intrinsic, state or circumstances of a case or an affair; as also ↓ bujodapN and ↓ bujudapN : (S, L, K:) or the true, or real, state or circumstances thereof; the positive, or established, truth thereof; from bajada baAlmakaAni . (A.) You say, huwa EaAlimN bibajodapi A^amorika , (S, A, L,) and ↓ bibujodatihi , and ↓ bibujudatihi , (S, L,) He is acquainted with the inward, or intrinsic, state or circumstances of thy case or affair: (S, L:) or, with the true, or real, state or circumstances thereof; with the positive, or established, truth thereof. (A.) And Einodihu bajodapu *`lika , (S, K,) with fet-h, (S,) He possesses the knowledge of that. (S, K.) And hence, (S,) hawa A@bonu bajodatihaA , (S, K,) contr. of hw Abn njodatihaA , (A in art, njd ,) or, as in the books of proverbs, A^anaA A@bonu bajodatihaA , the [affixed] pronoun referring to AlA^aroD [understood], as is said by Meyd and Z, (TA,) applied to [signify He is, or I am, ] the person acquainted with the thing; (S, L, K;) possessing, or exercising, the skill requisite for it; (S, L;) the discriminator, or discerner, thereof; (L;) and one says likewise, huwa A@bonu madiynatihaA waA@bonu bajodatihaA : (TA:) it is also applied to [signify he is, or I am, ] the skilful guide of the way [ thereof ]: (L, K:) and hence, [accord. to some,] it is proverbially applied to any one acquainted with an affair; skilful therein: (TA:) and to [signify he is, or I am, ] the person who will not quit, or depart from, his place; from the saying bajada baAlmakaAni : (L:) or the person who will not depart from his saying: (K: [there explained by the words limano laA yaboraHu mino qawolihi : but the TA supplies some apparent omissions in this explanation, making it to agree with that which here immediately precedes it, taken from the L; and adds that, in some copies of the K, En qwlh is erroneously put for mn qwlh : also, that he who remains in a place knows that place:]) or, accord. to some, bajodapN signifies dust, or earth; so that A^anaA A@bonu bajodatahaA is as though it meant I am created of its dust, or earth. (TA.) ― -b3- Also A [ desert, such as is termed ] SaHoriA=' . (K.) Kaab Ibn-Zuheyr uses the phrase Aibonu bajodatahaA as meaning Its male chameleon; the pronoun referring to a desert ( falaAp ) which he is describing. (TA.) And you say of a land covered with black locusts, A^aSobaHati AlA^aroDu bajodahF waAHidapF [ The land became, or has become, one desert, destitute of vegetable produce ]. (L.)

definition: A certain bird that assumes various colours;
sourceDefinition: A certain bird that assumes various colours; (S;) a small wild bird, like the qanofu* [or hedge-hog, but qunofu* is probably a mistranscription for qunobur , or lark], the upper part of whose feathers is dust-coloured ( A^agobaru , as in the K, accord. to the TA), or white ( A^agar~u , as in some copies of the K), and the middle red, and the lower part black, so that when it is roused, or provoked, it ruffles its feathers and becomes variously changed in colour: (Lth, K:) or a certain bird that is found in the trees called EiDaAh , and the colour of which is between blackness and whiteness, having six qawaAdim [or primary feathers], three on each side, heavy in the rump, that makes a noise with its wings when it flies, and assumes various colours: (IKh:) a certain variegated bird. (TA in art. Abw .) ― -b2- .) ― -b3- [Hence,] huwa A^abuw baraAqi$a (assumed tropical:) He is varying, or variable, in dispositions. (A, TA.)

definition: signifies The coming before or forward, presenting oneself, advancing, confronting, encountering, meeting, or opposing;
sourceDefinition: signifies The coming before or forward, presenting oneself, advancing, confronting, encountering, meeting, or opposing; (KL;) and so ↓ AlAinobiraA='u . (KL, PS.) You say, tbr~Y lahu He presented, addressed, applied, or betook, himself to him, i. e., one man to another man; advanced, came forward, or went forward, to him; or opposed himself to him; syn. taEar~aDa ; as also tbr~Ahu ; and lahu ↓ baraY , aor. : (T:) and lh ↓ AnbrY signifies AiEotaraDa lahu , (S, K, and Har p. 558,) meaning [as above; or] he betook himself, and advanced, or went forward, to it, namely, an action; (Har ubi suprà;) and it presented itself to it, as a thought to the heart, or mind, syn. tEr~D : (Ham p. 541:) lahu ↓ baraY , inf. n. baroYN , is syn. with EaraDa lahu [meaning as above, for it is syn. with taEar~aDa and AiEotaraDa ; or it happened to him, befell him, or occurred to him ]: (M:) and ↓ AnbrY is also syn. with EaraDa [meaning it happened, befell, or occurred ]. sourceDefinition: part. n. of 6. It is said in a trad., AlmutabaAriyaAni laA yujaAbaAni wa laA yuw^okalu TaEaAmuhumaA [ The two persons who vie with each other in the expensiveness of their entertainments shall not have their invitations accepted, nor shall their food be eaten ]. (El-Jámi' es-Sagheer of Es-Suyootee.) The mtbAryAn whose food is forbidden, in a trad., to be eaten, are They who vie with each other in order that each may render the other unable to equal him in respect of the repast prepared by him for his guests: and the doing of this is disliked because of the rivalry and ostentation that are involved in it. (TA.) ― -b2- AlmutabaAriyaAni is also an appellation of The night and the day. (Har p. 377.)

Erf :) [the last of these explanations plainly shows that what is meant thereby is the prepuce of the clitoris; which, it seems, in the Arabian and Egyptian races, and others throughout Eastern Africa, and still more so in the Hottentot race, grows to an extraordinary size; and this may be the reason why the bZr is described by some travellers as a caruncle for which we have no name: or it may, perhaps, be a distinct excrescence from the prepuce of the clitoris: it has been described to me as a caruncle a little in front of the meatus urinarius: many of the Egyptians assert that it is the clitoris itself that is amputated, (as Ludolph also does in his Comment. to his Ethiop. (Msb.) yaA A@bona muqaT~iEapi AlbuZuwri [ O son of her who amputates bZwr !] is an expression of contumely employed by the Arabs whether the mother of the person addressed be really a circumciser of females or not. (TA.)

definition: is an indecl. word with fet-h for its termination, like kayofa , and means daEo [ Let alone, or say nothing of ]; (S;) [i. e.] it is a noun for daEo ; indecl.; (Mughnee, K;) a verbal noun, meaning...
sourceDefinition: is an indecl. word with fet-h for its termination, like kayofa , and means daEo [ Let alone, or say nothing of ]; (S;) [i. e.] it is a noun for daEo ; indecl.; (Mughnee, K;) a verbal noun, meaning daEo and A^utoruko ; (IAth, TA;) and the noun that follows it, when it is thus used, is in the accus. case; (Mughnee, K;) i. e. it is indecl., with fet-h for its termination, when the noun following it is in the accus. case; so that you say, baloha zayodFA [ Let alone Zeyd, or say nothing of Zeyd ]; like as you say, ruwayoda zayodFA : (IB, TA:) and it is also an inf. n. in the sense of Alt~aroku ; likewise with fet-h for its termination, but decl.; and when it is thus used, the noun that follows it is in the gen. case; (Mughnee, K;) or it is put in the place of an inf. n., meaning taroka [which is virtually the same as Autoruko and daEo ], and is prefixed to a noun in the gen. case; so that you say, baloha zayodK , i. e. taroka zayodK [which is virtually the same as baloha zayodFA explained above; for taroka zayodK is originally Autoruko zayodFA tarokFA , like as faDaroba Alr~iqaAbi in the Kur xlvii. 4 is originally fA@DoribuwA Alr~iqaAba DarobFA ]; (IAth, TA;) for in this case it cannot be regarded as a verbal noun, since verbal nouns are not prefixed to other nouns, governed by them in the gen. case: (IB, TA:) and it is also a noun syn. with kayofa [ How? ]; likewise with fet-h for its termination, indecl.; and when it is thus used, the noun that follows it is in the nom. case. (Mughnee, K.) A poet says, describing swords, (S, Mughnee,) namely, Kaab Ibn-Málik, (S,) ta*aru AljamaAjima DaAHiyFA haAmatuhaA baloha AlA^akuf~a kaA^an~ahaA lamo tuxolaqi [ They leave the skulls with their crowns lying open to the sun (let alone, or say nothing of, the hands) as though they had not been created ]: (S, Mughnee:) he says, when they cut, or cut off, the crowns, then let alone, or say nothing of, the hands ( fadaEi AlA^akuf~a ): i. e., they are more fit for cutting off the hands: (TA:) Akh says that blh is here in the place of an inf. n.; that it is as when you say, Daroba zayodK : but AlAkf~ may be in the accus. case; so that the meaning may be daEi AlA^akuf~a : (S:) the verse is thus recited in two different ways: and also baloha AlA^akuf~u [ how then must be the case of the hands? ]. (Mughnee.) And hence the prov., tuHoriquka Aln~aAru A_ino taraAhaA baloha A^ano taSolaAhaA , i. e. The fire will burn thee if thou see it from a distance: then let alone, or say nothing of, ( fadaEo ,) thy entering into it. (TA.) A strange instance occurs in the Saheeh of El-Bukháree, in the explanation of the A=l=m= of the chapter of Als~ajodap [the 32nd ch. of the Kur]: he says, God says [by these three letters], A^aEodadotu liEibaAdiy AlS~aAliHiyna maA laA EayonN raA^ato walaA A^u*unN samiEato wa laA xaTari EalaY qalobi ba$arK *uxorFA mino balohi maA A@T~alaEotumo Ealayohi : (Mughnee, K: *) or mA A^aTalaEotuhumo Ealayohi : (so in some copies of the K:) thus blh is used as a decl. word, governed in the gen. case by mn , and deviating from the three meanings [explained above]: (Mughnee, K:) but the reading commonly known is, ElY qlb b$r baloha ma A^aTolaEotuhumo Elyh ; and this is the reading in the work of J, [the S,] and in the Nh, and other lexicological works: (TA:) it has been explained by gayor ; [so that the meaning of the sentence as first related above is, I have prepared for my righteous servants what eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, nor hath it occurred to the mind of man, as a treasure for the future, (obviously taken from Isaiah lxiv. 4, quoted by St. Paul in 1 Cor. ii. 9,) save, or except, that with which ye have become acquainted, or that with which I have acquainted them; and the same, with the omission of “ as a treasure for the future, “ is the meaning of the sentence as related in the S and Nh &c.;] (Mughnee, K;) i. e. siwaY , as in the S; (TA;) and this corroborates, (Mughnee,) or is agreeable with, (K,) the opinion of those who reckon blh as an exceptive word: (Mughnee, K:) and as meaning A^ajalo [app. a mistranscription for A^ajol ; i. e., it has been explained also as meaning I have done all this because of my promise to them; ( mino A^ajoli maA A^aTolaEotuhumo Ealayohi because of that with which I have acquainted them; ) and thus it may have been read by SM, for he has written Ajl without any syll. signs; and has given no other ex. of blh in the sense here intended except one commencing with the words, baloha An~iY lamo A^axuno EahodFA , which may mean because I have not broken a covenant, or yea, verily I have not &c., accord. as we read A^an~iY or A_in~iY ]: or as meaning kuf~a [or rather kuf~a Eano ] and daEo [ let alone, or say nothing of; but this explanation must relate to the sentence as given in the S and Nh]: (K, but omitted in an excellent copy of that work:) or, accord. to El-Ahmar, it means, in this trad. [as commonly known], kayufa [ how? which seems to be the least suitable of all these explanations]. (TA.) IAmb relates, on the authority of others, that baloha is also syn. with EalaY : [but I think that this is a mistake, arising from a misunderstanding of what here follows:] Fr says that he who makes it to govern a gen. case regards it as used in the manner of EalaY , and similar particles governing the gen. case. (TA.) ― -b2- maA balohaka means maA baAluka [ What is thy state, or condition, or case? ]: (K, TA:) or maA laka [which often has this meaning: see the letter l ]. (So in some copies of the K.)

definition: Heedless: (K:) or heedless of evil (K, TA) by reason of his goodness: (TA:) or simple, foolish, or of little sense, without discrimination: (K:) or weak in intellect: (Msb:) accord.
sourceDefinition: Heedless: (K:) or heedless of evil (K, TA) by reason of his goodness: (TA:) or simple, foolish, or of little sense, without discrimination: (K:) or weak in intellect: (Msb:) accord. to En-Nadr, (TA,) one whose evilness is dead, (K, TA,) so that he is not cognizant of it: (TA:) good in disposition; having little cognizance, or understanding, of subtilties; or having little skill therein: (K:) or one whose predominant quality is freedom of the bosom, or heart, or mind, from evil affections; (S, K, TA;) and good opinion of men: (TA:) simple-hearted: (TK:) naturally disposed to goodness, and therefore heedless of evil, not knowing it: (T, TA:) or heedless with respect to the present world and its people and their corruptness and malevolence, but intelligent and skilled in the law with respect to that which is commanded and that which is forbidden: (Ah- mad Ibn-Hambal, TA:) fem. balohaA='u : (S, Msb, K: *) pl. bulohN : (S, Msb:) and ↓ bulahaA='u , a pl., [as though the sing. were baliyhN ,] signifies dull, stupid, or wanting in intelligence: but this is post-classical. (TA.) Hence, $aAb~N A^abolahu [ A youth, or young man, who is heedless, &c.], because of his inexperience in affairs: the epithet is applied to a youth in like manner as freedom from care, or thought, and like as insanity, are attributed to him. (S.) And xayoru A^awolaAdinaA AlA^abolahu AlEaquwlu (tropical:) [ The best of our children is the heedless, &c., that has much intelligence ]; (S, Msb;) a saying of Ez-Zibrikán Ibn-Bedr; (S;) meaning such as, by reason of his bashfulness, is like the Ablh , (S, Msb,) so that he feigns heedlessness, and passes over things, (Msb,) though he has much intelligence; (S;) or such as is thought to be stupid, but, when examined, is found to be [very] intelligent. (IAth, TA in art. Eql .) And A^akovaru A^aholi Aljan~api Albulohu , a trad., meaning Most of the people of Paradise are the buloh [or heedless, &c.,] with respect to the present world, because of their being little concerned thereby, while they are intelligent with respect to the world to come; (S;) or they are thus termed because they are heedless of their affairs in the present world, and unskilful in the management thereof, and busy themselves with their affairs relating to the world to come. (TA.) ― -b2- balohaA='u , applied to a woman, Generous, strong-hearted, ( maziyrapN , for Almariyrapu in the copies of the K is a mistake for Almaziyrapu , with zAY , TA, [app. here meaning bold, ]) inexperienced in affairs, and simple, or unintelligent. (K, * TA.) ISh cites a poet as applying this epithet to a young girl with whom he had sported, and who acquainted him with her secrets, by reason of her inexperience, and want of cunning, not knowing what that implied against her. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, applied to a she-camel, (tropical:) That does not take fright, and flee from a thing, (ISh, A, K,) by reason of staidness, (ISh, K,) or heaviness, (A,) as though she were stupid. (ISh, A, K.) One does not say jamalN A^abolahu . (ISh, TA.) ― -b4- $abaAbN A^abolahu (tropical:) Soft, or delicate, youth; (T, A, K;) as though he who enjoys it were heedless of nocturnal accidents or calamities. (A, K.) ― -b5- And Eayo$N A^abolahu (tropical:) A soft, or delicate, or pleasant, or plentiful and easy, life: (K, TA:) or a life in which are few anxieties: (CK:) or a life in which are few griefs, or sorrows. (S.) [See also bulahoniyapN .]

sourceDefinition: A skin of a young unweaned camel stuffed (Lth, T, S, M, K) with straw (Lth, T, M, K) or with vumaAm [i. e. panic grass ] (M, K) or with dry herbage, (M,) to which a she-camel is made to incline (Lth, T, S) when her young one has died: (S:) it is brought near to the mother of the young camel [ that has died ], in order that she may incline to it, and yield her milk (M, K) over it. (M.) ― -b2- Also A she-camel's young one. (M, K.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Stupid; foolish; having little sense, or intellect; as also ↓ baw~iY~N ; (IAar, T, K;) applied to a man: (IAar, T:) fem. baw~apN . (K.) ― -b4- And Albaw~u , (K,) or baw~u AlA^avaAfiY , (Lth, T, S, M,) (tropical:) Ashes: (Lth, T, S, M, K:) so called [as being lifeless,] by way of comparison [to the stuffed skin of a young camel]. (M.)

definition: A state, condition, or case;
sourceDefinition: A state, condition, or case; syn. HaAlN (T, S, Msb, K) and $aA^onN : (T:) or a state, condition, or case, for which one cares; wherefore one says, maA baAlayotu bika*aA , inf. n. baAlapN , meaning “ I cared not for such a thing: ” (TA:) or a thing [or things ] for which one cares: (Har p. 94:) and AlbaAlu signifies also baAlu Aln~afosi , i. e. care, or concern; and hence is [said to be] derived baAlayotu , having for its inf. n. baAlapN . (T.) One says, maA baAluka What is thy state, or condition, or case? (S.) [See the Kur xii. 50 and xx. 53: and see an ex. in a verse cited in this Lex. voce A_iyhi .] When it was said to a man, in former times, “ How hast thou entered upon the morning? ” he used to reply, bixayorK A^aSolaHa A@ll~`hu baAlakumo [ With good fortune: may God make good your state, or condition ]. (Ham p. 77.) wa yuSoliHu baAlahumo , in the Kur [xlvii. 6], means And He will make good their state, or condition, in the present world: (I'Ab, T:) or their means of subsistence in the present world, together with their recompense in the world to come. (M.) One says also, huwa raxiY~u AlbaAli He is in ample and easy circumstances (T, Msb) of life; (T;) he is not straitened in circumstances, nor troubled: (T:) or he is in an easy, or a pleasant, state or condition: (TA in art. rxw :) or he is easy, or unstraitened, in mind: (S:) [for] AlbaAlu , (T, M, K,) or raxaA='u AlbaAli , (TA,) signifies ampleness and easiness of life: (T, M, K, TA:) or AlbAl signifies an easy, or unstraitened, state of the mind. (S.) And huwa kaAsifu AlbaAli He is in an evil state or condition: (TA:) or he is straitened in his hope, or expectation: for AlbAl is said to signify hope, or expectation: (T:) so says El-Hawaázinee. (TA.) And layosa h`*aA mino baAliY This is not of the things for which I care. (S.) definition: A kind of long serpent: (S:) a great serpent;
sourceDefinition: A kind of long serpent: (S:) a great serpent; applied to the male and the female: (Msb:) a bulky and long serpent, (Sh, K, TA,) that hunts the rat or mouse, to which latter animal the name is sometimes metaphorically applied, and that is more useful in the house than are cats: (Sh, TA:) or particularly the male [ serpent ], (Ktr, K,) that is yellow, and ruddy: (Ktr:) or the serpent in general, (ISh, K,) male and female, great and small: (ISh:) [also applied to an enormous fabulous serpent; described by Kzw and others:] pl. vaEaAbiynu . (S, Msb.) ― -b2- [ ray^yisu Alv~aEaAbiyni The basilisk. (Golius, from a Glossary.)] ― -b3- damu Alv~uEobaAni : see damN .

definition: [The outlet, or place of outpouring, of the water of a watering-trough &c.
sourceDefinition: [The outlet, or place of outpouring, of the water of a watering-trough &c.;] the place of passage for the water, in the side of a wateringtrough or tank: and a channel, or conduit, for water: (KL:) pl. mavaAEibu . (S, A.) You say mavoEabu AlHawpa [ The outlet for the water of the watering-trough or tank ]: (S, A:) and mavoEabu Als~aToHi [ the outlet for the water of the house-top ]: (A:) and mavoEabu AlmaTari [ the outlet, or channel, for the rain-water ]: (TA:) from vaEaba AlmaA='a “he gave vent to the water,” or, “made it to flow forth,” &c. (A, TA.) And mavaAEibu Almadiynapi , meaning The channels, or places of flowing, of the water of the city: (K, TA:) whence it appears that MF has erred in saying that mavoEabN signifies [only] a mizoraAb [or spout for conveying away water from a housetop &c.]: not a channel, or place of flowing. (TA.) [See also SunobuwrN , and lawolabo .]

definition: Steeped, or macerated, poison;

(TA.) ― -b3- See also vamaAlapN .

sourceDefinition: sing. of jawaAriHu . (Mgh, L, Msb, TA.) ― -b2- The latter signifies (tropical:) Beasts, and birds, of prey; or that catch game; (S, A, * Mgh, L, Msb, K:) thus the falcon is a jArHp , and so is the dog trained for hunting, because it gains for its owner: (L:) and this appellation is applied alike to the male and the female, like raAHilapN and raAwiyapN . (Msb.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) The members, or limbs, of a man, with which things are gained or earned; (S, K, TA;) or with which one works; (A;) as the hands or arms, and the feet or legs: (S, A, K, TA:) because they gain, or earn, or do, good and evil. (TA.) ― -b4- [And (tropical:) The organs of the body: thus, for instance, jArHp is applied (in the Msb, art. bSr ,) to the eye, which is termed (in the TA in that art.) the seeing jArHp ( AljaAriHapu Aln~aAZirapu ).] ― -b5- Also (assumed tropical:) Mares: [and the like: ] because they bring gain to their owners by their breeding. (AA, T.) You say, maA lahu jaAriHapN (assumed tropical:) He possesses not a female beast that bears young: he possesses not that which makes gain. (TA.) And h`*ihi Aln~aAqapu mino jawaAriHi AlmaAli , and h*h AlA^ataAnu , (K,) and h*h Alfarasu , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) This she-camel, and this she-ass, and this mare, is young, unimpaired by age ( muqobilapN [i. q. muqotabalapN ]) in the womb, (K, TA,) and in youthful vigour, and one of which the offspring is wished for. (TA.)

definition: , aor (Msb, K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , aor (Msb, K,) inf. n. jazaA='N , (Msb,) It (a thing) paid; gave, or rendered, as a satisfaction; or made, gave, or rendered, satisfaction: (Msb:) or satisfied; sufficed; or contented. (K.) And jazayotu Ald~ayona I paid the debt. (Msb.) And jazayotu fulaAnFA Haq~ahu I paid such a one his right, or due. (TA.) And maA yajoziyniY h`*aA Alv~awobu This garment does not suffice me. (TA.)― -b2- And hence, (TA,) jazaY Eanohu , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) [aor. and] inf. n. as above, (Mgh,) It (a thing) paid for him; gave, or rendered, [a thing] as a satisfaction for him; made, gave, or rendered, satisfaction for him; (S, Mgh, Msb,* K;) and some of the lawyers use ↓ AjzY in this sense, like AjzA^ : (Az, Mgh, Msb:) jazaY is of the dial. of El-Hijáz, and AjzA^ of the dial. of Temeem. (Akh, Msb.) Hence, in the Kur [ii. 45], laA tajoziY nafosN Eano nafosK $ayoy^FA [ A soul shall not give anything as a satisfaction for a soul, i. e. for another soul: or a soul shall not make satisfaction for a soul at all; accord. to the latter rendering, $yy^A being put in the accus. case after the manner of an inf. n.]. (S, Msb.) You say also, jazato Eanoka $aApN A sheep, or goat, made satisfaction for thee [as a sacrifice]; (S, TA;) as also ↓ A^ajozato : (TA:) Benoo-Temeem say A^ajozaA^ato , with ' : (S, TA:) this last, thus explained, is a dial, var. mentioned by IKtt (Msb.) And ka*aA Eano ka*aA ↓ AjzY Such a thing stood, or served, in lieu, in the place, or in stead, of such a thing, without sufficing. (Zj, K.) And qaliylN mino kaviyrK ↓ yujoziY ; and h`*aAmino h`*aA ; A little stands, or serves, in lieu of much; and this, of this. (IAar, TA.) And Eanohu mujozaY ↓ AjzY fulaAnK and mujozaApa fulaAnK and (as though the augmentative letter [ A in AjzY ] were imagined to be rejected, TA) majozaY flAn and majozaApa flAn He satisfied, sufficed, or contented, him as such a one; he stood, or served, him in stead of such a one; a dial. var. of AjzA^ . (K.) And ↓ AjzY mujozaY gayorihi It (a thing) satisfied, sufficed, or contented, as another thing; it stood, or served, in stead of another thing. (Msb.) And ↓ AjzAka , with the [second] objective complement suppressed, It was sufficient for thee. (Mgh.) ― -b3- jazaAha ka*aA (Msb,* TA,) and jazaAhu bihi (K,) or bimaA SanaEa , (S,) and Ealayohi , (K,) [aor. and] inf. n. as above, (S, K,) He repaid, requited, compensated, or recompensed, him (Msb, K TA) [ for such a thing, for it, or for what he had done ]; as also ↓ jAzAhu , (S, K,) inf. n. mujaAzaApN and jizaA='N : (K:) or, accord. to Fr, [contr. to many instances in the Kur,] the former verb relates only to good; and the latter, to good and to evil: but accord. to others, the former may relate to good and to evil; and the latter, to evil. (TA.) [See also jazaA='N , below.] One says, in praying for another, jazaAhu A@ll~`hu xayorFA May God repay him good: and requite, or recompense, him for good [that he has done]. (Msb.) And bi*anobihi ↓ jaAzayotuhu I punished him for his crime, or sin, or act of disobedience. (Msb.) And jazaY Eanohu fulaAnFA He requited, compensated, or recompensed, for him, such a one. (TA.)― -b4- jaAzayotuhu fajazayotuhu : see 3.

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. jaEolN (S, Msb, K) and juEolN and jaEaAlapN and jiEaAlapN (K) and majoEalN , (S, TA,) He made a thing; syn. SanaEa ; (Msb, K;) but having a more general signification than faEala and SanaEa and their equivalents [as will be shown by what follows]; (Er-Rághib, TA;) and so ↓ AjtEl : (K:) both these verbs signify the same. (S.) ― -b2- He made a thing of, or from, a thing; as in the saying [in the Kur xvi. 74 and xlii. 9], jaEala lakumo mino A^anofusikumo A^azowaAjFA [ He hath made for you, of, or from, yourselves, wives ]; and [in the Kur xvi. 83] wajaEala lakumo mina AljibaAli A^akonaAnFA [ And He hath made for you, of the mountains, places of retreat; as caves, and excavated houses or chambers: so explained by Bd]. (TA.) ― -b3- He created; (K, TA;) brought into being, or existence; (TA;) as in the saying [in the Kur vi. 1], waJaEala AlZ~ulumaAti waAln~uwri [ And hath created, or brought into being, the darknesses and the light ]; (K, TA;) and [in the Kur xxi. 31] wajaEalonaA mina AlmaA='i kul~a $aYo'K HaY~K [ And We have created of water, or the seminal fluid, everything living ]; and [in the Kur xvi. 80, &c.,] wajaEala lakumu Als~amoEa wa AlA^aboSaAra waAlA^afoy^idapa [ And He created for you the ears and the eyes and the hearts ]. (TA.) ― -b4- He made, or prepared; as in the saying [in the Kur lxv. 2], yajoEalu lahu maxorajFA [ He will make, or prepare, for him a way of escape, or safety ]; and [in the Kur lxv. 4] yajoEalu lahu mino A^amorihi yusorFA [ He will make, or prepare, for him an easy state of his circumstances; i. e., will make his circumstances, or case, easy to him ]. (TA.) ― -b5- He made; meaning he made to be, or become; he constituted; he appointed; [in which sense it is doubly trans.;] (S, K;) as in the saying in the Kur [xix. 31], wajaEaloniY nabiy~FA [ And He hath made me a prophet ]; (S;) [and in the elliptical phrase, jaEalahu Ealayohi He made him to be superintendant, or the like, over it; set him, or appointed him, over it: ] and in the phrase, jaEala AlqabiyHa HasanFA [ He made that which was bad to be, or become, good ]. (K.) ― -b6- He made a thing to be in a particular state or condition; as in the saying [in the Kur ii. 20], Al~a*i jaEala lakumu AlA^aroDa firaA$FA [ Who hath made for you the earth to be as a bed ]; and [in the Kur lxxi. 15] wajaEala Alqamara fiyhin~a nuwrFA [ And hath made the moon, in them (the heavens), to be as a light ]; and so, as some say, in the saying [in the Kur xliii. 2], A_in~aA jaEalonaAhu quroA=nFA Earabiy~FA [ Verily we have made it an Arabic Kur-án ]. (TA.) ― -b7- [ He made a thing to be in an altered, or changed, state or condition; i. e.,] the verb signifies also the changing a thing from its state or condition; as in the saying [in the Kur xi. 84 and xv. 74], jaEalonaA EaAliyahaA saAfilahaA [ We made their upper part to be their lower part ]; (K;) and in the words of the Kur [lvi. 81], watajoEaluwna rizoqakumo A^an~akumo tuka*~ibuwna [ And do ye make the thanks that ye should render for your sustenance to be that ye charge with falsehood the Giver thereof by attributing it to the stars called A^anowaA=' as expl. by Bd and Jel]. (TA.) ― -b8- He pronounced (Er-Rághib, K) a thing by a true judgment or decision, (Er-Rághib,) or as a legal ordinance; (K;) as in the saying (of the Legislator, TA), jaEala A@ll~`hu AlS~alawaAti AlmaforuwDaAti xamosFA [ God hath pronounced the prayers that are made obligatory to be five ] (K.) And He pronounce (Er-Rághib, K *) a thing by a false judgment or decision, (Er-Rághib,) or according to his own judgment, heretically; (K;) as in the saying [in the Kur xv. 91], Al~a*iyna jaEaluwA AlquroA=na EiDiyna [ Who pronounced the Kur-án to be lies, or enchantment, &c.]. definition: and janaAzapN signify the same, (Mgh, Msb, K,) namely, A dead person;
sourceDefinition: and janaAzapN signify the same, (Mgh, Msb, K,) namely, A dead person; a corpse: (K:) but the former is the more chaste: (Msb:) or the former signifies the dead person; and the latter, the bier: (As, IAar, Msb, K:) or the former, the bier; and the latter, the dead person: (Mgh, Msb, K:) so accord. to Th, as related by Aboo-'Amr Ez-Záhid: (Msb:) or the former is said by the vulgar to mean the bier: (As, TA:) or the former signifies the bier with the dead person: (K:) or the dead person upon the bier: (S:) and the bier is not so called unless the dead person is upon it: (AAF:) when the dead person is not upon it, it is called sariyrN and naEo$N : (AAF, S:) but the vulgar say janaAzapN , with fet-h; (S;) which is not allowable: (Lth, As, Mgh, TA:) or janaAzapN [so in the TA] signifies the man: or the bier with the man: (En-Nadr, TA:) jnAzp is derived from janazahu , in the first of the senses assigned to it above: (A, Msb, TA:) so some assert: (IDrd, TA:) but ISd says, I know not whether this be correct: (TA:) or a janaAzap is so called because the clothes are gathered together when the man is upon the bier: ('Abd-Allah Ibn-El-Hasan, TA:) some say that it is Nabathean: (TA:) the pl. is janaAy^izu . (S.) The Arabs say, tarakotuhu jinaAzapF I left him a corpse, or dead. (As, TA.) And Duriba Alr~ajulu Hat~aY turika janaAzapF [so in the TA, The man was beaten until he was left a corpse ]. (ISh, TA.) And rumiYa fiY jinaAzatihi , meaning, He died: (Lth, Mgh:) or he has been carried, or lifted, and put [ into his bier ]: this they say when they give information of the death of a man: (TA:) and they say also, TuEina fiY jinaAzatihi , meaning the same. (Lth, Mgh, TA.) ― -b2- Also jinaAzapN [or janaAzapN ] (tropical:) A wine-skin [ when emptied; as though it were a body without a soul]. (K.) A certain impudent man of the Arabs, 'Amr Ibn- Ki'ás, says, wakunotu A_i*aA A^araY ziq~FA SariyEFA yunaAHu EalaY janaAzatihi bakayotu [ And I used, when I saw a wine-skin laid prostrate, its corpse being wailed over, to weep, or accord. to Th, as is said in the TA in art. bkY , to sing ]. (TA.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) Anything oppressive and grievous, EalaY qawomK to a people. (Lth, K.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A sick person. (Sgh, K.)
