definition: , (S, A, L, &c.,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. jahodN , (TA,) He strove, laboured, or toiled; exerted himself or his power or efforts or endeavours or ability; employed himself vigorously, strenuously,...
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, L, &c.,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. jahodN , (TA,) He strove, laboured, or toiled; exerted himself or his power or efforts or endeavours or ability; employed himself vigorously, strenuously, laboriously, diligently, studiously, sedulously, earnestly, or with energy; was diligent, or studious; took pains, or extraordinary pains; (S, A, L, K;) fiY ka*aA in such a thing; (S;) or fiY AlA^amori in the affair; (A;) as also ↓ Ajthd ; (A, K;) and so ↓ jAhd , with respect to speech and actions: (L:) or jahada fiY AlA^amori , aor. and inf. n. as above, he did his utmost, or used his utmost power or efforts or endeavours or ability, in prosecuting the affair: (Msb:) and ↓ Ajthd and ↓ tjAhd he exerted unsparingly his power, or ability: (S, A, K:) or fiY AlA^amori ↓ Ajthd he exerted unsparingly his power, or ability, in the prosecution of the affair, so as to effect his utmost. (Msb.) You say also, Aijohado jahadaka fiY h*aA AlA^amori (tropical:) Do thine utmost in this affair: (Fr, S, K: *) but not juhodaka . (Fr, S.) And raA^oyahu ↓ Ajthd (tropical:) He took pains, or put himself to trouble or fatigue, to form a right judgment or opinion. (MA.) And raA^oyiY wanafosiY Hat~aY ↓ Aijotahadotu balagotu majohuwdiY (assumed tropical:) I exerted my judgment and my mind so that I attained the utmost of my power, or ability. (T, L.) ― -b2- jahadabihi He tried, proved, or examined, him, (L, K,) Eani Alxayori wa gayorihi [ respecting good qualities, &c.]. (L.) -A2- jahadahu , (Mgh, L, Msb,) aor. , (Mgh, L,) inf. n. jahodN , (L, Msb,) It, (an affair, and a disease,) and he, (a man,) affected him severely; harassed, embarrassed, distressed, afflicted, troubled, inconvenienced, fatigued, or wearied, him: (Msb:) it (disease, L and K, and fatigue, and love, L) rendered him lean; emaciated him: (L, K:) he burdened him beyond his power; imposed upon him that which was beyond his power; as also ↓ Ajhdhu : (Mgh:) and, [as also ↓ Ajhdhu ,] he importuned him, harassed him, or plied him hard, in asking, begging, or petitioning. (A.) [Hence,] juhida , said of a man, He was severely affected, harassed, embarrassed, distressed, afflicted, troubled, inconvenienced, fatigued, or wearied: (S, L:) or was grieved, or made sorry or unhappy. (L.) And A^aSaAbahumo quHuwTN mina AlmaTari fajuhiduwA jahodFA $adiydFA Drought befell them, and they consequently became severely distressed. (S.) And juhiduwA They were, or became, afflicted with drought, barrenness, or dearth; or with drought, and dryness of the earth. (L.) And rajulN yajohadu A^ano yaHomila silaAHahu mina AlD~aEofi , for yajohadu nafosahu , A man who imposes upon himself a difficulty, or trouble, or fatigue, or a difficult or severe task, or who strains, or strains himself, in the carrying of his weapons, or arms, by reason of weakness. (Mgh.) And jahada daAb~atahu and ↓ AjhdhA He jaded, harassed, distressed, fatigued, or wearied, his beast; i. q. ↓ balaga jahodahaA : (K:) or he tasked, or plied, his beast beyond his power in journeying, or marching, or in respect of pace. (S, Msb.) And A^ajohadotuhu EalaY A^ano yafoEala ka*aA wa ka*aA [ I importuned him, or harassed him, to do such and such things ]. (L.) ― -b2- Also, (S, Msb,) aor. as above, (A,) and so the inf. n., (Msb,) (tropical:) He deprived it (namely, milk,) of its butter, (S, A, K,) entirely: (S, K:) or churned it so as to extract its butter and render it sweet and pleasant: or mixed it with water: (Msb:) or diluted it so that it consisted for the most part of water: and in like manner it is used in relation to broth. (A.) ― -b3- Hence, (Msb,) jahadahaA (assumed tropical:) He lay with her; or compressed her: (L, Msb, from a trad.:) or i. q. dafaEahaA , and HafazahaA [which has a similar meaning]. (L.) ― -b4- jahada AlT~aEaAmi (assumed tropical:) He desired the food eagerly; longed for it; (S, K;) as also ↓ Ajhdhu . (K.) And juhida AlT~aEaAmu and ↓ A^ujohida (assumed tropical:) The food was eagerly desired, or longed for. (S.) ― -b5- Also (tropical:) He ate much of the food: (S, K:) he left nothing of it. (A.) You say also, h`*aA kalaA^N yajohaduhu AlmaAlu (assumed tropical:) This is herbage, or pasture, of which the cattle eat perseveringly. (AA, TA.) -A3- jahida It (a state of life) was, or became, hard, difficult, strait, or distressful. (S, K.)

(Msb.) You say also, Aijohado jahadaka fiY h*aA AlA^amori (tropical:) Do thine utmost in this affair: (Fr, S, K: *) but not juhodaka . (Fr, S.) And raA^oyahu ↓ Ajthd (tropical:) He took pains, or put himself to trouble or fatigue, to form a right judgment or opinion. (MA.) And raA^oyiY wanafosiY Hat~aY ↓ Aijotahadotu balagotu majohuwdiY (assumed tropical:) I exerted my judgment and my mind so that I attained the utmost of my power, or ability. (T, L.) ― -b2- jahadabihi He tried, proved, or examined, him, (L, K,) Eani Alxayori wa gayorihi [ respecting good qualities, &c.]. (L.) -A2- jahadahu , (Mgh, L, Msb,) aor. , (Mgh, L,) inf. n. jahodN , (L, Msb,) It, (an affair, and a disease,) and he, (a man,) affected him severely; harassed, embarrassed, distressed, afflicted, troubled, inconvenienced, fatigued, or wearied, him: (Msb:) it (disease, L and K, and fatigue, and love, L) rendered him lean; emaciated him: (L, K:) he burdened him beyond his power; imposed upon him that which was beyond his power; as also ↓ Ajhdhu : (Mgh:) and, [as also ↓ Ajhdhu ,] he importuned him, harassed him, or plied him hard, in asking, begging, or petitioning. (A.) [Hence,] juhida , said of a man, He was severely affected, harassed, embarrassed, distressed, afflicted, troubled, inconvenienced, fatigued, or wearied: (S, L:) or was grieved, or made sorry or unhappy. (L.) And A^aSaAbahumo quHuwTN mina AlmaTari fajuhiduwA jahodFA $adiydFA Drought befell them, and they consequently became severely distressed. (S.) And juhiduwA They were, or became, afflicted with drought, barrenness, or dearth; or with drought, and dryness of the earth. (L.) And rajulN yajohadu A^ano yaHomila silaAHahu mina AlD~aEofi , for yajohadu nafosahu , A man who imposes upon himself a difficulty, or trouble, or fatigue, or a difficult or severe task, or who strains, or strains himself, in the carrying of his weapons, or arms, by reason of weakness. (Mgh.) And jahada daAb~atahu and ↓ AjhdhA He jaded, harassed, distressed, fatigued, or wearied, his beast; i. q. ↓ balaga jahodahaA : (K:) or he tasked, or plied, his beast beyond his power in journeying, or marching, or in respect of pace. (S, Msb.) And A^ajohadotuhu EalaY A^ano yafoEala ka*aA wa ka*aA [ I importuned him, or harassed him, to do such and such things ]. (L.) ― -b2- Also, (S, Msb,) aor. as above, (A,) and so the inf. n., (Msb,) (tropical:) He deprived it (namely, milk,) of its butter, (S, A, K,) entirely: (S, K:) or churned it so as to extract its butter and render it sweet and pleasant: or mixed it with water: (Msb:) or diluted it so that it consisted for the most part of water: and in like manner it is used in relation to broth. (A.) ― -b3- Hence, (Msb,) jahadahaA (assumed tropical:) He lay with her; or compressed her: (L, Msb, from a trad.:) or i. q. dafaEahaA , and HafazahaA [which has a similar meaning]. (L.) ― -b4- jahada AlT~aEaAmi (assumed tropical:) He desired the food eagerly; longed for it; (S, K;) as also ↓ Ajhdhu . (K.) And juhida AlT~aEaAmu and ↓ A^ujohida (assumed tropical:) The food was eagerly desired, or longed for. (S.) ― -b5- Also (tropical:) He ate much of the food: (S, K:) he left nothing of it. (A.) definition: , inf. n. of jAhd , properly signifies The using, or exerting, one's utmost power, efforts, endeavours, or ability, in contending with an object of disapprobation; and this is of three kinds, namely,...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. of jAhd , properly signifies The using, or exerting, one's utmost power, efforts, endeavours, or ability, in contending with an object of disapprobation; and this is of three kinds, namely, a visible enemy, the devil, and one's self; all of which are included in the term as used in the Kur xxii. 77. (Er-Rághib, TA.) See also 1, first sentence. You say, jAhd AlEaduw~a , (JK, A, Mgh,) inf. n. as above (JK, Mgh, K) and mujaAhadapN , (JK, K,) He fought with the enemy: (K:) or he encountered the enemy, imposing upon himself difficulty or distress or fatigue, or exerting his power or efforts or endeavours or ability, [or the utmost thereof, ] to repel him, his enemy doing the like: and hence jAhd came to be used by the Muslims to signify generally he fought, warred, or waged war, against unbelievers and the like. (Mgh.) You say also, jAhd fiY sabiyli A@ll~`hi , inf. n. jihaAdN (S, Msb) and mujaAhadapN , (S,) [ He fought, &c., in the way of God; i. e., in the cause of religion. ]

(JK.) ― -b3- A^ujohida He was thrown into a state of difficulty, distress, affliction, trouble, inconvenience, or fatigue. (L.) ― -b4- Ajhd maAlahu He consumed, or wasted, and dispersed, his property: (K:) or gave it away, and dispersed it, altogether, here and there. (En-Nadr, TA.) -A2- As intrans., He (an enemy) strove, laboured, or exerted himself, in enmity, (K, TA,) EalayonaA against us. (TA.) ― -b2- He acted with energy, or with the utmost energy: so in the phrases saAra faA^ajohada He marched, or journeyed, and did so with energy, or with the utmost energy; and Halafa biA@ll~`hi faA^ajohada He swore by God, and did so with energy, &c.: in which cases one should not say fajahada . (Aboo-' Amr Ibn-El-'Alà, L.) ― -b3- He took the course prescribed by prudence, precaution, and sound judgment, fiY AlA^amori in the affair; syn. AiHotaATa . (L, K.) ― -b4- He became in a state of difficulty, embarrassment, distress, affliction, trouble, inconvenience, or fatigue. (L.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) It (a thing) became mixed, or confused. (K.) -A3- He entered upon land such as is termed jahaAd : he went forth into the desert; and into the plain, or open country. (JK.) ― -b2- It rose up; rose into view; appeared. (JK.) You say, Ajhd liYa Alqawomu The people, or company of men, came within my sight, or view; syn. A^a$orafuwA . (AA, K.) And Ajhd fiyhi Al$~ayobu Hoariness appeared upon him, and became much: (TA:) or (tropical:) became much, and spread: (A:) or became much, and was quick in its progress, (K, TA,) and spread. (TA.) And A^ajohadato lahu AlA^aroDu The land became open to him. (L, K. *) And in like manner, Ajhd lh AlT~ariyqu , (L,) and AlHaq~u , (L, K, *) The road, and (assumed tropical:) the truth, became open, apparent, and manifest, to him. (L, K. *) And Ajhd laka AlA^amoru (assumed tropical:) The thing became, or has become, within thy power, or reach; (Aboo-Sa'eed, K;) and offered, or presented, itself to thee. (Aboo-Sa'eed, TA.)

definition: Power; ability; as also ↓ juhodN ; (S, A, IAth, L, Msb, K;) the latter of the dial. of El- Hijáz, and the former of other dials.; (Msb;) and ↓ majohuwdN : (A:) jhd in the Kur ix. 80 is read both...
sourceDefinition: Power; ability; as also ↓ juhodN ; (S, A, IAth, L, Msb, K;) the latter of the dial. of El- Hijáz, and the former of other dials.; (Msb;) and ↓ majohuwdN : (A:) jhd in the Kur ix. 80 is read both jahod and ↓ juhd : (S:) and jahodN signifies also labour, toil, exertion, effort, endeavour, energy, diligence, painstaking, or extraordinary painstaking: (L: [see jahada :]) or ↓ juhodN has the signification first mentioned above, (Fr, S, IAth, Msb,) and jahodN , with fet-h, is from Aijohado jahodaka fiY h`*aA AlA^amori , (Fr, S,) or from jahada fiY AlA^amori , being an inf. n. from this verb, (Msb,) and signifies, [as also ↓ majohuwdN ,] one's utmost; the utmost of one's power or ability or efforts or endeavours or energy. (Fr, S, IAth, Msb, K.) You say, ba*ala Aljahoda , (Msb in art. blg , &c.,) and ↓ Almajohuwda , (S, A,) or jahodahu , (Mgh,) [and ↓ majohuwdahu ,] He exerted unsparingly his power or ability: (Mgh:) [or his utmost power or ability or efforts or endeavours or energy; as shown above.] And balaga jahodahu , (A, L,) and ↓ majohuwdahu , (A,) He accomplished the utmost of his power or ability; did his utmost. (A, L. [Like jahada jahodahu . See also balaga jahoda daAb~atihi , below.]) And ↓ juhayodaY is syn. with jahodN ; (K;) as in the saying, laA^abolugan~a juhayodaAYa fiY AlA^amori (JK, TK,) i. e. I will assuredly accomplish the utmost of my power, or ability, in the affair. (TK. [In a copy of the A, juhayodaAka ; and so in the TA, I believe from that same copy.]) [So, too, is ↓ juhaAdaY ; as in the saying,] juhaAdaAka A^ano tafoEala The utmost of thy power, or ability, and the utmost of thy case, is, or will be, thy doing [such a thing]; syn. quSaAraAka [q. v.], (JK, K,) and gaAyapu A^amorika . (TA.) Al~a*iyna A^aqosamuwA biA@ll~`hi jahoda A^ayomaAnihimo , in the Kur [v. 58, &c.], means Who swore by God with the most energetic of their oaths: (K, * Jel:) or the strongest, or most forcible, of their oaths; jhd being originally an inf. n., and in the accus. as a denotative of state with yajohaduwna understood before it, or as an inf. n. (Bd.) ― -b2- Also Difficulty, or grievousness; embarrassment, distress, affliction, trouble, inconvenience, fatigue, or weariness; (S, A, IAth, Mgh, Msb, K;) so accord. to some who say that ↓ juhodN , with damm, has the first of the significations assigned to it above; (Msb;) as also ↓ majohuwdN : (Mgh:) a disease, or difficulty, that distresses or afflicts, a man; as also ↓ juhodN . (JK.) Hence, jahodu AlbalaA='i , (Msb,) i. e. A state of difficulty, or trouble, to which death is preferred: or largeness of one's family, or household, combined with poverty. (L, K. *) [Hence also,] balaga jahoda daAb~atihi , [i. e. balaga ma$aq~atahaA ,] i. q. jahadahaA : see 1. (K.) ― -b3- Also Small provision, upon which a man possessing little property can live (JK, L) with difficulty. (L.) And jahodN Almuqil~i What a man who possesses little property can afford to give in payment of the poor-rate required by the law. (L, from a trad.)

definition: He disliked residing in it, namely, a country, or town, even if in the enjoyment of ease and plenty: (S:) or he disliked it, (K, TA,) and found it to disagree with him;
sourceDefinition: He disliked residing in it, namely, a country, or town, even if in the enjoyment of ease and plenty: (S:) or he disliked it, (K, TA,) and found it to disagree with him; (TA;) as also ↓ jawiyahu : (K, TA:) or he disliked it, namely, a city, and found it to be insalubrious: or, as AZ says, he disliked it, namely, a country, even if it agreed with him in respect of his body: and he says, in his Nawádir, that AijotiwaA='N signifies the yearning towards, or longing for, home, and disliking a place, even if in the enjoyment of ease and plenty: and disliking it without yearning towards, or longing for, home: and also the not finding the food nor the beverage in a land to be wholesome: but not when one likes the residing in it but its food and beverage do not agree with him. (TA.) -A2- And AjtwY His heart was burnt by the fire of enmity. (Ham p. 219.)

HuduwvN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and HadaAvapN , (A, K,) It was new, or recent; contr. of qaduma : (S, * A, K:) it (a thing) came into existence; began to be; had a beginning; began, or originated; existed newly, for the first time, not having been before: (S, Mgh, Msb, TA:) but when mentioned with qaduma , it is written Haduva , with damm to the d , (S, Mgh, K,) as in the saying, A^axa*aniY maA qaduma wamaAHaduva , (S,) or A^axa*ahu Alx , (A, Mgh,) meaning Old and new anxieties and thoughts [ came into my mind, or his mind, or overcame me, or him ]; (TA;) or old and new griefs or sorrows; (Mgh;) the former saying occurring in a trad.: (TA:) the verb is not thus in any other case [in this sense]. (S.) You say, Hadava bihi EayobN A vice, or fault, or the like, originated in him, or it, not having been before. (Msb.) And Hadava A^amorN An affair, or event, originated: (Mgh:) or happened, or came to pass. (S.) HuduwvN is of two kinds: HuduwvN zamaAniY~N , which is A thing's being preceded by non-existence: and HuduwvN *aAtiY~N , which is a thing's being dependent upon another for its existence. (KT.) ― -b2- HadaAvapN and HuduwvapN , [as inf. ns. of which the verb, if they have one, is, accord. to analogy, Haduva ,] relating to a man, signify The being young; or [as simple substs.] youthfulness. (ISd, K.)

(TA.)

definition: A novelty, or new thing;
sourceDefinition: A novelty, or new thing; an innovation; a thing not known before: and particularly relating to El-Islám [i. e. to matters of religious doctrine or practice or the like ]: (Mgh:) [and so ↓ A^amorN muHodavN ; for] muHodavaAtu AlA^umuwri (pl. of muHodavN , TA) signifies innovations of people of erroneous opinions, (Msb, TA,) inconsistent with the doctrines, or practices, of the just of preceding times: or what is not known in revealed scripture, nor in the Sunneh, nor in the general conventional tenets of the doctors of the law: and HadavN , [in like manner,] an innovation that is disapproved, not agreeable with custom, or usage, and not known in the Sunneh. (TA.) ↓ A=waY muHodavFA , occurring in a trad., means He entertained an innovation; [i. e. he embraced, or held, it; ] or he was content, or pleased, with it; or he bore it patiently: or, as some say, it is ↓ A=waY muHodivFA , meaning he entertained, or harboured in his dwelling, a criminal, or an offender, and protected him from retaliation. (TA.) ― -b2- Also i. q. ↓ HaAdivapN and ↓ HadavaAnN [in some copies of the S ↓ HidovaAn ] and ↓ HudovaY [signifying An accident, an event, a hap, or a casualty: and generally an evil accident or event, a mishap, a misfortune, a disaster, a calamity, or an affliction ]: (S:) [the most common of these words is ↓ HaAdivapN ; and its pl., HawaAdivu , is more common than the sing.:] the pl. of HadavN is A^aHodaAvN . (TA.) A^aHodaAvu Ald~ahori and ↓ HawaAdivuhu (A, K) and ↓ HidovaAnuhu , (K,) or, as is said by Fr and others, this last is ↓ HadavaAnuhu , (TA,) signify The accidents, or casualties, of time or fortune; or the evil accidents, or calamities, of time or fortune. (A, K.) ↓ HawaAdivu occurs used as a sing., said to be put by poetic license for ↓ HadavaAnN : and this latter is also used [as a pl.] for HawaAdivu : so say Az and AAF: and it is said to be a noun in the sense of HawaAdivu Ald~ahori and nawaAy^ibu Ald~ahori : accord. to Fr, the Arabs say, [using it as a pl.,] A^aholakatonaA AlHadavaAnu [ The accidents, or evil accidents, of time, or fortune, destroyed us ]: some say AlHadavaAni , making it dual of HadavN , and meaning thereby the night and day; like as they say [in the same sense] AljadiydaAni and AlmalawaAni &c. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence] HadavN is a term applied by Sb to The maSodar [or infinitive noun ]; because all mSAdir are [significant of] accidents [considered as subsisting in, or proceding from, agents]: and the pl. which he assigns to it in this sense is A^aHodaAvN . (TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) The voiding of ordure; or the breaking of wind; syn. A_ibodaA='N : (K:) or legal impurity that forbids, or prevents, one's performing prayer &c.: (KT:) or a state annulling legal purity: pl. A^aHodaAvN . (Msb.) [See 4.] ― -b5- I. q. waliY~N (assumed tropical:) [The rain following that called the wasomiY~ ]: (L:) or AlA^aHodaAvu [pl. of AlHadavu ] signifies the rains of the commencement, or first part, of the year. (K.) ― -b6- Young, applied to a man, (A, * L, Msb, *) and to a horse or an ass or the like, and a camel, and, accord. to IAar, to a mountain-goat: (L:) pl. A^aHodaAvN (A, L, Msb,) and HudovaAnN . (L.) You say rajulN HadavN , (Th, S, L, &c.,) and ↓ Hadiyvu Als~in~i , (Th, S, A, Msb, K,) and Hadavu Als~in~ , (IDrd, K, [but this is by some disallowed, as will be seen below,]) A young man: (S, L, Msb, K:) and in the pl. sense you say gilomaAnN A^aHodaAvN and HudovaAnN [pls. of HadavN ], (S,) and rijaAlN A^aHodaAvu Als~in~i and HudovaAnu Als~in~i , [or these, as is implied above, are not allowable,] and HudavaA='u Als~in~i [pl. of ↓ HadiyvN ]. (ISd, TA.) J says, [in the S,] if you mention the sin~ , you say Als~in~i ↓ Hadiyvu [lit. Young of tooth ]: and IDrst says, the vulgar say, huwa Hadavu Als~in~i , like as you say Hdyv Als~in~i ; but it is a mistake; for HadavN is an epithet applied to the man himself, and is originally an inf. n.; one should not apply it as an epithet to the sin~ nor to the Diros nor to the nAb ; but ↓ HadiyvN is an epithet applied to anything recent. (TA.)

definition: The first, or beginning, or commencement, of a state, or a case, or an affair;
sourceDefinition: The first, or beginning, or commencement, of a state, or a case, or an affair; (S, A, Mgh, K;) as also ↓ HadaAvapN : (S, Mgh, K:) and its freshness; which is also a signification of both these words. (S, Mgh.) So in the saying, AifoEalo *`lika AlA^amora biHidovaAnihi and ↓ biHadaAvatihi [ Do thou that thing while it is in its first and fresh state ]. (S, Mgh. *) One says also, A^atayotuhu fiY HidovaAni $abaAbihi and $bAbh ↓ HidovaY and $bAbh ↓ Hadiyvi (assumed tropical:) I came to him in the beginning, or first period, of his youth. (Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, TA.) And it is said in a trad., addressed to 'Áïsheh, lawolaA HidovaAnu qawomiki biAlkufori lahadamotu AlkaEobapa wabanayotuhaA , (Mgh, * TA,) or, as some relate it, qwmk ↓ HadaAvapu , which means the same, (Mgh,) i. e. Were it not for the shortness of the period that has elapsed since thy people were in the state of infidelity, I would pull down the Kaabeh, and build it [anew]. (TA.) ― -b2- See also HadavN , in two places.

sourceDefinition: New, recent; (K;) contr. of qadiymN : (S:) having, or having had, a beginning; existing newly, for the first time, not having been before; as also ↓ HaAdivN : (Msb:) brought into existence, caused to be, made, produced, or done, newly, for the first time, not having been before; begun, or originated; invented; innovated; as also ↓ muHodavN . (TA.) ― -b2- See HadavN , last two sentences, in four places. And see HidovaAnN . You say also, huwa Hadiyvu EahodK biAlA_isolaAmi He is, or was, recently become a Muslim. (Msb.) And Hadiyvuw EahodK bikuforihimo , (TA,) or biAljaAhiliy~api , or HadiyvN Eahoduhumo , (Mgh,) Men lately in their state of infidelity [or in the state of paganism or ignorance ]; who have but recently ceased to be in their state of infidelity [&c.]. (TA.) -A2- Also i. q. xabarN [ Information; a piece of information; intelligence; an announcement; news, or tidings; a piece of news; an account; a narration, or narrative; a story; &c.]; (S, K;) employed to signify little and much; (S;) and ↓ Hid~iyvaY signifies the same: (K:) or a thing, or matter, that is talked of, told, or narrated, and transmitted: (Msb:) [and talk, or discourse: ] and [in like manner] ↓ A^uHoduwvapN signifies a thing that is talked of, told, or narrated: (S, K:) or this last signifies a wonderful thing: (IB, TA:) it has been asserted, says MF, that there is no difference between AHdwvp and Hdyv in usage, and in denoting what is good and what is evil; in contradiction to such as say that the former peculiarly signifies that [ kind of story ] in which there is no profit nor any truth; such as amatory stories, and the like fictions of the Arabs: Fr asserts it to signify peculiarly a laughable and an absurd story; differing from Hdyv : and Ibn-Hishám El-Lakhmee, in his Expos of the Fs, says that it is only used to denote what is bad, or evil: but Lb replies against him, in his Expos., that it is sometimes used to denote what is good; as in a saying mentioned by Yaakoob, which see below: (TA:) the pl. of HadiyvN is A^aHaAdiyvu , contr. to analogy, (S, K,) said by Fr to be pl. of ↓ A^uHoduwvapN , and then used as pl. of Hdyv , (S,) but IB says that this is not the case; (TA;) and HidovaAnN and HudovaAnN are also pls. of Hdyv , (K, TA,) sometimes occurring; the latter, rare. (TA.) You say, samiEotu HadiyvFA HasanFA (TA) and HasanapF ↓ Hid~iyvaY (S, A, * TA) [ I heard a good story or narrative &c.]; both meaning the same. (TA.) And Ainota$ara HasanapN ↓ lahu fiY Aln~aAsi A^uHoduwvapN [ A good story of him became spread abroad among the people ]: a saying mentioned by Yaakoob in his “ Isláh. ” (TA.) And maliyHapN ↓ A^vHoduwvapN [ A pretty story ], and A^aHaAdiyvu milaAHN [ pretty stories ]. (A.) And ↓ qado SaAra fulaAnN A^aHoduwvapF [(tropical:) Such a one has become the subject of a story, or of a wonderful story: and in like manner, as is said in the A, SaAruwA A^aHaAdiyva : there said to be tropical]. (IB, TA.) ― -b2- Hence the Hadiyv of the Apostle of God: (Msb:) [i. e.] HadiyvN also signifies A narration of a muHad~iv : (L:) [meaning HadiyvN nabawiY~N , i. e. a tradition, or narration, relating, or describing, a saying or an action &c. of Mo- hammad: ] this word and xabarN both signify a tradition that is traced up to Mohammad, or to a Sahábee, or to a Tábi'ee: (TA in art. rqA^ :) or Hdyv is applied to what comes from the Prophet: xabarN , to what comes from another than the Prophet; or from him or another: and A^avarN to what comes from a Companion of the Prophet; but it may also be applied to a saying of the Prophet: (Kull p. 152:) the word in this sense, i. e. the Hdyv of the Prophet, has for its pl. only A^aHaAdiyvu ; and therefore Sb mentions it in the category of those words which have pls. anomalously formed; such as EaruwDN , pl. A^aEaAriyDu ; and baATilN , pl. A^abaATiylu . (TA.) [ AlHadiyva written at the end of a quotation of a part of a trad. is for AiqoraA^i AlHadiyva Read the tradition. ] ― -b3- HadiyvN qudosiY~N [ A holy tradition or narration ] means what God has told to his prophet by inspiration, or by a dream, or in sleep, and the prophet has told in his own phraseology: the Kur-án is esteemed above this, because [it is held that] its words also were revealed: (KT:) that of which the words are from the apostle, but the meaning is from God, by inspiration, or by a dream, or in sleep. (Kull p. 288.)

sourceDefinition: , in its primary acceptation, A party, or company of men, assembling themselves on account of an event that has befallen them ( liA^amori Hazabahumo ): (Ksh and Bd in v. 61:) [and then, in a general sense,] an assembly, a collective body, or company, of men: (IAar, A, Mgh, L, K:) a party, portion, division, or class, (S, A, L, Msb, K, TA,) of men: (L, Msb, TA:) the troops, or combined forces, of a man; (K, TA;) his party, partisans, or faction, prepared, or ready, for fighting and the like: (TA:) the companions, (S, K,) sect, or party in opinions or tenets, (K,) of a man: (S, K:) any party agreeing in hearts and actions, whether meeting together or not: (El-Moajam, TA:) pl. A^aHozaAbN . (S, A, Mgh, Msb, L, K.) And the pl., with the article, Those people who leagued together to wage war against Mohammad: (K:) or the parties that combined to war with the prophets. (S.) And in the Kur xl. 31, The people of Noah and 'Ád and Thamood, and those whom God destroyed after them, (K, TA,) as the people of Pharaoh. (TA.) And yawomu AlA^aHozaAbi [ The day of the combined forces; ] the day [or war ] of the moat ( Alxanodaq ). (Mgh, Msb, TA.) ― -b2- I. q. wirodN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA,) either in its proper sense, A turn, or time, of coming to water: or in the sense next following, which is tropical. (TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) A set portion of the Kur-án, (A, Mgh, L, TA,) and of prayer, (Mgh, L, TA,) &c., (Mgh,) of which a man imposes upon himself the recital (A, Mgh, TA) on a particular occasion, (Mgh,) or at a particular time; (TA;) a set portion of prayer, and of recitation [ of the Kur-án ], &c., which a person is accustomed to perform: (Msb:) pl. as above. (Mgh.) You say, qaraA^a Hizobahu mina AlquroA=ni (tropical:) [ He recited his set portion of the Kur-án ]. (A.) And kamo Hizobuka (tropical:) [ How much is thy set portion of the Kur-án ?]. sourceDefinition: It (a thing) became filled [or stuffed; as also ↓ AnH$Y ]. (K.) And in like manner you say of a man, AHt$Y mina AlT~aEaAmi He became filled [or stuffed ] with food. (TA.) sourceDefinition: , like the inf. n., (TA,) Stuffing; (PS;) [i. e.] what is put into a pillow, or cushion, &c.: (K, TA:) and [hence] cotton: and the seeds used for seasoning food, [and the rice &c., ] with which the belly of a lamb is stuffed: pl. ↓ maHaA$K , deviating from rule. (TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) The soul of a man. (K, TA.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) [ A parenthesis; ] a redundant part, or portion, of speech, or of a sentence, (K, TA,) upon which nothing is syntactically dependent. (TA. [See Har pp. 85 and 86.]) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) [ A digression. ] ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) The portion of either hemistich of a verse that is comprised between the first and last foot. (KT, &c.) ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) Small, or young, camels, (S, K,) among which are no great, or old, ones; (S, TA;) as also ↓ HaA$iyapN : (S, K:) so called because they enter, or occupy the spaces, among the latter; or because they go against the sides of the latter: (TA:) accord. to ISk, (S,) ↓ AlHaA$iyataAni signifies [ the camel termed ] Aibonu AlmaxaADi and [ that termed ] Aibonu All~abuwni : (S, and K in art. H$Y :) the pl. [of HaA$iyapN ] is ↓ HawaA$K . (TA.) It is said in a trad. respecting the poorrate, A^amowaAlihimo ↓ Hu*o mino HawaA$iY , i. e., accord. to IAth, (assumed tropical:) Take thou of the small, or young, of their camels; such as those termed Abn AlmxAD and Abn Allbwn . (TA. [But see another explanation of this saying voce HaA$iyapN in art. H$Y .]) ― -b7- And Ha$owN and ↓ HaA$iyapN signify also (assumed tropical:) The like of mankind; (S;) [i. e.] HaA$iyapN signifies (tropical:) the lower or lowest, baser or basest, meaner or meanest, sort, or the rabble, or refuse, of mankind, or of the people; (TA in art. H$Y , and Har p. 61;) as also Ha$owN [which is of frequent occurrence in this sense]; (KL;) and ↓ Hi$owapN ; (S, TA;) such as servants and the like. (Har ubi suprà, in explanation of HA$yp . [See also this word in art. H$Y .]) You say, ↓ jaA='a fulaAnN maEa HaA$iyatihi (assumed tropical:) Such a one came with those who were in his quarter and protection: but this may be from Ha$FA signifying “a region, quarter, or tract;” servants and followers being in the quarter and protection of their master. (Har ubi suprà.) And fulaAnN baniY fulaAnK ↓ mino Hi$owapi (assumed tropical:) Such a one is of the lower or lowest, &c., of the sons of such a one. (S.) ― -b8- See also Hu$owapN . -A2- Also A stuffed garment. (Mgh.)

sourceDefinition: A receptacle for spindles: (S, K:) a safaT [or receptacle woven of palm-leaves, in which are stowed perfumes and similar things, of the apparatus of women ]; (K; [in the CK, Als~FqaTu is erroneously put for Als~afaTu ;]) a safaT in which perfumes are kept: (TA:) a duroj , (K,) i. e. a small receptacle of the kind called safaT , in which a woman keeps her perfumes and apparatus, or implements; (TA in art. drj ;) a woman's duroj : (Mgh:) pl. as below. (TA.) It is said in a trad., daxalato Hifo$FA , meaning (assumed tropical:) She entered a small byt [or tent ]. (Mgh.) And in another trad., hal~aA qaEada fiY Hifo$i A^um~ihi , (S,) or hlaA jalasa Alx , (Mgh,) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ Wherefore did he not sit ] in the small byt of his mother? (S, Mgh:) or, accord. to some, the meaning is, Einoda Hifo$i A^um~ihi [i. e., by the receptacle for the spindles, &c., of his mother ]: (S:) or, as some say, by the faroj of his mother; for (TA) ― -b3- It also signifies (assumed tropical:) The faroj [ pudendum muliebre ]. (K.) ― -b4- And Any vessels that are held in little account, (Lth, K, TA,) that are used as receptacles in the house, or tent, for perfumes and the like, (Lth, TA,) such as glass flasks, or bottles, &c.: (Lth, K, TA:) and an old and worn-out thing, (K, TA,) that is of no use: (TA:) and a large, old and worn-out, sack (K, TA) of [ goats' ] hair: (TA:) pl. (in all the senses of the word, TA) A^aHofaA$N (K, TA) and HafaA$N : (TA:) or A^aHofaA$u Albayoti means the furniture and utensils of the house or tent; and the paltry articles thereof, or such as are held in little account. (Aboo-Sinán, K.) ― -b5- And A^aHofaA$u AlA^aroDi means The [ lizards called ] DibaAb , and the hedgehogs, (K, TA,) and the jerboas, (TA,) of the earth: (K, TA:) not the same as A^aHonaA$ : so says Aboo-Ziyád. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. HamodN (S, L, Msb, K) and maHomadN and maHomidN (L, K) and maHomadapN (S, L, K) and maHomidapN ; (L, K, and so in a copy of the S;) the last of these inf. ns. [and the third also] extr.; (L;) or the last is an inf. n. and the last but one signifies “ a praiseworthy quality, ” or “ a quality for which one is praised; ” (ElFenáree, MF;) or the last may be a simple subst.; (Har p. 392;) He praised, eulogized, or commended, him; spoke well of him; mentioned him with approbation; (Akh, S, L, Msb;) EalaY ka*aA for such a thing; (L, Msb;) contr. of *am~ahu : (S, L:) accord. to IAmb, formed by transposition from madaHa : (marginal note in a copy of the MS:) but it is of less common application than the latter verb; (Msb in art. mdH ;) signifying he praised him, &c., for something depending on his (the latter's) own will: thus, the describing a pearl as clear is not HamodN , but it is madoHN : (Kull p. 150:) or i. q. $akarahu : (Lh, K:) but it differs [sometimes] from this; (Msb;) for $ukorN is only on account of favour received; whereas HamodN is sometimes because of favour received, (Th, Az, Msb,) and sometimes from other causes; (Th;) [and thus] the latter is of more common application than the former; (S;) therefore you do not say, $akarotuhu EalaY $ajaAEatihi ; but you say, Hamidotuhu ElY $jAEth I praised him, &c., for his courage. (Msb.) Hmd also implies admiration: and it implies the magnifying, or honouring, of the object thereof; and lowliness, humility, or submissiveness, in the person who offers it; as in the saying of the afflicted, AlHamodu lil~`hi Praise be to God; since in this case there is no worldly blessing, favour, or benefit. (Msb.) This last phrase is generally pronounced as it is written above: but some of the Arabs are related to have pronounced it AlHamoda lil~`hi , putting the former word in the accus. case as the absolute complement of the verb A^aHomadu understood: and others, AlHamodilil~`hi ; assimilating the final vowel of the former word to the vowel immediately following it: and others, AlHamodu lul~`hi ; assimilating the first vowel in ll~`h to the vowel immediately preceding it: Zj, however, disapproves of the latter two modes of pronouncing it: some of them also said, badaA^otu biAlHamodu lil~`hi , meaning I began with the saying Praise be to God. (L.) [See also HamodN below.] You say, A^aHomadu A_ilayoka A@ll~`ha I praise God (Az, A, * L, K) to thee, or in thy presence: (L:) or with thee: (Kh, Az:) or I praise to thee God's benefits, and his blessings, or favours; or I praise to thee God's blessings, or favours, and discourse to thee of them. (L.) And Hamida lahu A^amorFA (tropical:) He approved of a thing for him. (L, K. *) And Hamida A_ilayohi A^amorFA (tropical:) He approved of a thing for him, and commanded, or enjoined, him to do it. (L.) And jAwarotuhu famaA Hamidotu jiwaArahu (tropical:) [ I became his neighbour, and did not approve of being so ]. (A.) Hmd also implies admiration: and it implies the magnifying, or honouring, of the object thereof; and lowliness, humility, or submissiveness, in the person who offers it; as in the saying of the afflicted, AlHamodu lil~`hi Praise be to God; since in this case there is no worldly blessing, favour, or benefit. (Msb.) This last phrase is generally pronounced as it is written above: but some of the Arabs are related to have pronounced it AlHamoda lil~`hi , putting the former word in the accus. case as the absolute complement of the verb A^aHomadu understood: and others, AlHamodilil~`hi ; assimilating the final vowel of the former word to the vowel immediately following it: and others, AlHamodu lul~`hi ; assimilating the first vowel in ll~`h to the vowel immediately preceding it: Zj, however, disapproves of the latter two modes of pronouncing it: some of them also said, badaA^otu biAlHamodu lil~`hi , meaning I began with the saying Praise be to God. definition: He (a man, S) came to a state, or result, such as was praised, or commended, or approved;
sourceDefinition: He (a man, S) came to a state, or result, such as was praised, or commended, or approved; properly, his affair, or case, came to such a state or result: (S, L, K:) or (so in the K, but in the L “ and ”) he did, or said, that for which he should be praised, or commended; or that which was praiseworthy, or commendable; (A, L, K; *) contr. of A^a*am~a . (A.) And AHmd A^amoruhu (assumed tropical:) His affair, or case, was, or became, praiseworthy, or approvable, in his estimation: (K:) or AHmd A^amorahu (as in the L) he esteemed his affair, or case, praiseworthy, or approvable. (L [agreeably with what next follows].) -A2- AHmdhu He found him (a man, A, L) [or it ] to be such as is praised, commended, or approved; or praiseworthy, commendable, or approvable; (S, A, L, Msb;) contr. of A^a*am~ahu : (TA in art. *m :) he made it manifest that he was worthy of praise, eulogy, commendation, or approbation: (L:) he approved of his action, and his course of conduct, or his tenet or tenets, and did not expose it, or them, to others. (K.) And A^aHomadotu SaniyEahu (tropical:) [ I found his action to be praiseworthy, or commendable, or approvable ]. (A.) And AHmd AlA^aroDa (tropical:) He approved the land as a dwelling-place: (A:) or he found the land to be such as is praised, commended, or approved; as also ↓ HamidahaA ; (L, K;) but the former verb is the more chaste in this sense. (L.) And AHmd mawoDiEFA (tropical:) He found a place to be such as is praised, commended, or approved, and convenient, or suitable, so that he approved it as a dwelling-place, or for its pasture. (S, L.)

definition: He affected, or made a show of, ( takal~afa ,) praise.
sourceDefinition: He affected, or made a show of, ( takal~afa ,) praise. (A.) You say, ↓ wajadotuhu mutaHam~idFA muta$ak~irFA [ I found him affecting, or making a show of, praise and thanks ]. (A.) ― -b2- He praised himself. (KL.) [Golius assigns this meaning to ↓ AHtmd , as on the authority of the KL; but it is not assigned to this verb in my copy of the KL.] ― -b3- fulaAnN yataHam~adu Aln~As [app. a slight mistranscription, for liln~aAsi , i. q. A_ilaY Aln~aAsi , as in an ex. in the next sentence but one,] Such a one pretends to men, or shows them, that he is praiseworthy, bijuwdihi for his liberality. (L.) ― -b4- tHm~d Ealayohi He reproached him for a favour, or benefit, which he (the former) had bestowed, or conferred; or recounted his gifts, or actions, to him; syn. Aimotan~a . (S, L, K.) One says, mano A^anofaqa maAlahu EalaY nafosihi falaA yataHam~ado bihi EalaY Aln~aAsi [ Whoso expends his property upon himself, he shall not reproach men therewith as for favours, or benefits, bestowed ]: (S, A:) or flA ytHm~d bih A_ilaY Aln~aAsi [ he shall not pretend to men that he is praiseworthy on account of it ]: a prov., meaning that a man is not praised for his beneficence to himself, but for his beneficence to others. (L.)

definition: Praise, eulogy, or commendation;
sourceDefinition: Praise, eulogy, or commendation; &c. (S, &c. [For further explanations of this word, and respecting the phrase AlHamodu lil~`hi and its variations, see 1: and see also $akara .]) suboHaAnaka A@ll~`hum~a wabiHamodika , said by a person praying, means [ I extol, or celebrate, or declare, thy remoteness, or freedom, from every impurity, or imperfection, &c., O God, (see art. sbH ,)] and I begin with praising Thee; A^abotadiy^u being understood: (Az, L, Msb:) or by bHmdk is meant AlHamodu laka praise be to Thee: and nearly the same is said in explanation of the phrase in the Kur [ii. 28], nusab~iHu biHamodika , that by bHmdk is meant HaAmidiyna laka : [see, again, art. sbH :] or by the expression wbHmdk is meant, accord. to Aboo-'Othmán ElMázinee, and by praising Thee I extol thy remoteness, or freedom, from every impurity, &c.; sab~aHotuka being understood: or the w is redundant, as it is in the phrase, rab~anaAwalaka AlHamodu [ O our Lord, praise be to Thee ], in which the w is sometimes omitted: or, accord. to Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà, the w is corroborative, as in the phrase, wahuwa laka , for huwa laka . (Msb.) liwaA='u AlHamodi biyadiY yawoma AlqiyaAmapi [ The standard of praise shall be in my hand on the day of resurrection (said by Mohammad)] means that he shall be singularly distinguished by praise, or praising, on that day. (L.) ― -b2- See HamaAdi : ― -b3- and HumaAdaAka . -A2- See also HamiydN . -A3- It is also said to signify The young one of the kind of bird called qaTFA : so in the prov., Hmodu qaTaApK yasotamiY AlA^araAniba A young one of a katà desires to make the hares its prey: applied to a weak man who desires to insnare a strong one. (Meyd, TA.) -A4- See also what next follows.

sourceDefinition: and ↓ maHomuwdN (S, A, L, K) and ↓ HamuwdN (as in copies of the K, but this seems to be an intensive epithet,) Praised, eulogized, or commended; spoken well of; mentioned with approbation; approved; such as is praised, &c.; praiseworthy, laudable; commendable, or approvable: (S, L, K: [in which, as well as in numberless exs., all these significations are clearly indicated, though not so clearly explained; the Arabic words to which they apply exactly agreeing with the Latin “ laudatus, ” which means both “ praised ” and “ praiseworthy: ”]) the fem. of the first is with p , (L, K,) because the signification, though properly that of a pass. part. n., nearly agrees with that of an act. part. n.: (L:) you say, [ hiYa HamiydapN She is praised, &c.; and] A^afoEaAluhu HamiydapN (tropical:) [ His actions are praised, &c.]. (L.)

sourceDefinition: is a prov., (S,) meaning (tropical:) Repetition is more attributive of praise ( A^akovaru HamodFA ): (S, A, K:) for generally you do not desire to return to a thing save after experience, or knowledge, [and approbation,] thereof: [the act of returning, therefore, implies praise:] or the meaning is, when one begins a kind act, he attracts praise to himself; and when one repeats, he gains more praise for himself: or AHmd is from the pass. part. n., and the meaning is, the beginning is praised, or praiseworthy; and repetition is more deserving of being praised. (K.) [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 130]

definition: (tropical:) He bore rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite, [ cleaving to him, so as ] not be relaxed;

(K, TA.) See also 1. ― -b2- It (the back-bone, or the back, AlS~ulobu ) clave to the belly [ by reason of leanness ]. (K.) ― -b3- It (a camel's hump) became lean and thin. (S.) ― -b4- He (an ass, K, or, as some say, a camel, and a horse or a mule or an ass, TA) became lean, or light of flesh, or slender, and lean, or lean, and lank in the belly, in consequence of much covering: (K, TA:) or, said of a horse or other animal, (A, TA,) or of a camel, (Har p. 173,) his belly clave to his back-bone, or back, by reason of leanness. definition: One who whitens clothes, or garments, by washing and beating them.
sourceDefinition: One who whitens clothes, or garments, by washing and beating them. (S, M, Msb, K.) Hence its pl. HawaAriy~uwna is applied to The companions [i. e. apostles and disciples ] of Jesus, because their trade was to do this. (S, M, Msb.) [Or it is so applied from its bearing some one or another of the following significations.] ― -b2- One who is freed and cleared from every vice, fault, or defect: [or] one who has been tried, or proved, time after time, and found to be free from vices, faults, or defects; from HaAra “ he returned. ” (Zj, TA.) ― -b3- A thing that is pure, or unsullied : anything of a pure, or an unsullied, colour: and hence, ― -b4- One who advises, or counsels, or acts, sincerely, honestly, or faithfully: (Sh:) or a friend; or true, or sincere, friend: (TA:) or an assistant: (S, Msb, K:) or a strenuous assistant: (TA:) or an assistant of prophets: (K:) or a particular and select friend and assistant of a prophet : and hence the pl. is applied to the companions of Mohammad also. (Zj.) ― -b5- A relation. (K.) ― -b6- And HawaAriy~apN A white, or fair, woman; (A;) as also ↓ HawarowarapN ; (T, K;) and so ↓ HaworaA='u , without implying HawarN of the eye: (TA:) pl. of the first HawaAriy~aAtN : (A:) or this pl. signifies women of the cities or towns; (K;) so called by the Arabs of the desert because of their whiteness, or fairness, and cleanness: (TA:) or women clear in complexion and skin; because of their whiteness, or fairness: (TA:) or women inhabitants of regions, districts, or tracts, of cities, towns, or villages, and of cultivated land : (Ksh and Bd in iii. 45:) or [simply] women; because of their whiteness, or fairness. (S.)

definition: The pin of wood, or, as is sometimes the case, of iron, on which the sheave of a pulley turns;
sourceDefinition: The pin of wood, or, as is sometimes the case, of iron, on which the sheave of a pulley turns; (S;) the iron [ pin ] that unites the bent piece of iron which is on each side of the sheave of a pulley, and in which it [the mHwr ] is inserted, and the sheave itself: and a piece of wood which unites ( tajomaEu ) the sheave of a large pulley [app. with what is on each side of the latter; for it seems to mean here, also, the pivot ]: (K:) some say that it is so called because it turns round, returning to the point from which it departed: others, that it is so called because, by its revolving, it is polished so that it becomes white: (Zj:) pl. maHaAwiru . (A.) One says, qaliqato maHaAwiruhu , meaning (tropical:) His circumstances, (A,) or affair, or case, (K,) became unsettled: (A, K:) from the state of the pin of the sheave of a pulley when it becomes smooth, and the hole becomes large, so that it wabbles. (A.) ― -b2- Also A thing (K) of iron (TA) upon which turns the tongue of a buckle at the end of a waist-belt. (K.) ― -b3- And An iron instrument for cauterizing [app. of a circular form: see 2]. (K.) ― -b4- And The wooden implement (S, K) of the baker, or maker of bread, (S,) with which he expands the dough, (K,) and prepares it, and makes it round, to put it into the hot ashes in which it is baked: (TA:) so called because of its turning round upon the dough, as being likened to the mHwr of the sheave of a pulley, and because of its roundness. (T.)

sourceDefinition: She (a camel) brought forth her young one imperfectly formed, (S, Mgh, K,) even if the period of gestation were complete: (S, K:) or so Axdjt waladahaA : and the former, she brought forth her young one imperfectly formed at the completion of the period: (IKt, Msb:) or she brought forth her young one completely formed before the proper time of bringing forth. (TA.) See also 1, in two places. ― -b2- Hence, (TA,) Axdjt Al$~atowapN , (IAar, S,) or AlS~ayofapu , (K,) (tropical:) [ The winter, or the spring or summer (but more probably the former),] had little rain. (IAar, S, K, TA.) And Axdjt Alz~anodapu , (T, TA,) or ↓ xadajat , (TA,) (tropical:) [ The lower of the two wooden instruments for producing fire ] failed to emit fire. (T, TA.) And Axdj (tropical:) He rendered a man defective in a limb, or member: said of God. (A.) And (tropical:) He performed incompletely his prayer; (Es-Sara- kustee, A, Msb;) or so ↓ xadaja : (Msb:) and in like manner, (i. e. the former verb,) (assumed tropical:) a salutation: (TA, from a trad.:) and (tropical:) he performed unsoundly his affair: (A, TA:) and (tropical:) he formed unsoundly his opinion. (A.)

definition: Food that is prepared on the occasion of the birth of a child;

(TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, &c.) Dumb; prevented from speaking by natural conformation; (Msb;) speechless, or destitute of the faculty of speech, by natural conformation, (T and Msb in art. bkm ,) like the beast that lacks the faculty of articulation; (T ibid;) differing from A^abokamu , q. v.: (T and Msb ibid:) or tonguetied, or speechless, (K, TA,) either from inability to find words to express what he would say, or by natural conformation [ of the organs of speech ]: (TA:) fem. xarosaA='u : (Msb:) pl. xurosN (Msb, K) and xurosaAnN . (K.) ― -b2- jamalN A^axorasu A he-camel that has no perforation to his $iqo$iqap , for his bray to issue therefrom, so that he reiterates it therein: such a one they like to send among the [she-camels in the state in which they are termed] $awol , because in most instances he begets females: and naAqapN xarosaA='u a she-camel that is not heard to utter the cry termed rugaA=' . (TA.) ― -b3- EalamN A^axorasu (tropical:) A sign of the way, (K,) [or a mountain, ] from which, (A,) or at, or in, which, ( fiyhi , K,) no echo is heard: (A, K:) or a sign of the way in the mountain whereof no echo is heard: (Lth, T:) or [it seems to be applied to a mountain where no echo is heard; for] it is said when no sound of an echo is heard in the mountain. (S.) ― -b4- saHaAbapN xarosaA='u (tropical:) A cloud that does not thunder: (A:) or a cloud in which is no thunder nor lightning, (S, K, TA,) and of which no sound is heard; which is mostly in winter. (TA.) ― -b5- EayonN xarosaA='u (assumed tropical:) A spring of the running whereof no sound is heard. (TA.) ― -b6- SaxorapN xarosaA='u (assumed tropical:) A hard and solid rock: (Akh, TA:) and EiZaAmN xurosN (assumed tropical:) hard and solid bones. (Th, TA.) ― -b7- katiybapN xarosaA='u (tropical:) An army, or a portion thereof, without any clamour or confused noise: (A:) or whereof no sound is heard, by reason of their staidness in war: (S, K:) or that is silent, by reason of the multitude of the coats of mail, without any clashing of arms. (A 'Obeyd, S, K.) ― -b8- labanN A^axorasu (tropical:) Thick milk, (S, A, K,) that makes no sound in the vessel, (S, K,) or that does not shake about in its vessel: (A:) or thick milk, of which no sound is heard when it is poured out: (Az, TA:) and $arobapN xarosaA='u (assumed tropical:) a thick draught of milk. (M, TA.) ― -b9- wal~iAniY EiroDFA A^axorasa A^amorasa [or EuroDFA ?] (assumed tropical:) He turned from me, and would not speak to me. sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. xa$obN , (TA,) He mixed a thing (S, K) with ( bi ) another thing. (S.) ― -b2- And He picked out, chose out, or selected, a thing: the verb thus having two contr. significations. (K, TA.) -A2- Also, (S, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S,) He polished a sword, (S, K,) by laying on it a broad and smooth spearhead and rubbing it therewith: so accord. to ElAhmar, who relates that an Arab of the desert said to him, I said to a sword-polisher, “ Hast thou finished my sword? ” and he answered, naEamo A_il~aA A^an~iY lamo A^axo$ibohu [ Yes, except that I have not polished it ]. (S.) And [or, as in the TA, “ or ”] He sharpened it. (K, TA.) ― -b2- And He forged a sword: (K:) or fashioned it with the file, without polishing it: (TA:) or he made it imperfectly, not thoroughly, or not well: (A:) thus, again, the verb has two contr. significations: (K:) also he thus made an arrow: (A:) or he shaped out a bow, (AHn, K,) and an arrow, (TA,) [ in a rough manner, or] by the first operation, (AHn, K, TA,) without perfecting it, or making it smooth, or even. (TA.) You say of a sword, before it has been filed, maA A^aHosana maA xu$iba [ How well has it been forged! ]: and in like manner one says of an arrow, when it has been filed, before the safan [with which it is smoothed] has been applied to it. (Skr, on a verse of Sakhr, cited below, voce xa$iybapN .) ― -b3- [Hence,] xa$aba Al$~iEora , (ISk, S, A, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (A,) (tropical:) He said, spoke, or uttered, the poetry (ISk, S, A, K) as it came, (ISk, S,) [ unpolished, and unstudied, ] without affecting nicety, or refinement, therein, (ISk, S, A, K,) and without study, or labour: (A, K:) Jereer did thus, and Farezdak trimmed his verses; but the verses of Jereer thus produced are better than the trimmed verses of Farezdak: (A, TA:) and ↓ Axt$bhu signifies the same. (A, K.) You say also, humo yaxo$ibuwna AlkalaAma waAlEamala (tropical:) [ They say, speak, or utter, words, and do work, without affecting nicety, or refinement, and without study, or labour ]: (A:) or imperfectly, or not thoroughly; inelegantly, or not well. (TA.) And Ait~axa*a Als~ayofa xa$abFA : see 8.

definition: [ Wood, such as is used in carpentry and the like;
sourceDefinition: [ Wood, such as is used in carpentry and the like; timber; ] thick wood: (A, K:) [a coll. gen. n.:] n. un. xa$abapN [signifying a piece of wood or timber ]: (Msb:) the pl. of the latter, (S, Msb, *) or of the former, (K,) is xa$abN , (S, K, [i. e., accord. to the K, the pl. is the same as the sing., but properly speaking, as said above, this is a coll. gen. n.,]) and xu$ubN and xu$obN (S, Msb, K) and xu$obaAnN , (S, K,) [which last is agreeable with analogy as pl. of xa$abN ,] or xu$obaAnN is pl. of xu$obN , and xu$obN is pl. of xa$abapN . (JK.) The hypocrites are described in a trad. as xu$ubN biAll~ayoli SuxubN biAln~ahaAri Like timbers, or pieces of wood, in the night; [ clamorous in the day; ] meaning that they pass the night in sleep, without prayer. (TA.) ― -b2- maAlN xa$abN (assumed tropical:) Cattle that are lean, or emaciated, syn. hazolaY , (K,) in consequence of their feeding upon dry herbage. (TA.) [And it seems that ↓ xa$abN signifies the same: for I find in the TA, and in a copy of the A which I believe to have been used by the author of the TA, mentioned as tropical, maAlN xa$abN waHaTibN jazolN , app. meaning that maAlN xa$ibN and HaTibN signify jazolN ; but jazolN , I think, is here evidently a mistranscription for hazolaY ; as HaTibN is explained in the S and K as signifying “ very lean or meagre. ”]

definition: Rough, or coarse;

(A, TA.) ― -b4- See also xa$iybN voce xa$ibN , in three places. ― -b5- It also signifies Bad, corrupt, or vile. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. xaTofN ; (S, TA;) this is the approved form of the verb; (T, S;) and xaTafahu , aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. as above; (Msb;) a form of the verb mentioned by Akh, (S,) but this is rare, (S, K,) or (K) bad, (S, K,) scarcely, or not at all, known; (S;) and ↓ AxtTfhu , (S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) and ↓ txT~fhu ; (S Msb, TA;) He seized it; or took it, or carried it off, by force: (S, K:) or he did so quickly; snatched it away: (Mgh, Msb, TA:) and ↓ xT~f has been said to imply repetition of the action [unless it be a variation of AxtTf as in a case mentioned below]; but this is strange, and not known on any other authority than that of the “ Akáneem et-Taaleem ” by El-Khuweiyee, a disciple of El-Fakhr Er-Rázee. (MF, TA.) Hence, in the Kur [xxix. 67], Aln~aAsu ↓ wayutaxaT~afu mino Hawolihimo [ And men are carried off by force from around them ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] h`*aA sayofN yaxoTafu Alr~aA^osa (tropical:) [ This is a sword that will strike off the head ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And xaTifa AlbaSara and xaTafahu , said of lightning, (K,) and of a ray of light, and of a [glistening] sword, and of any polished body, (TA,) (tropical:) It took away the sight: (K, TA:) and ↓ AuxotuTifa baSaruhu (tropical:) His sight was suddenly taken away. (M and K in art. mls .) It is said in the Kur [ii. 19], yakaAdu Albaroqu yaxoTafu A^aboSaArahumo (tropical:) [ The lightning almost taketh away their sight, lit. sights ]: (TA:) Yoo read yaxoTifu AbSArhm ; (S, TA;) and so did Aboo-Rejà and Mujáhid: and some read ↓ yixiT~ifu , and ↓ yaxaT~ifu , originally yaxotaTifu , accord. to the opinion of the Basrees, disputed by Fr, but confirmed by Zj. (TA.) ― -b4- And xaTifa Als~amoEa , (K,) aor. , (S,) said of a devil, (tropical:) He stole [ an opportunity of ] hearing [ the speech of the angels, from the confines of the lowest Heaven; or snatched it ]; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ AxtTfhu : (K:) the two verbs being like nazaEahu and AinotazaEahu . (Sb, TA.) Hence, in the Kur [xxxvii. 10], ↓ A_il~aA mano xaTifa AlxaTofapa (tropical:) Except him who steals the [ opportunity of ] hearing: (TA:) or who snatches unawares and by stealth, (Bd,) or hears and snatches, (Jel,) the speech of the angels: (Bd, Jel:) EL-Hasan read Al~A mn AlxTfp ↓ xaT~afa , originally A@xotaTafa : (S, TA:) and another reading, ascribed to him and others, is ↓ xiT~ifa ; but this is very weak. (TA.) ― -b5- xaTifa , aor. ; and xaTafa , aor. ; inf. n. xaTafaAnN ; (K;) thus in all the copies of the K, but correctly xaTofN , as in the L; (TA;) said of a camel, (assumed tropical:) He went along quickly. (K, TA.) And mar~a yaxoTafu xaTofFA munokarFA (assumed tropical:) He went along at a quick rate [ such as was deemed strange, or disapproved ]. (TA.) And xaTifati Als~afiynapu , and xaTafat , (assumed tropical:) The ship sailed, or voyaged: you say, xaTifati Alyawoma mino EumaAna (assumed tropical:) She sailed,. or voyaged, to-day, from 'Omán. (TA.)

definition: A single act of seizing;
sourceDefinition: A single act of seizing; or, of taking, or carrying off, by force: (TA:) or, of doing so quickly; of snatching away. (Mgh, Msb, TA.) Hence, [in a trad.,] accord. to one reading, nahaY Eano kul~i *iY xaTofapK , meaning He prohibited the prey of whatever snatches away the prey, and goes away with it, not withholding it for its owner: or, as some say, what snatches away with its talon, or claw: but the reading commonly known is, nahaY Eani AlxaTofapi : (Mgh:) and AlxaTofapu signifies what the wolf, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) or the like, (Msb,) snatches away, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) of the limbs, or members, of a living sheep or goat, (Mgh, TA,) or of a living animal; (Msb;) or what the dog snatches away from the limbs, or members, of the animal of the chase, of flesh &c., while the animal is alive: (Mgh, TA:) or the limb, or member, which the beast or bird of prey seizes, or carries off by force, or which a man cuts off, from the beast that is alive: (K, TA:) for whatever is separated from the living animal, (Mgh, TA,) of flesh or fat, (TA,) is carrion, (Mgh, TA,) unlawful to be eaten: the prohibition originated from the Prophet's finding, when he came to El-Medeeneh, that the people loved and ate the humps of camels and the tails of sheep: (TA:) the reading AlxaTafap , of the measure faEalap , with fet-h to the medial radical letter, as pl. of xaATifN , is a mistake. (Mgh.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) A single suck of a small quantity of milk quickly taken by a child from the breast. (TA.) ― -b3- For its meaning in the Kur xxxvii. 10, see 1. ― -b4- See also xuTofN .

definition: The drinking of camels on the fifth day, counting the day of the next preceding drinking as the first;
sourceDefinition: The drinking of camels on the fifth day, counting the day of the next preceding drinking as the first; their drinking one day, then pasturing three days, then coming to the water on the fifth day, the first and last days, on which they drink, being thus reckoned : this is the correct explanation, accord. to Aboo-Sahl El-Khowlee; and Aboo-Zekereeyà says the like; (TA;) or their pasturing three days, and coming to the water on the fourth day [ not counting the day of the next preceding watering; for it is evident that this explanation is virtually the same as that preceding]: (S, K:) accord. to Lth, the drinking of camels on the fourth day, counting the day on which they returned from [ the next preceding ] watering; but Az says, that this is a mistake; the day of returning from watering not being counted [when it is explained as meaning the drinking on the fourth day]: (TA:) pl. A^axomaAsN , the only pl. form. (Sb, TA.) [See Zimo'N .] Hence, falaApN ximosN [as in copies of the K, or it may be falaApu ximosK ,] A desert in which the water is far distant, so that the camels come to the water on the fourth day, exclusive of the [ next preceding ] day on which they drank. (Az, K, TA.) Hence also the saying, fulaAnN yaDoribu A^axomaAsFA liA^asodaAsK (S, K *) (tropical:) Such a one makes a pretence of AxmAs [or fifth-day waterings ] for the purpose of AsdAs [or sixth-day waterings ]: i. e., he advances his camels from the ximos to the sidos : (K:) a prov.: (TA:) meaning, such a one strives to deceive, or circumvent : (S, K:) applied to him who acts towards another with artifice, pretending that he obeys him, or complies with his desire: (TA:) or to him who pretends one thing while he means another: (K:) and taken from the saying, related by AO and IAar, Daraba A^axomaAsFA liA^asodaAsK [ He made a pretence of AxmAs for the purpose of AsdAs ]; said of him who proposes a thing whereby he means another thing, which he commences and by slow degrees accomplishes: (TA:) for a man, when he desires to make a long journey, accustoms his camels to drink ximosFA sidosFA [i. e. on the fifth day and then on the sixth, in each case counting the day of the next preceding drinking as the first ]: (K, TA:) the origin of the saying, accord. to IAar, being this: an old man was among his camels, accompanied by his sons, men, who pastured them, and who had been long far distant from their families; and he told them one day to pasture their camels riboEFA [i. e. watering on the fourth day, counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first], which they did, proceeding in the way towards their families: then they proposed to do so ximosFA ; and then, sidosFA : whereupon the old man, understanding what they meant, said, ye are doing nothing but making a pretence of AxmAs for the purpose of AsdAs : the object of your desire is not the pasturing of them, but it is only your families. (TA.) [See below, voce xumusN , a saying similar in words but different in meaning.] ― -b2- It is also used for sayoru ximosK [ A journey in which the camels are watered only on the first and fifth days; a journey in which the second and third and fourth days are without water ]. (L in art. jl* .) You say ximsN baSobaASN , [and SaboSaAbN ,] and qaEoqaAEN , and HavoHaAvN , [and HaSoHaASN , &c.,] i. e. A journey [ in which the camels are watered only on the first and fifth days, ] in the course of which, to the water, there is no flagging, by reason of its remoteness. (TA.) El-'Ajjáj uses the expression ximosN kaHaboli Al$~aEari AlmunoHat~i meaning, A [ journey of the kind termed ] xms without any deviation, like a rope made of hair that has fallen off and that is free from any unevenness. (L, TA.) ― -b3- ximosN also signifies The fifth young one, or offspring. (A in art. vlv .) -A2- A [ garment of the kind called ] burod , (S, K,) of the fabric of El-Yemen; (S;) so called because first made for a king of El-Yemen named ximosN , (AA, S,) or Alximosu ; (K, TA;) as also ↓ xamiysN . (TA.) For the latter word, we find in the work of Bkh, xamiyS , with S ; which, if correct, is masc. of xamiySapN , which is a small kind of kisaA=' . (IAth, and L.) [The pl. of ximosN applied to a burodap is A^axomaAsN .] See also maxomuwsN , in four places.

Hence also the saying, fulaAnN yaDoribu A^axomaAsFA liA^asodaAsK (S, K *) (tropical:) Such a one makes a pretence of AxmAs [or fifth-day waterings ] for the purpose of AsdAs [or sixth-day waterings ]: i. e., he advances his camels from the ximos to the sidos : (K:) a prov.: (TA:) meaning, such a one strives to deceive, or circumvent : (S, K:) applied to him who acts towards another with artifice, pretending that he obeys him, or complies with his desire: (TA:) or to him who pretends one thing while he means another: (K:) and taken from the saying, related by AO and IAar, Daraba A^axomaAsFA liA^asodaAsK [ He made a pretence of AxmAs for the purpose of AsdAs ]; said of him who proposes a thing whereby he means another thing, which he commences and by slow degrees accomplishes: (TA:) for a man, when he desires to make a long journey, accustoms his camels to drink ximosFA sidosFA [i. e. on the fifth day and then on the sixth, in each case counting the day of the next preceding drinking as the first ]: (K, TA:) the origin of the saying, accord. to IAar, being this: an old man was among his camels, accompanied by his sons, men, who pastured them, and who had been long far distant from their families; and he told them one day to pasture their camels riboEFA [i. e. watering on the fourth day, counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first], which they did, proceeding in the way towards their families: then they proposed to do so ximosFA ; and then, sidosFA : whereupon the old man, understanding what they meant, said, ye are doing nothing but making a pretence of AxmAs for the purpose of AsdAs : the object of your desire is not the pasturing of them, but it is only your families. (TA.) [See below, voce xumusN , a saying similar in words but different in meaning.] ― -b2- It is also used for sayoru ximosK [ A journey in which the camels are watered only on the first and fifth days; a journey in which the second and third and fourth days are without water ]. (L in art. jl* .) You say ximsN baSobaASN , [and SaboSaAbN ,] and qaEoqaAEN , and HavoHaAvN , [and HaSoHaASN , &c.,] i. e. A journey [ in which the camels are watered only on the first and fifth days, ] in the course of which, to the water, there is no flagging, by reason of its remoteness. (TA.) El-'Ajjáj uses the expression ximosN kaHaboli Al$~aEari AlmunoHat~i meaning, A [ journey of the kind termed ] xms without any deviation, like a rope made of hair that has fallen off and that is free from any unevenness. (L, TA.) ― -b3- ximosN also signifies The fifth young one, or offspring. (A in art. vlv .) -A2- A [ garment of the kind called ] burod , (S, K,) of the fabric of El-Yemen; (S;) so called because first made for a king of El-Yemen named ximosN , (AA, S,) or Alximosu ; (K, TA;) as also ↓ xamiysN . (TA.) For the latter word, we find in the work of Bkh, xamiyS , with S ; which, if correct, is masc. of xamiySapN , which is a small kind of kisaA=' . (IAth, and L.) [The pl. of ximosN applied to a burodap is A^axomaAsN .] See also maxomuwsN , in four places.

sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) masc.; and xamosN , fem.; (S;) [ Five; ] a certain number. (S, K.) You say xamosapu rijaAlK [ Five men ], and xamosu nisowapK [ Five women ]. (S.) You say also, EinodiY xamosapu daraAhimo [ I have five dirhems ], with refa: and if you please, you incorporate the p into the d [and say, xamosap d~araAhima ]: but when you prefix Al to drAhm , you say, EinodiY xamosapu Ald~araAhimi [ I have the five dirhems ], with damm; and may not incorporate, because you have incorporated the l into the d : and in the case of a fem. n. you say, EinodiY xamosu Alquduwri [ I have the five cooking-pots ]: also, h`*ihi Alxamosapu Ald~araAhimi [ These five dirhems ]; and, if you please, Ald~araAhimu , using it in the manner of an epithet: and in like manner [you use the other nouns of number] to Ea$arapN [inclusive]. (S.) You say also, SumonaA xamosFA mina Al$~ahori [ We fasted during a period of five nights of the month with their days]; making layaAlK to predominate over A^ay~aAm , when you do not mention the word Ay~Am , though the fasting is in the day; because the night of each day precedes the day: but when you mention the word Ay~Am , you say, SumonaA xamosapa A^ay~aAmK [ We fasted five days ]. (ISk, TA.) yaEaD~u biAlxamosi means He bites the fingers: these being [five in number and] of the fem gender: (Ham p. 790:) [i. e.] xamosN means the five fingers. (Har p. 76.) [Respecting a peculiar pronunciation of the people of El-Hijáz, and a case in which xamosap is imperfectly decl., see valaAvapN .] ― -b2- [ xamosapa Ea$ara , masc.; and xamosa Ea$orapa , fem.; Fifteen. For variations thereof, see art. E$r .]

definition: Five cubits in length;
sourceDefinition: Five cubits in length; applied to a spear, (S, A, K,) as also ↓ xamiysN ; (K;) and to a garment, or piece of cloth, (S, A, K,) as also ↓ xamiysN , (S, A, Mgh, K,) which occurs in a trad. as meaning a small garment or piece of cloth, (Mgh,) and ↓ xumaAsiY~N [q. v. suprà]; (TA;) and in like manner, ↓ burodapu A^axomaAsK a [ garment of the kind called ] brdp fire cubits long. (ISk, TA.) Hence the saying, ↓ humaA fiY burodap A^axomaAsK (assumed tropical:) They two have become near together, and in a state of agreement. (K.) A poet says, Say~araniY juwdu yadayhi wamano ↓ A^ahowaAhu fiY burodapi A^axomaAsi i. e., (assumed tropical:) The bounty of his hands has made me and the person whom I love to be near together, as though we were in a brdp five cubits long: (Th, TA:) app. meaning that the person thus spoken of had purchased for him a female slave, or had given for him the dowry of his wife. (Az, Sgh, TA.) You also say, ↓ layotanaAfiY burodapi A^axomaAsK , a prov., meaning (assumed tropical:) Would that we were near together. (ISk, TA.) [See also burodN .] ― -b2- Also A rope made of five strands twisted together. (S, A, K.)

Ye used to act unfaith fully to yourselves ] means ye used to act un faithfully, one to another: (S, * TA:) or ye used to act wrongfully to yourselves: AixotiyaAnN has a more intensive signification than xiyaAnapN . (TA.) ― -b3- And xaAnatohu rijolaAhu (assumed tropical:) [ His two legs were unfaithful to him; ] he was unable to walk. (TA.) ― -b4- And xAn Ald~alowa Alr~i$aA='u (assumed tropical:) The well-rope broke off, or be came severed, from the bucket. (TA.) ― -b5- And xAnhu Ald~ahoru , inf. n. xawonN ; (T, TA;) and ↓ txw~nhu ; (TA;) (assumed tropical:) Time altered his state, or condition, (T, TA,) from softness, or easiness, to hardness, or difficulty, (TA,) or to evil; (T, TA;) and in like manner, Aln~aEiymu [ enjoyment, &c.]: and of everything that has altered thy state, or condition, [for the worse,] one says, ↓ taxaw~anaka . (T, TA.)

sourceDefinition: : see 1, last sentence, in two places. You say also, taxaw~anahumo meaning He sought [ to discover, or show, ] their xiyaAnap [i. e. treachery, perfidy, or unfaithfulness ], and their slip, lapse, or wrong action; and suspected them, or accused them. (TA.) ― -b2- Also He, or it, diminished it, wasted it, impaired it, or took from it; and so ↓ xw~nhu , and xw~n minohu : (K:) or diminished it, wasted it, impaired it, or took from it, by little and little; syn. tanaq~aSahu . (JK, * S, Msb.) You say, taxawananiY fulaAnN Haq~iY Such a one took from me by little and little of my right, or due. (S, TA.) And Dhu-r-Rummeh says, laA balo huwa Al$~awoqu mino daArK taxaw~anahaA mar~FA saHaAbN wamar~FA baAriHN taribu [ No, but it is, or was, yearning of the soul arising from a place of abode from which some times raining clouds, and sometimes a hot wind carrying with it dust, took away by little and little, so as gradually to efface the traces thereof]. (S, TA.) And Lebeed says, (S, TA,) describing a she-camel, (TA,) taxaw~anahaA nuzuwliY waA@rotiHaAliY [ Which my alighting and my journeying had wasted by little and little; ] i. e. whose flesh and fat my alighting and my journeying had diminished by little and little. (S, TA.) -A2- Also He paid frequent attention to him, or it; or he, or it, returned to him, or it, time after time; syn. taEah~adahu ; (JK, S, K;) and so ↓ xw~nhu : (K:) in this sense, the former verb is [said to be] from txw~lhu , by the substitution of n for l (TA.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, [describing a young gazelle,] laA yanoEa$u AlT~arofa A_il~aA maA taxaw~anahu daAEK yunaAdiyhi biA@somi AlmaA='i maboguwmu (S,) [ He raises not his eye, or eyes, except when a caller calling him by the sound of maA='i returns to him time after time, addressed by the cry termed bugaAm :] i. e. except when he hears the bugaAm of his mother calling him by the cry maA='i maA='i : (TA in art. bgm : [it is there added, that the pass. part. n. maboguwm is used in this instance for the act. part. n.; but for this I see no sufficient reason:]) he says that the young gazelle is slum bering, not raising his eye, or eyes, unless his mother comes to him time after time: or, as some say, unless his mother's call to him takes by little and little from his sleep. (S in the present art.) One says also AlHum~aYtaxaw~anuhu [for tataxaw~anuhu ] The fever returns to him time after time: (S:) or in its time. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (M, Msb, K,) inf. n. daro'N (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and daroA^apN ; (K;) and ↓ dr~A^hu ; (M, TA; [or this latter has probably an intensive signification;]) He pushed it, or thrust it; or pushed it, or thrust it, away, or back; repelled it; or averted it; syn. dafaEahu ; (S, * M, Mgh, * Msb, K;) namely, a thing. (Msb.) Hence, kaAna bayona Eumara wamuEaA*i boni EaforaA='a daro'N There was, between 'Omar and Mo'ádh Ibn-'Afrà, a contending, and a mutual pushing or thrusting, &c. (Mgh.) And daraA^a Eanohumo He repelled from them, or defended them; as also daraha , which is formed by substitution from the former, like haraAqa from A^araAqa . (S in art. drh .) And daraA^a Eanohu AlHad~a He averted ( dafaEa ) from him the prescribed castigation: (M, Mgh:) or he deferred his prescribed castigation: and in like manner the verb is used in relation to other things. (AZ, T.) It is said in a trad., Aidoraw^uwA AlHuduwda biAl$~ubuhaAti [ Avert ye, or defer ye, the prescribed castigations on account of dubious circumstances ]. (ISk, M, TA.) And Aidoraw^uwA AlHuduwda maA A@sotaTaEotumo [ Avert ye, or defer ye, the prescribed castigations as long as ye are able ]. (S, form a trad.) ― -b2- See also 5. ― -b3- daraA^a Eani AlbaEiyri AlHaqaba is explained by Sh as meaning He pushed back the kind girth of the camel: but AM says that the correct meaning is, he spread the kind girth upon the ground, and made the camel to lie down upon it [in order that he might gird him]. (TA.) [For] daraA^a signifies also He spread, or laid flat, (K, TA,) a thing upon the ground. (TA.) ― -b4- daraA^a Al$~aYo'a biAl$~aYo'a He supported the thing by the thing; made the. thing to be a support to the thing. (TA.) [Hence,] daraA^a AlHaAy^iTa bibinaA='K He conjoined the wall with a structure [ so as to support the former by the latter ]. (TA.) ― -b5- daraA^a biHajarK He cast a stone; like radaA^a . (TA.) You say, daraA^ahu biHajar and radaA^ahu bihi He cast a stone at him. (M in art. rdA^ .) ― -b6- daraA^a said of a torrent, (K,) inf. n. daro'N , (TA,) (tropical:) It rushed, or poured forth with vehemence; as also ↓ AndrA^ . (K.) And daraA^a AlwaAdiY biAls~ayoli (assumed tropical:) The valley poured along the torrent. (TA.) [See also daro'N , below.] ― -b7- daraA^a , (K,) inf. n. duruwo'N , (TA,) is syn. with TaraA^a [ He came from a place, or from a distant place, unexpectedly; &c.]. (K.) And you say, daraA^a EalayonaA fulaAnN , (T, S, K, * TA,) inf. n. duruwo'N (S, TA) and daro'N ; (TA;) and ↓ AndrA^ (S, TA) and ↓ tdr~A^ ; (TA;) Such a one came, or came forth, upon us unexpectedly, (T, S, K, * TA,) or whence we knew not; as also TaraA^a , (T,) and daraha . (IAar, TA in art. drh .) And Ealayohi bi$ar~K ↓ AndrA^ , vulg. AndrY , He came upon him suddenly with evil, or mischief. (TA.) ― -b8- Hence, i. e. from daraA^a signifying “ he came, or came forth, unexpectedly, ” (T, S, TA,) daraA^a , inf. n. duruwo'N , said of a star, meaning (tropical:) It shone, or glistened, (S, K, TA,) intensely, (S, TA,) and its light spread: (TA:) or, as some say, it rose. (T.) [Hence also,] daraA^ati Aln~aAru (assumed tropical:) The fire gave light, shone, was bright, or shone brightly. (Sh, K.) -A2- daraA^a , (T, S, K,) aor. , (T,) inf. n. duruwo'N , (T, S,) He (a camel) had what is termed the gud~ap , (S, K,) i. e. the plague, or pestilence, ( TaAEuwn ,) of camels, (T,) and had therewith a tumour in his back, (S, K,) or in his naHor [or stabbing-place, in the uppermost part of the breast ]: but in a female, it is in the udder: (TA:) or had a tumour in his naHor . (IAar, T.) The epithet applied to the male is ↓ daAriy^N : and so, accord. to ISk, to the female, (T, S,) meaning Attacked by the gud~ap in her maraAq , (T, and so in a copy of the S,) thus, without teshdeed to the q , signifying the part, of her throat, which is the place of passage of the water, (T, TA,) or in her maraAq~ [or thin and soft parts of the belly], (so in one of my copies of the S,) so that the protuberance of the gud~ap [or pestilential tumour ] is apparent: which protuberance is termed ↓ daro'N . definition: , primarily, (TA,) signifies The act of opposing;
sourceDefinition: , primarily, (TA,) signifies The act of opposing; and repelling, or striving to repel: (S, TA:) or treating in an evil, or adverse, manner; and opposing: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) or the putting one off in the matter of a right or due, by promising to render it time after time; and treating in an evil, or adverse, and a contrary, manner. (Mgh in arts. drY and $rY .) One says, daraA^otuhu I repelled him, or strove to repel him. (T, Msb, K.) And fulaAnN laA yudaAriy^u wa laA yumaAriY , (S, TA,) i. e. Such a one does not act in an evil, or adverse, manner, nor oppose, [ nor does he wrangle, or dispute obstinately: ] and lA yudaAriY , meaning, accord. to Sgh, if for lA yudaAriy^u , does not repel, or strive to repel, him who has a right from his right. (TA.) ― -b2- Accord. to El-Ahmar, in [the exercise of] good disposition, (T, S,) and in social intercourse, (S,) it is with and without ' ; (T, S;) contr. to the assertion of A 'Obeyd, who says that in this case it is without ' . (T.) [F says,] daAraA^otuhu is syn. with daArayotuhu and daAfaEotuhu and laAyanotuhu [the second of which has a meaning explained above; the first and last meaning I treated him with gentleness or blandishment, soothed him, coaxed him, or wheedled him; &c.]; thus bearing two contr. significations: (K:) [or] daraA^otuhu and daArayotuhu both signify I was fearful, or cautious, of him; and treated him with gentleness or blandishment, or soothed him, coaxed him, wheedled him, or cajoled him: (S:) [but Az says,] I say that the verb with ' means I was fearful, or cautious, of him, as says AZ; or of his evil, or mischief: and daArayotu signifies “ I deceived, deluded, beguiled, circumvented, or outwitted; ” as also darayotu . (T.)
