definition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. rafoEN , (S, Mgh, Msb,) He raised it: [this is generally the best rendering, as it serves to indicate several particular significations which will be found explained in what follows:] he elevated it; upraised it; uplifted it: he took it up: contr. of xafaDahu : (Msb:) or of waDaEahu : (S, Mgh, K:) as also ↓ rf~Ehu , (K,) inf. n. tarofiyEN ; (TA;) and ↓ ArtfEhu ; (K;) for accord. to the “ Nawádir, ” you say, ArtfEhu biyadihi and rafaEahu [ he raised it, lifted it, heaved it, or took it up, with his hand ]; but Az says that ArtfE is intrans., and that he has heard no authority for its being trans., in the sense of rafaEa , except that which he had read in the “ Nawádir el-Aaráb:” (TA:) rafoEN is sometimes applied to corporeal things, meaning the raising, or elevating, a thing from the resting-place thereof: sometimes to a building, meaning the rearing it, uprearing it, or making it high or lofty: (Er-Rághib:) or in relation to corporeal things, it is used properly to denote motion, and removal: (Msb:) it signifies the putting away or removing or turning back a thing after the coming or arriving thereof; like as dafoEN signifies the putting away or removing or turning back a thing before the coming or arriving [thereof]: (Kull p. 185:) but in relation to ideal things, it is [tropically used, as it is also in many other cases, and] accorded in meaning to what the case requires. (Msb.) [In its principal senses, proper and tropical, rafoEN agrees with the Latin Tollere. .] It is said in the Kur [ii. 60 and 87], rafaEonaA fawoqakumu A@lT~uwra We raised above you from its resting-place the mountain: and in the same [xii. 2], Aall~`hu A@l~a*iY rafaEa Als~am`waAti bigayori EamadK tarawonahaA [ God is He who raised the heavens without pillars that ye see; or, as ye see them ]: and in the same [ii. 121], waA_i*o yarofaEu A_ibor`hiymu AlqawaAEida mina Albayoti [ And when Abraham ] was rearing or uprearing or making high or lofty [ the foundations of the House of God, at Mekkeh]. (Er-Rághib.) And you say, AirofaEo h`*aA Take thou this: (Mgh:) or take it and carry it [ away; or take it up and remove it ]. (TA.) And rafaEa Alz~arEa , (Lh, K,) or rafaEahu A_ilaY Albayodari , (Msb,) aor. , (Lh,) inf. n. rafoEN (Lh, S) and rifaAEapN and rifaAEN [perhaps a mistranscription for rafaAEu , which see below], (Lh, TA,) He removed, or transported, the seed-produce from the place in which he had reaped it, (Lh,) or carried it after the reaping, (S, K,) to the place in which the grain was to be trodden out. (Lh, S, K.) [This last signification is said in the TA to be tropical; but according to a passage of the Msb quoted in the first sentence of this art., it is proper. In most of the phrases here following, the verb is undoubtedly used tropically.] ― -b2- rafaEuwA A_ilaY~a Euyuwnahumo (tropical:) [ They raised towards me their eyes ]. (TA.) ― -b3- daxalotu EalaY fulaAnK falamo yarofaEo biY raA^osFA (Mgh, TA *) (tropical:) I went in to such a one, and he did not look towards me, nor pay any regard, or attention, to me. (Mgh.) [ biY is not here a mistake for liY , for the phrase is often found thus written.] ― -b4- rufiEa liYa Al$~aYo'u (assumed tropical:) [ The thing was, as it were, raised into view, i. e. it rose into view, to me; ] I saw the thing from afar. (TA.) ― -b5- rafaEa Als~araAbu Al$~axoSa , aor. , inf. n. rafoEN , (tropical:) The mirage raised, or elevated [ to the eye, (see an ex. near the end of the first paragraph of art. zwl )] the figure of a man or some other thing seen from a distance; [or it may be allowable to render it, made it to appear tall, and as though quivering, vibrating, or playing up and down; ] syn. zahaAhu [of which, when it relates to the mirage, the meaning is best expressed by the latter of the two explanations here given]. (TA.) ― -b6- warafaEonaA baEoDahumo fawoqa baEoDK darajaAtK , in the Kur [xliii. 31], means (assumed tropical:) And we have exalted some of them above others in degrees of rank, or station: and narofaEu darajaAtK mano na$aA='u , in the same, [vi. 83, and xii. 76,] (assumed tropical:) We exalt in degrees of rank, or station, whom We please: (Er-Rághib:) and waA@ll~`hu yarofaEu mano ya$aA='u wayaxofiDu (assumed tropical:) And God exalteth whom He pleaseth, and abaseth: (S and TA:) and [in like manner,] rafoEu Al*~ikori means the exalting of one's fame; as in the Kur xciv. 4. (Er-Rághib.) But the words, waA_ilaY Als~amaA='i kayofa rufiEato , in the Kur [lxxxviii. 18], indicate two meanings; And to the heaven, how it is elevated in respect of its place; and (assumed tropical:) how it is exalted in respect of excellence, and exaltation of rank. (Er-Rághib.) [In like manner also,] fiY buyuwtK A^a*ina A@ll~`hu A^ano turofaEa , in the Kur [xxiv. 36], means In houses which God hath permitted to be built; (Bd, TA;) accord. to some: (TA:) or, (assumed tropical:) to be honoured; (Zj, Bd;) so says El-Hasan; (Zj;) or, (assumed tropical:) to be exalted in estimation. (Er-Rághib.) It is said in a trad., A_in~a A@ll~`ha yarofaEu AlEadola wayaxofiDuhu (assumed tropical:) Verily God exalteth the just, and maketh him to have the ascendency over the unjust, and at one time abaseth him, so that He maketh the unjust to overcome him, in order to try his creatures, in the present world. (Az, TA.) [See also art. xfD .] And you say, rafaEahu EalaY SaAHibihi fiY Almajolisi (assumed tropical:) He advanced him above his companion [ in the sitting-place, or sitting-room, or assembly ]. (TA.) And rafaEotuka Eano ka*aA (assumed tropical:) [ I exalted thee, or held thee, above such a thing ]: (M voce rabaA^a :) and A_in~iY laA^arofaEoka Eano h`*aA AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) [ Verily I exalt thee, or hold thee, above this thing ]. (S voce rabaA^a , q. v.) ― -b7- rafaEa A@ll~`hu Eamalahu (assumed tropical:) [ God honoured his work by acceptance; or] God accepted his work. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xxxv. 11], waA@loEamalu AlS~aAliHu yarofaEuhu (assumed tropical:) And righteous work He will accept: (Jel:) or the meaning is yarofaEu AlEamalu AlS~aAliHu Alkalima AlT~ay~aba (assumed tropical:) [ righteous work will cause praise, or the like, (mentioned immediately before the above-cited words of the Kur,) to ascend, and obtain acceptance ]: (Mujáhid, TA:) Katádeh says, [that the meaning is,] speech will not be accepted without work. (TA.) ― -b8- rafoEN Also signifies (assumed tropical:) The bringing a thing near; or presenting, or offering, it; syn. taqoriybN . (S.) And hence, rafaEotuhu A_ilaY Als~uloTaAni , (S, Mgh, K,) and A_ilaY AlHakami , (TA,) inf. n. rafoEN (S, * TA) and rufoEaAnN (S, K) and rifoEaAnN , (TA,) (tropical:) I presented him to, or brought him before, or brought him forward to, the Sultán, (S, * Mgh, * K, * TA,) and the judge, to arraign him and contest with him: (TA:) and A_ilaY AlHaAkimi ↓ raAfaEahu , (S K,) inf. n. muraAfaEapN , (TA,) [in like manner] signifies (tropical:) he preferred a complaint against him to the governor, or judge: (K:) or (tropical:) he presented him to, or brought him before, or brought him forward to, the governor, or judge, to arraign him and contest with him, and preferred a complaint against him: (TA:) [or it denotes the doing so mutually; for, accord. to Mtr,] xaSomahu A_ilaY Als~uloTaAni ↓ raAfaEa signifies (tropical:) he brought his adversary before the Sultán ( qar~abahu A_ilayohi ), the latter doing the same with him. (Mgh.) [See also 2.] ― -b9- rafaEa AlquroA=na EalaY Als~uloTaAni (tropical:) [ He adduced, or brought forward, the Kur-án against the Sultán; ] he interpreted the Kur-án against the Sultán, and judged thereby that he should rebel against him. (TA.) ― -b10- rafoEotu Alr~ajula also signifies (tropical:) I traced up the man's lineage to his greatest ancestor; or I mentioned his lineage, saying, He is such a one the son of such a one, or He is of such a tribe, or city, &c.; syn. namayotuhu , and nasabotuhu . (TA.) ― -b11- And hence, rafaEa AlHadiyva A_ilaY Aln~abiY~i (tropical:) [ He traced up, or ascribed, or attributed, the tradition to the Prophet, mentioning, in ascending order, the persons by whom it had been handed down, up to the Prophet; in the manner more fully explained in the sentence here next following]. (TA.) You say also, rafaEa AlHadiyva A_ilaY qaAy^ilihi , meaning A^asonadahu [i. e. (assumed tropical:) He traced up, or ascribed, or attributed, the tradition to the author thereof, by mentioning him, or by mentioning, uninterruptedly, in ascending order, the persons by whom it had been transmitted, up to the Prophet; or by mentioning the person who had related it to him from the Prophet if only one person intervened, saying, “ Such a one told me, from such a one, ” ( and so on if more than one intervened between him and the Prophet, ) “ from the Apostle of God; ” or with an interruption in the mention of the persons by whom it had been transmitted ]. (S * and Msb in art. snd .) [And hence what next follows.] It is said in a trad., rafaEato A_ilayonaA mina AlbalaAgi ↓ kul~u raAfiEapK faqado Har~amotuhaA A^ano tuEoDada A^awotuxobaTa , (S, * TA, [in a very old and excellent copy of the former of which I find, as above, A_ilayonaA , and so in some copies of the K and in the O and TA in art. blg ; but in one copy of the S and in the TA in the present art., I find in its place EalayonaA , and so in the CK in art. blg , where the verb preceding it is erroneously written rufiEato ; and in the L, in the place of AlynA is put Ean~aA ; of all which three readings I prefer the first; though the last is agreeable with an explanation of rafaEotuhu given in the Msb and in the sentence next following;]) i. e. (assumed tropical:) Every company of men ( jamaAEap , S, TA), or person ( nafos , TA), that communicates, or announces, from us, (S, TA,) and makes known, [lit. traces up to us, ] what we say, (TA,) [or rather, aught of what is communicated, or announced, ] or [aught] of what is communicated, or announced, of the Kur-án and of the [ statutes, or ordinances, &c., termed ] sunan , (K in art. blg ,) or the meaning is mino *awiY AlbalaAgi , i. e., Alt~aboliygi , [ of those who have the office of communicating, or announcing, ] the simple subst. being put in the place of the inf. n., (T, O, K, TA, all in art. blg ,) let that company, or person, communicate, or announce, and relate, that I have forbidden [ its trees' being lopped, or being beaten with a stick in order that their leaves may fall off, ] referring to El-Medeeneh: (S, * TA:) but some relate it differently, saying, mina Albul~aAgi [ of the communicaters, or announcers, ] like Hud~aAv in the sense of muHad~ivuwn : (TA:) and some say, mina AlbilaAgi , meaning mn AlmubaAligiyna fiY Alt~aboliygi , i. e. of those who do their utmost in communicating, or announcing. (Hr, and K in art. blg .) ― -b12- [Hence,] rafaEotuhu [alone] signifies (tropical:) I made it known. (Msb.) You say, rafaEa Ealayohi kalaAmFA (assumed tropical:) [ He told, or related, a saying against him; informed against him ]. (S and K voce raq~aY , q. v.) And rafaEa EalaY AlEaAmili rafiyEapF (tropical:) He communicated, (S,) or made known, (Msb,) [or submitted, or referred, ] a case [ to the administrator of the law ]; (S;) and A_ilaY AlHaAkimi [ to the governor, or judge ]. (TA.) And rafaEotu AlA^amora A_ilaY Als~uloTiAni , inf. n. rufoEaAnN , (tropical:) I made known [or submitted, or referred, by way of appeal, ] the affair, or matter, to the Sultán. (Msb.) [See also 2.] ― -b13- [And hence, app.,] rufiEato lahu gaAyapN fasamaA lahaA (tropical:) [ An object to be reached, or accomplished, was proposed to him, and he aspired to it ]. (TA.) ― -b14- rafaEa AlbaEiyra , (Sb, K,) and Aln~aAqapa , (TA,) or rafaEa Aln~aAqapa fiY Als~ayori , and Ald~aAb~apa , (M in art. nS ,) inf. n. rafoEN , (TA in that art.,) (tropical:) He made the camel, (S, Msb, K,) and the she-camel, (TA,) and the beast, (M ubi suprà,) to exert himself, or herself, to the full, or to the utmost, or beyond measure, in going, or pace; (S, K, TA;) or to go quickly; (Msb;) or to go with the utmost celerity: (TA in art. nS :) or constrained him, or her, to go the pace termed marofuwE [q. v. infrà], (TA,) which is an inf. n. of the intrans. verb rafaEa [q. v. infrà] said of a camel (S, TA) and of a beast: (TA:) and ↓ rf~Ehu , (S, TA,) [and rf~EhA ,] and rf~E minohu , (TA,) [and minohaA ,] inf. n. tarofiyEN , signify the same: (S, TA:) or the phrase used by the Arabs is AirofaEo mino daAb~atika (tropical:) [ Make thou thy beast to exert itself, &c.]. (L, TA.) [You say also, app. in like manner, rafaEatoniY A^aroDN : or in this case the verb may have a different meaning: see an ex. in the first paragraph of art. xfD .] ― -b15- [Hence,] rafaEotuhu A_ilaY Had~i maA Einodahu mina AlEilomi (assumed tropical:) [ I urged him to tell the utmost of what he knew; ] (A in art. nS ;) i. e. I went to the utmost point [ with him ] in questioning him, or asking him. (TA in that art.) ― -b16- [ rafaEa Aln~aAra (assumed tropical:) He stirred up the fire; made it to burn up. ] ― -b17- rafaEati Aln~aAqapu labanahaA (tropical:) The she-camel [ drew up, or withdrew, or withheld, her milk; i. e.,] did not yield her milk: (A, TA:) and rafaEati All~ibaA^a fiY DaroEihaA (tropical:) [ She (a camel) drew up, & c., or refused to yield, the biestings in her udder ]. (As, S, K.) ― -b18- rafaEahu fiY xizaAnatihi , and Sunoduwqihi , (tropical:) He kept it, preserved it, laid it up, stowed it, or reposited it, in his repository, store-room, or closet, and his chest. (TA.) ― -b19- huwa laA yarofaEu AlEaSaA Eano EaAtiqihi , (Msb, TA,) or EaSaAhu En EAtqh , or Eano A^aholihi , (Mgh,) (tropical:) [lit. He does not put away the staff, or stick, or his staff, or stick, from his shoulder, or from his wife, ] is an allusion to discipline, chastisement, or punishment, (Mgh, TA,) or to severity thereof, (Msb,) and to beating (Mgh, TA) of women; (Mgh;) not meaning that the staff, or stick, is on the shoulder: (Msb:) or the first is an allusion to many journeyings. (TA.) ― -b20- rufiEa Alqalamu Eano valaAvK ; (Mgh, Msb;) so in the “ Firdows, ” on the authority of 'Alee and I' Ab and 'Áïsheh, meaning valaAvi A^anofusK ; (assumed tropical:) [ The pen of the recording angel is withheld from three persons;] a saying of Mohammad, which means that nothing is recorded either for or against three persons; (Mgh, Msb; *) these three being the sleeper until he awakes, the afflicted with disease or the like, or the demented, until he recovers, and the child until he becomes big, or attains to puberty. (El-Jámi' -es-Sagheer of Es-Suyootee; in which we find valaAvapK in the place of valaAvK .) This is like the saying next before mentioned; the pen having never been put [to the tablet to record aught] against the child. (Msb.) ― -b21- [ rafaEa often signifies (assumed tropical:) He withdrew, put away, removed, did away or did away with, annulled, revoked, or remitted. ] You say, Aall~`hum~a A@rofaEo Ean~aA h`*ihi AlD~ugoTapa (assumed tropical:) [ O God, withdraw, put away, or remove, from us this straitness, difficulty, distress, or affliction ]. (S in art. DgT .) [And in like manner also you say, rafaEa Eanohu AlEa*aAba (assumed tropical:) He withdrew, or put away, from him the punishment; he annulled, revoked, or remitted, his punishment. ] rafaEuwA AlHaroba [may also be rendered in a similar manner; (assumed tropical:) They gave over, or relinquished, war; as though they put it away; like waDaEuwhaA : but] is used by Moosà Ibn-Jábir [in the contr. sense, (assumed tropical:) they raised, or made, war; ] in opposition to wDEwhA . (Ham p. 180.) ― -b22- AixotalafuwA faqaAla baEoDuhumo narofaEu TariyqFA waqaAla baEoDuhumo laA narofaEu means (assumed tropical:) [ They disagreed; and some of them said, ] We will exclude a way, or passage, from among the portions, or shares, ( qisomp , [q. v.,]) of the land, or the house; and [ some of them said, ] We will not exclude it. (Mgh.) ― -b23- In the conventional language of the grammarians, rafoEN , in the inflection of words, is like Dam~N in the non-inflection. (S) [You say, rafaEa AlHarofa , aor. , inf. n. rafoEN , (assumed tropical:) He made the final letter to have or in its inflection. ] -A2- rafaEa Alqawomu (tropical:) The people, or company of men, went up, or upwards, through the countries, or lands. (As, K, TA.) ― -b2- rafaEa AlbaEiyru , (S, Msb, K,) fiY Als~ayori , (S,) or fiY sayorihi , (Msb, K,) inf. n. marofuwEN (Sb, S, TA) and rafoEN , (S, A, K, all in art. xfD ,) the former an inf. n. (Sb, S, TA) of the measure mafoEuwlN , (Sb, TA,) like [its contr. maxofuwDN , and] majoluwdN , and maEoquwlN , (S, TA,) and mawoDuwEN , (Sb, TA,) (tropical:) The camel exerted himself to the full, or to the utmost, or beyond measure, in going, or pace, or in his going, or his pace: (S, K, TA:) or was quick therein: (Msb:) or went the pace termed marofuwE , [q. v. infrà,] which is a running below that termed HuDor : (S, TA:) as though he had that [manner of going] which raised him, as well as that which lowered him. (Sb and TA with reference to the inf. n. mrfwE and mwDwE .) And rafaEuwA fiY masiyrihimo (assumed tropical:) They [namely men] rose above the [ easy and quick pace termed ] hamolajap in their going, or journeying. (ISk.) -A3- rafuEa , inf. n. rifoEapN ; (S, K;) or, accord. to Aboo-Bekr Mohammad Ibn-Es-Sereé, [so in two copies of the S, but in others, accord. to the TA, Ibn-EsSarráj,] they did not say rafuEa from rafiyEN in the sense of $ariyfN ; (S, O;) so says Sb; and he adds, but [they said] ↓ ArtfE ; (TA;) (tropical:) He (a man, S) was, or became, high, elevated, exalted, lofty, or eminent, in rank, condition, or state; (S, K, TA;) noble, honourable, glorious, or illustrious. (TA.) And rafuEa fiY Hasabihi wanasabihi (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, of high or exalted rank, or noble, or honourable, in his grounds of pretension to respect, and his relationship, or race, or lineage. rawSourceText: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. rafoEN , (S, Mgh, Msb,) He raised it: [this is generally the best rendering, as it serves to indicate several particular significations which will be found explained in what follows:] he elevated it; upraised it; uplifted it: he took it up: contr. of xafaDahu : (Msb:) or of waDaEahu : (S, Mgh, K:) as also ↓ rf~Ehu , (K,) inf. n. tarofiyEN ; (TA;) and ↓ ArtfEhu ; (K;) for accord. to the “ Nawádir, ” you say, ArtfEhu biyadihi and rafaEahu [ he raised it, lifted it, heaved it, or took it up, with his hand ]; but Az says that ArtfE is intrans., and that he has heard no authority for its being trans., in the sense of rafaEa , except that which he had read in the “ Nawádir el-Aaráb:” (TA:) rafoEN is sometimes applied to corporeal things, meaning the raising, or elevating, a thing from the resting-place thereof: sometimes to a building, meaning the rearing it, uprearing it, or making it high or lofty: (Er-Rághib:) or in relation to corporeal things, it is used properly to denote motion, and removal: (Msb:) it signifies the putting away or removing or turning back a thing after the coming or arriving thereof; like as dafoEN signifies the putting away or removing or turning back a thing before the coming or arriving [thereof]: (Kull p. 185:) but in relation to ideal things, it is [tropically used, as it is also in many other cases, and] accorded in meaning to what the case requires. (Msb.) [In its principal senses, proper and tropical, rafoEN agrees with the Latin Tollere. .] It is said in the Kur [ii. 60 and 87], rafaEonaA fawoqakumu A@lT~uwra We raised above you from its resting-place the mountain: and in the same [xii. 2], Aall~`hu A@l~a*iY rafaEa Als~am`waAti bigayori EamadK tarawonahaA [ God is He who raised the heavens without pillars that ye see; or, as ye see them ]: and in the same [ii. 121], waA_i*o yarofaEu A_ibor`hiymu AlqawaAEida mina Albayoti [ And when Abraham ] was rearing or uprearing or making high or lofty [ the foundations of the House of God, at Mekkeh]. (Er-Rághib.) And you say, AirofaEo h`*aA Take thou this: (Mgh:) or take it and carry it [ away; or take it up and remove it ]. (TA.) And rafaEa Alz~arEa , (Lh, K,) or rafaEahu A_ilaY Albayodari , (Msb,) aor. , (Lh,) inf. n. rafoEN (Lh, S) and rifaAEapN and rifaAEN [perhaps a mistranscription for rafaAEu , which see below], (Lh, TA,) He removed, or transported, the seed-produce from the place in which he had reaped it, (Lh,) or carried it after the reaping, (S, K,) to the place in which the grain was to be trodden out. (Lh, S, K.) [This last signification is said in the TA to be tropical; but according to a passage of the Msb quoted in the first sentence of this art., it is proper. In most of the phrases here following, the verb is undoubtedly used tropically.] ― -b2- rafaEuwA A_ilaY~a Euyuwnahumo (tropical:) [ They raised towards me their eyes ]. (TA.) ― -b3- daxalotu EalaY fulaAnK falamo yarofaEo biY raA^osFA (Mgh, TA *) (tropical:) I went in to such a one, and he did not look towards me, nor pay any regard, or attention, to me. (Mgh.) [ biY is not here a mistake for liY , for the phrase is often found thus written.] ― -b4- rufiEa liYa Al$~aYo'u (assumed tropical:) [ The thing was, as it were, raised into view, i. e. it rose into view, to me; ] I saw the thing from afar. (TA.) ― -b5- rafaEa Als~araAbu Al$~axoSa , aor. , inf. n. rafoEN , (tropical:) The mirage raised, or elevated [ to the eye, (see an ex. near the end of the first paragraph of art. zwl )] the figure of a man or some other thing seen from a distance; [or it may be allowable to render it, made it to appear tall, and as though quivering, vibrating, or playing up and down; ] syn. zahaAhu [of which, when it relates to the mirage, the meaning is best expressed by the latter of the two explanations here given]. (TA.) ― -b6- warafaEonaA baEoDahumo fawoqa baEoDK darajaAtK , in the Kur [xliii. 31], means (assumed tropical:) And we have exalted some of them above others in degrees of rank, or station: and narofaEu darajaAtK mano na$aA='u , in the same, [vi. 83, and xii. 76,] (assumed tropical:) We exalt in degrees of rank, or station, whom We please: (Er-Rághib:) and waA@ll~`hu yarofaEu mano ya$aA='u wayaxofiDu (assumed tropical:) And God exalteth whom He pleaseth, and abaseth: (S and TA:) and [in like manner,] rafoEu Al*~ikori means the exalting of one's fame; as in the Kur xciv. 4. (Er-Rághib.) But the words, waA_ilaY Als~amaA='i kayofa rufiEato , in the Kur [lxxxviii. 18], indicate two meanings; And to the heaven, how it is elevated in respect of its place; and (assumed tropical:) how it is exalted in respect of excellence, and exaltation of rank. (Er-Rághib.) [In like manner also,] fiY buyuwtK A^a*ina A@ll~`hu A^ano turofaEa , in the Kur [xxiv. 36], means In houses which God hath permitted to be built; (Bd, TA;) accord. to some: (TA:) or, (assumed tropical:) to be honoured; (Zj, Bd;) so says El-Hasan; (Zj;) or, (assumed tropical:) to be exalted in estimation. (Er-Rághib.) It is said in a trad., A_in~a A@ll~`ha yarofaEu AlEadola wayaxofiDuhu (assumed tropical:) Verily God exalteth the just, and maketh him to have the ascendency over the unjust, and at one time abaseth him, so that He maketh the unjust to overcome him, in order to try his creatures, in the present world. (Az, TA.) [See also art. xfD .] And you say, rafaEahu EalaY SaAHibihi fiY Almajolisi (assumed tropical:) He advanced him above his companion [ in the sitting-place, or sitting-room, or assembly ]. (TA.) And rafaEotuka Eano ka*aA (assumed tropical:) [ I exalted thee, or held thee, above such a thing ]: (M voce rabaA^a :) and A_in~iY laA^arofaEoka Eano h`*aA AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) [ Verily I exalt thee, or hold thee, above this thing ]. (S voce rabaA^a , q. v.) ― -b7- rafaEa A@ll~`hu Eamalahu (assumed tropical:) [ God honoured his work by acceptance; or] God accepted his work. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xxxv. 11], waA@loEamalu AlS~aAliHu yarofaEuhu (assumed tropical:) And righteous work He will accept: (Jel:) or the meaning is yarofaEu AlEamalu AlS~aAliHu Alkalima AlT~ay~aba (assumed tropical:) [ righteous work will cause praise, or the like, (mentioned immediately before the above-cited words of the Kur,) to ascend, and obtain acceptance ]: (Mujáhid, TA:) Katádeh says, [that the meaning is,] speech will not be accepted without work. (TA.) ― -b8- rafoEN Also signifies (assumed tropical:) The bringing a thing near; or presenting, or offering, it; syn. taqoriybN . (S.) And hence, rafaEotuhu A_ilaY Als~uloTaAni , (S, Mgh, K,) and A_ilaY AlHakami , (TA,) inf. n. rafoEN (S, * TA) and rufoEaAnN (S, K) and rifoEaAnN , (TA,) (tropical:) I presented him to, or brought him before, or brought him forward to, the Sultán, (S, * Mgh, * K, * TA,) and the judge, to arraign him and contest with him: (TA:) and A_ilaY AlHaAkimi ↓ raAfaEahu , (S K,) inf. n. muraAfaEapN , (TA,) [in like manner] signifies (tropical:) he preferred a complaint against him to the governor, or judge: (K:) or (tropical:) he presented him to, or brought him before, or brought him forward to, the governor, or judge, to arraign him and contest with him, and preferred a complaint against him: (TA:) [or it denotes the doing so mutually; for, accord. to Mtr,] xaSomahu A_ilaY Als~uloTaAni ↓ raAfaEa signifies (tropical:) he brought his adversary before the Sultán ( qar~abahu A_ilayohi ), the latter doing the same with him. (Mgh.) [See also 2.] ― -b9- rafaEa AlquroA=na EalaY Als~uloTaAni (tropical:) [ He adduced, or brought forward, the Kur-án against the Sultán; ] he interpreted the Kur-án against the Sultán, and judged thereby that he should rebel against him. (TA.) ― -b10- rafoEotu Alr~ajula also signifies (tropical:) I traced up the man's lineage to his greatest ancestor; or I mentioned his lineage, saying, He is such a one the son of such a one, or He is of such a tribe, or city, &c.; syn. namayotuhu , and nasabotuhu . (TA.) ― -b11- And hence, rafaEa AlHadiyva A_ilaY Aln~abiY~i (tropical:) [ He traced up, or ascribed, or attributed, the tradition to the Prophet, mentioning, in ascending order, the persons by whom it had been handed down, up to the Prophet; in the manner more fully explained in the sentence here next following]. (TA.) You say also, rafaEa AlHadiyva A_ilaY qaAy^ilihi , meaning A^asonadahu [i. e. (assumed tropical:) He traced up, or ascribed, or attributed, the tradition to the author thereof, by mentioning him, or by mentioning, uninterruptedly, in ascending order, the persons by whom it had been transmitted, up to the Prophet; or by mentioning the person who had related it to him from the Prophet if only one person intervened, saying, “ Such a one told me, from such a one, ” ( and so on if more than one intervened between him and the Prophet, ) “ from the Apostle of God; ” or with an interruption in the mention of the persons by whom it had been transmitted ]. (S * and Msb in art. snd .) [And hence what next follows.] It is said in a trad., rafaEato A_ilayonaA mina AlbalaAgi ↓ kul~u raAfiEapK faqado Har~amotuhaA A^ano tuEoDada A^awotuxobaTa , (S, * TA, [in a very old and excellent copy of the former of which I find, as above, A_ilayonaA , and so in some copies of the K and in the O and TA in art. blg ; but in one copy of the S and in the TA in the present art., I find in its place EalayonaA , and so in the CK in art. blg , where the verb preceding it is erroneously written rufiEato ; and in the L, in the place of AlynA is put Ean~aA ; of all which three readings I prefer the first; though the last is agreeable with an explanation of rafaEotuhu given in the Msb and in the sentence next following;]) i. e. (assumed tropical:) Every company of men ( jamaAEap , S, TA), or person ( nafos , TA), that communicates, or announces, from us, (S, TA,) and makes known, [lit. traces up to us, ] what we say, (TA,) [or rather, aught of what is communicated, or announced, ] or [aught] of what is communicated, or announced, of the Kur-án and of the [ statutes, or ordinances, &c., termed ] sunan , (K in art. blg ,) or the meaning is mino *awiY AlbalaAgi , i. e., Alt~aboliygi , [ of those who have the office of communicating, or announcing, ] the simple subst. being put in the place of the inf. n., (T, O, K, TA, all in art. blg ,) let that company, or person, communicate, or announce, and relate, that I have forbidden [ its trees' being lopped, or being beaten with a stick in order that their leaves may fall off, ] referring to El-Medeeneh: (S, * TA:) but some relate it differently, saying, mina Albul~aAgi [ of the communicaters, or announcers, ] like Hud~aAv in the sense of muHad~ivuwn : (TA:) and some say, mina AlbilaAgi , meaning mn AlmubaAligiyna fiY Alt~aboliygi , i. e. of those who do their utmost in communicating, or announcing. (Hr, and K in art. blg .) ― -b12- [Hence,] rafaEotuhu [alone] signifies (tropical:) I made it known. (Msb.) You say, rafaEa Ealayohi kalaAmFA (assumed tropical:) [ He told, or related, a saying against him; informed against him ]. (S and K voce raq~aY , q. v.) And rafaEa EalaY AlEaAmili rafiyEapF (tropical:) He communicated, (S,) or made known, (Msb,) [or submitted, or referred, ] a case [ to the administrator of the law ]; (S;) and A_ilaY AlHaAkimi [ to the governor, or judge ]. (TA.) And rafaEotu AlA^amora A_ilaY Als~uloTiAni , inf. n. rufoEaAnN , (tropical:) I made known [or submitted, or referred, by way of appeal, ] the affair, or matter, to the Sultán. (Msb.) [See also 2.] ― -b13- [And hence, app.,] rufiEato lahu gaAyapN fasamaA lahaA (tropical:) [ An object to be reached, or accomplished, was proposed to him, and he aspired to it ]. (TA.) ― -b14- rafaEa AlbaEiyra , (Sb, K,) and Aln~aAqapa , (TA,) or rafaEa Aln~aAqapa fiY Als~ayori , and Ald~aAb~apa , (M in art. nS ,) inf. n. rafoEN , (TA in that art.,) (tropical:) He made the camel, (S, Msb, K,) and the she-camel, (TA,) and the beast, (M ubi suprà,) to exert himself, or herself, to the full, or to the utmost, or beyond measure, in going, or pace; (S, K, TA;) or to go quickly; (Msb;) or to go with the utmost celerity: (TA in art. nS :) or constrained him, or her, to go the pace termed marofuwE [q. v. infrà], (TA,) which is an inf. n. of the intrans. verb rafaEa [q. v. infrà] said of a camel (S, TA) and of a beast: (TA:) and ↓ rf~Ehu , (S, TA,) [and rf~EhA ,] and rf~E minohu , (TA,) [and minohaA ,] inf. n. tarofiyEN , signify the same: (S, TA:) or the phrase used by the Arabs is AirofaEo mino daAb~atika (tropical:) [ Make thou thy beast to exert itself, &c.]. (L, TA.) [You say also, app. in like manner, rafaEatoniY A^aroDN : or in this case the verb may have a different meaning: see an ex. in the first paragraph of art. xfD .] ― -b15- [Hence,] rafaEotuhu A_ilaY Had~i maA Einodahu mina AlEilomi (assumed tropical:) [ I urged him to tell the utmost of what he knew; ] (A in art. nS ;) i. e. I went to the utmost point [ with him ] in questioning him, or asking him. (TA in that art.) ― -b16- [ rafaEa Aln~aAra (assumed tropical:) He stirred up the fire; made it to burn up. ] ― -b17- rafaEati Aln~aAqapu labanahaA (tropical:) The she-camel [ drew up, or withdrew, or withheld, her milk; i. e.,] did not yield her milk: (A, TA:) and rafaEati All~ibaA^a fiY DaroEihaA (tropical:) [ She (a camel) drew up, & c., or refused to yield, the biestings in her udder ]. (As, S, K.) ― -b18- rafaEahu fiY xizaAnatihi , and Sunoduwqihi , (tropical:) He kept it, preserved it, laid it up, stowed it, or reposited it, in his repository, store-room, or closet, and his chest. (TA.) ― -b19- huwa laA yarofaEu AlEaSaA Eano EaAtiqihi , (Msb, TA,) or EaSaAhu En EAtqh , or Eano A^aholihi , (Mgh,) (tropical:) [lit. He does not put away the staff, or stick, or his staff, or stick, from his shoulder, or from his wife, ] is an allusion to discipline, chastisement, or punishment, (Mgh, TA,) or to severity thereof, (Msb,) and to beating (Mgh, TA) of women; (Mgh;) not meaning that the staff, or stick, is on the shoulder: (Msb:) or the first is an allusion to many journeyings. (TA.) ― -b20- rufiEa Alqalamu Eano valaAvK ; (Mgh, Msb;) so in the “ Firdows, ” on the authority of 'Alee and I' Ab and 'Áïsheh, meaning valaAvi A^anofusK ; (assumed tropical:) [ The pen of the recording angel is withheld from three persons;] a saying of Mohammad, which means that nothing is recorded either for or against three persons; (Mgh, Msb; *) these three being the sleeper until he awakes, the afflicted with disease or the like, or the demented, until he recovers, and the child until he becomes big, or attains to puberty. (El-Jámi' -es-Sagheer of Es-Suyootee; in which we find valaAvapK in the place of valaAvK .) This is like the saying next before mentioned; the pen having never been put [to the tablet to record aught] against the child. (Msb.) ― -b21- [ rafaEa often signifies (assumed tropical:) He withdrew, put away, removed, did away or did away with, annulled, revoked, or remitted. ] You say, Aall~`hum~a A@rofaEo Ean~aA h`*ihi AlD~ugoTapa (assumed tropical:) [ O God, withdraw, put away, or remove, from us this straitness, difficulty, distress, or affliction ]. (S in art. DgT .) [And in like manner also you say, rafaEa Eanohu AlEa*aAba (assumed tropical:) He withdrew, or put away, from him the punishment; he annulled, revoked, or remitted, his punishment. ] rafaEuwA AlHaroba [may also be rendered in a similar manner; (assumed tropical:) They gave over, or relinquished, war; as though they put it away; like waDaEuwhaA : but] is used by Moosà Ibn-Jábir [in the contr. sense, (assumed tropical:) they raised, or made, war; ] in opposition to wDEwhA . (Ham p. 180.) ― -b22- AixotalafuwA faqaAla baEoDuhumo narofaEu TariyqFA waqaAla baEoDuhumo laA narofaEu means (assumed tropical:) [ They disagreed; and some of them said, ] We will exclude a way, or passage, from among the portions, or shares, ( qisomp , [q. v.,]) of the land, or the house; and [ some of them said, ] We will not exclude it. (Mgh.) ― -b23- In the conventional language of the grammarians, rafoEN , in the inflection of words, is like Dam~N in the non-inflection. (S) [You say, rafaEa AlHarofa , aor. , inf. n. rafoEN , (assumed tropical:) He made the final letter to have or in its inflection. ] -A2- rafaEa Alqawomu (tropical:) The people, or company of men, went up, or upwards, through the countries, or lands. (As, K, TA.) ― -b2- rafaEa AlbaEiyru , (S, Msb, K,) fiY Als~ayori , (S,) or fiY sayorihi , (Msb, K,) inf. n. marofuwEN (Sb, S, TA) and rafoEN , (S, A, K, all in art. xfD ,) the former an inf. n. (Sb, S, TA) of the measure mafoEuwlN , (Sb, TA,) like [its contr. maxofuwDN , and] majoluwdN , and maEoquwlN , (S, TA,) and mawoDuwEN , (Sb, TA,) (tropical:) The camel exerted himself to the full, or to the utmost, or beyond measure, in going, or pace, or in his going, or his pace: (S, K, TA:) or was quick therein: (Msb:) or went the pace termed marofuwE , [q. v. infrà,] which is a running below that termed HuDor : (S, TA:) as though he had that [manner of going] which raised him, as well as that which lowered him. (Sb and TA with reference to the inf. n. mrfwE and mwDwE .) And rafaEuwA fiY masiyrihimo (assumed tropical:) They [namely men] rose above the [ easy and quick pace termed ] hamolajap in their going, or journeying. (ISk.) -A3- rafuEa , inf. n. rifoEapN ; (S, K;) or, accord. to Aboo-Bekr Mohammad Ibn-Es-Sereé, [so in two copies of the S, but in others, accord. to the TA, Ibn-EsSarráj,] they did not say rafuEa from rafiyEN in the sense of $ariyfN ; (S, O;) so says Sb; and he adds, but [they said] ↓ ArtfE ; (TA;) (tropical:) He (a man, S) was, or became, high, elevated, exalted, lofty, or eminent, in rank, condition, or state; (S, K, TA;) noble, honourable, glorious, or illustrious. (TA.) And rafuEa fiY Hasabihi wanasabihi (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, of high or exalted rank, or noble, or honourable, in his grounds of pretension to respect, and his relationship, or race, or lineage. (Msb.) ― -b2- rafuEa Alv~awobu (assumed tropical:) The garment, or piece of cloth, was fine, fine in texture, delicate, or thin. (Msb.) ― -b3- rafuEa , (S, K,) inf. n. rafaAEapN , (K,) (tropical:) He (a man, S) was, or became, high, or loud, ( rafiyE ,) in voice. (S, K.) [See rafaAEapN below.]

(Lth, K.)

definition: It became raised;
sourceDefinition: It became raised; or it rose: it rose high, or became high or elevated or lofty: [ it became raised, upraised, uplifted, or elevated, or it rose, from its resting-place: and, said of a building, it became reared, upreared, or made high or lofty: ] it became taken up: [ it became taken away, put away, or removed; or it went away; after its coming or arriving: thus when said of corporeal things: but when said of ideal things, it is tropically used, as it is also in many other cases, and accorded in meaning to what the case requires:] quasi-pass. of rafaEahu as signifying the contr. of waDaEahu . (S, K.) [See 1; first sentence.] ― -b2- It (the water of a well) rose, by its becoming copious: and also it went away: (A in art. qlS :) [in which latter sense, likewise, it is said of milk in the udder; or as meaning it became drawn up, or withdrawn, or withheld: see 1. See also a usage of this verb voce raqaA^a .] ― -b3- (tropical:) Said of a man: see 1, voce rafuEa , near the end of the paragraph. ― -b4- ArtfE qadoruhu (tropical:) [ His rank became high, elevated, exalted, lofty, or eminent ]. (S, TA.) ― -b5- AirotafiEo , said to a man entering a sittingplace, sitting-room, or assembly, means (tropical:) Advance thou: it is not from AirotifaAEN denoting height. (TA.) ― -b6- See also 5. ― -b7- ArtfEt AlD~uHaY (tropical:) [ The morning became advanced; meaning] the sun became high: AlD~uHaY being originally a pl., namely, of AlD~aHowapu ; [wherefore the verb is fem.;] but afterwards used as a sing. [as in the next ex. here following]. (Msb.) You say also, AlD~uHaY ↓ taraf~aEa (tropical:) [meaning the same]. (TA.) And ArtfE Aln~ahaAru (assumed tropical:) [ The day became advanced, the sun being somewhat high: a phrase said by the doctors of the law in the present day to be employed when the sun has risen the measure of a rumoH or more]. (S and K in art. mtE ; &c.) ― -b8- ArtfE Als~iEoru waA@noHaT~a (tropical:) [ The price rose, or advanced, and became low, or abated ]. (TA.) ― -b9- [ ArtfEwA (assumed tropical:) They removed from, or to, a place. ― -b10- ArtfE Eanohu , said of a disease, pain, an affliction, and the like, (assumed tropical:) It quitted him; became withdrawn from him. ] ― -b11- Aln~aqiyDaAni laA yajotamiEaAni walaA yarotafiEaAni (assumed tropical:) [ What are termed nqyDAn cannot be coexistent in the same thing, nor simul taneously nonexistent in the same thing ]; as existence itself and nonexistence, and motion and rest. definition: [ A certain shrub, resembling a dwarftamarisk;
sourceDefinition: [ A certain shrub, resembling a dwarftamarisk; ] a certain pasture of camels; (S, A, Msb, K;) a species of tree [or shrub ], (T,) of the kind termed HamoD , (T, S, A, Msb, K,) growing in plain, or soft, ground, (Msb,) the leaves of which fall, [or droop ], like the A^u$onaAn [i. e. kali, or glasswort ]; eagerly desired by the camels when they are satiated with, and tired of, the [ sweet pasture termed ] xul~ap : (T:) it is a species of tree [or shrub ] resembling that called gaDFA , (M, K,) which does not grow tall, but the leaves of which spread, [app. meaning that its sprigs spread out flat, and (as described above) droop, like those of the common tamarisk, ] and it resembles the A^u$onaAn : (M:) like the gDA and A$nAn , it is burned for making qiloY [or potash ]: (TA &c. in art. qlY :) AHn says that it has long and slender hadab [generally, and app. here, meaning sprigs garnished with minute leaves overlying one another like the scales of a fish ], and is a pasture upon which camels and sheep or goats will live when they have nothing else with it; sometimes there comes forth upon it a white honey, [ a species of manna, ] resembling jumaAn [i. e. pearls, or silver beads like pearls ], very sweet; it affords firewood, and wood for other uses; its kindled firewood is hot; and its smoke is beneficial as a remedy for the rheum: AHn also says in one place, that, accord. to certain of the Basrees, the rmv occupies the space of a man sitting, and grows in the manner of the $iyH [ a species of wormwood ]: also that he had been told by certain of [the tribe of] Benoo-Asad that it rises not so high as the stature of a man, and is used as firewood: (M, TA:) [a coll. gen. n.:] the n. un. is with p . (T, M.) [See a prov. cited voce *uw^onuwnN , in art. *A^n .] ― -b2- Also A man whose clothes are old and worn out: (A, K:) said by MF to be tropical, but not said to be so in the A. (TA.) ― -b3- And Weak in the maton [i. e. the back, or the flesh on either side of the back-bone ]. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. yaruwgu , (S, Msb,) inf. n. rawogN (S, Msb, K) and rawagaAnN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) said of a fox, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and of a man, (K,) He turned aside or away from a thing: (K:) or went this way and that, (Mgh,) or to the right and left, quickly, (Msb,) and deceitfully, or guilefully: (Mgh, Msb:) [or turned aside to deceive him who was behind him: for] the primary signification of rawogN is the turning aside to deceive him who is behind one. (Er-Rághib, TA.) It is said in a prov., ruwgiY jaEaAri wa A@noZuriY A^ayona Almafiro [for Almafir~u , i. e. Turn aside or away, or go this way and that, &c., O she-hyena, and look where is the place to which to flee: or, as some relate it, the first word is ruwEiY : see art. jEr ]. (S, TA. [Freytag seems to have found AlmEz for Almfr ; and has explained ruwgiY jaEaAri as meaning “ Vide ubi capræ sint, hyæna! ”]) And you say, rAg AlS~ayodu The game, or object of the chase, went away this way and that, or hither and thither. (TA. [There said to be tropical; but I see not wherefore.]) And one says, rAg Eano fulaAnK He turned aside, or away, from such a one [and particularly with deceit or guile; eluded him; dodged him ]. (JK.) And huwa yaruwgu Eani AlHaq~i [ He deviates from the truth, or from that which is right or just ]. (TA.) And rAg AlT~ariyqu The road turned aside or away, or deviated. (Msb.) And rAg mino ka*aA He turned away from such a thing, and returned, concealing his return: (Har p. 21:) [for,] accord. to Fr, rAg is not said of one who has returned unless he concealed his return. (Har ibid., and TA.) And rAg A_ilaY ka*aA , (S, Msb,) or AlY fulaAnK , (TA,) He turned aside (S, Msb, TA) to such a thing, (S, Msb,) or to such a one, (TA,) secretly. (S, Msb, TA.) Hence, in the Kur [li. 26], farAga A_ilaY A^aholihi fajaA='a biEijolK samiynK And he turned aside, (Jel, TA,) or went away, (Bd,) to his family secretly [ and brought a fat calf ]: (Bd, Jel, TA:) or he returned to his family concealing his return. (Fr, TA.) And in the Kur [xxxvii. 91], faraAga Ealayohimo DarobFA biA@loyamiyni And he turned against them (Fr, S, Bd, TA) secretly, (Bd, TA,) smiting them with the right hand, or because of the oath that he had sworn; (Bd;) as though the rawog in this case consisted in his employing a pretext against them in order that he might do to their gods what he did: (S, L:) or the meaning is, he advanced against them. (S, TA.) ― -b2- rAg HaAjapF A_ilaY fulaAnK , aor. as above, He sought to obtain quickly an object of want of such a one. (JK, TA. [See also 4.]

definition: , (MA, TA,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (MA, TA,) inf. n. muraAwagapN (KL, TA) and riwaAgN , (TA,) He practised deceit, delusion, guile, or artifice, (MA, KL, TA,) with him, or towards him; (MA, TA;) or strove, endeavoured, or desired, to deceive, delude, beguile, circumvent, or outwit, him; syn. xaAdaEahu ; as also ↓ ArAghu , inf. n. A_iraAgapN : and both signify he endeavoured to turn him; or endeavoured to turn him by blandishment, or by deceitful arts, or to entice him to turn; syn. raAwadahu . (TA.) It is said when its object is a person who has turned away from, or shunned, or avoided, that which one has devised, planned, or plotted, against him. (TA.) You say, fulaAnN yuraAwigu fiY AlA^amori [ Such a one practises deceit, &c., in the affair ], inf. n. muraAwagapN . (S.) And maA zilotu A^uraAwiguhu Eano ka*aA I ceased not to endeavour to turn him, or to entice him to turn, from such a thing, syn. A^uraAwiduhu ; (TA in this art;) and Ealayohi to it: (TA in art. mnE :) and [in like manner] you say, EalaY A^amorK ↓ fulaAnN yuriyguniY Such a one endeavours to turn me, or to entice me to turn, to a thing; and Eano A^amorK from a thing; syn. yuraAwiduniY ; and seeks, or demands, my doing so. (TA.) ― -b2- muraAwagapN also signifies The act of wrestling together; (S, K;) like ↓ taraAwugN . (K.) You say, raAwghu He wrestled with him: (TK:) or rwAg baEoDuhumo baEoDFA One of them wrestled with another; [or they wrestled, one with another; or they wrestled together; ] as also ↓ trAwgwA . (S, TA.)

[ A^ariyguwniY A_iraAgatakumo is expl. in one of my two copies of the S by the words AuTolubuwniY Talibatakumo : in the other of those copies, the latter of these words is written Tlibtakm : I think that the right reading is Tilobatakumo ; and the meaning, Seek ye me with, or in, your mode, or manner, of seeking: the proper meaning is seek ye me with your seeking. ] Khálid Ibn-Jaafar Ibn-Kiláb says, speaking of his mare Hi*oqap , A^ariyguwniY A_iraAgatakumo faA_in~iY wa Hi*oqapa kaAl$~ajaA taHota Alwariydi [ Seek ye me with your seeking; but ye will not be able to take me; for I, with Hidhkah, am like the bone sticking fast in the throat beneath the carotid artery ]. (TA.) And you say, A^aragotu AlS~ayoda [ I sought, or pursued, the game, or object of the chase ]. (S.) And ArAgt AlEuqaAbu AlS~ayoda The eagle pursued the game this way and that, as the latter went. (Mgh and TA in art. hwY .) And xarajotu A^uriygu baEiyrFA $arada min~iY I went forth seeking in every road, or way, a camel that had run away from me. (TA, from a trad.) And maA *aA turiygu What is this that thou seekest and desirest? or that which thou seekest and desirest? (S, TA.) And fulaAnN yuriygu ka*aA wa ka*aA Such a one eeks, and devises or plans or plots, such and such things. (T, TA.)

definition: [ Wont to turn aside or away from a thing: or to go this way and that, or to the right and left, quickly, and deceitfully, or guilefully: or to turn aside for the purpose of deceiving him who is behind: or to elude, or dodge ].
sourceDefinition: [ Wont to turn aside or away from a thing: or to go this way and that, or to the right and left, quickly, and deceitfully, or guilefully: or to turn aside for the purpose of deceiving him who is behind: or to elude, or dodge ]. Mo'áwiyeh said to 'Abd-Allah Ibn-Ez-Zubeyr, A_in~amaA A^anota vaEolabN raw~aAgN kul~amaA xarajota mino juHorK A@nojaHarota fiY juHorK [ Thou art only a fox wont to elude: whenever thou comest forth from a burrow, thou enterest into a burrow ]. (TA.) [Hence,] Alr~aw~aAgu is an appellation of The fox. (JK, K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yazobiyhi , (S, K,) inf. n. zaboYN , (S,) i. q. Hamalahu [ He bore it, carried it, took it up and carried it, conveyed it, &c.]; (S, K;) namely, a thing; (S;) as also ↓ AizodabaAhu ; thus accord. to the T and S and M; (TA; [accord. to one of my copies of the S, i. q. AHtmlhu , which is often syn. with Hamalahu ];) or ↓ A^azobaAhu ; thus in the copies of the K: (TA:) or the first and ↓ last signify he bore upon his back a heavy burden: (JM:) and hence the saying of Kaab, bi*`lika ↓ faqulotu lahu kalimapF A^uzobiyhi (JM, TA) i. e. [(assumed tropical:) And I said to him a saying, ] disquieting, or disturbing, him, (JM, TA, *) [ by reason of that: ] because, when a thing is borne, or carried, it is removed from its place. (JM.) ― -b2- Also, (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) He drove, urged, or incited, him; (K, TA;) and so ↓ zb~Ahu , (K,) inf. n. tazobiyapN ; (TA;) and ↓ AzdbAh . (K.) [And i. q. daEaAhu .] You say, maA zabaAhumo A_ilaY h`*aA , i. e. maA daEaAhumo A_ilayohi [ What drew, led, induced, caused, constrained, or drove, them to this? or What hath led, &c.?]. (JM, TA.) And ↓ zab~aY lahu $ar~FA , inf. n. tazobiyapN , i. e. daEaAhu [ He drew, or caused, evil to him ]. (TA.) And lahu ↓ zab~ayotu , inf. n. tazobiyapN , I prepared [app. evil] for him. (TA.) And zabaAhu bi$ar~K , (K, TA,) or bimakoruwhK , (TA,) He smote him with evil. (K, TA.)

definition: A hill, or an elevated piece of ground, which the water does not overflow: (S, K:) pl.
sourceDefinition: A hill, or an elevated piece of ground, which the water does not overflow: (S, K:) pl. rubFY . (S, TA.) Hence, (TA,) it is said in a prov., balaga Als~ayolu Alz~ubaY [ The torrent reached the tops of the hills which they do not usually overflow ]: (S, TA:) or Alz~ubaY is here pl. of Alz~uboyapu in the sense next following: [but the meaning is virtually the same:] (Meyd:) the prov. is applied to a thing, or an affair, or a case, exceeding the ordinary bounds or limit. (Meyd, TA.) ― -b2- A pitfall for a lion (S, Mgh, Msb, K) or a wolf (Mgh) &c., (Msb,) dug in a high place, (S, Mgh, Msb,) for which reason it is thus called: (S:) pl. as above. (Msb.) ― -b3- A hollow dug in the ground, in which a sportsman conceals himself [ from the objects of the chase ]. (TA.) ― -b4- A hollow dug in the ground, in which one roasts, or broils, for himself, and bakes bread. (ISd, TA.) ― -b5- A well: so where it is said in a trad. of an Arab of the desert, tarad~aY fiY zuboyapK [ He fell into a well ]. (Mgh.) ― -b6- The excavation made by ants; which they make not save in a high place. (TA.) ― -b7- Some include this word among those that have contr. significations. (TA.)

definition: Quickness, and briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness: (S, K:) [originally A^uzobuwYN ,] of the measure A^ufoEuwlN .
sourceDefinition: Quickness, and briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness: (S, K:) [originally A^uzobuwYN ,] of the measure A^ufoEuwlN . (S) ― -b2- A certain mode of going, or pace, (S, M, K,) of camels: (M, TA:) accord. to As, A^azaAbiY~u , which is its pl., signifies various modes of going or pace. (S.) ― -b3- Evil: (AZ, S:) or a great evil: (K:) and a great, momentous, or terrible, thing or affair: (AZ, S, K:) pl. as above. (AZ, S.) One says, laqiytu minohu AlA^azaAbiY~a I experienced from him, or it, evils; and great, momentous, or terrible, things. (AZ, S.) ― -b4- And i. q. EajabN [app. as meaning A wonderful thing ]. (TA.) ― -b5- And The sound of a bow; (JM, TA; *) its musical ringing, or plaintive, sound. (JM.)

definition: , (Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. zaHomN (Msb, K) and zaHomapN (Msb) and ziHaAmN , with kesr; (K; [but see what here follows, and see also zaHomapN below;] and ↓ zAHmhu , (S, Msb, TA,) inf. n. muzaAHamapN (Msb, TA) and ziHaAmN ; (Msb;) i. q. DaAyaqahu [i. e. He straitened him, meaning, in this instance, by pressure; and properly, being in like manner straitened by him ]: (K in explanation of zaHamahu , and TA in explanation of zAHmhu :) or i. q. dafaEahu [ he pushed him, or repelled him ]; generally meaning [ he pushed against him ] in a strait, or narrow, [or crowded,] place: (Msb in explanation of zaHamahu , and app. in explanation of zAHmhu also:) [or i. q. daAfaEahu , which often signifies the same as dafaEahu ; but more properly, he pushed him, &c., being pushed, &c., by him: for] zaHamaniYa Aln~aAsu means daAfaEuwniY [i. e. The people pushed against me; or pushed me, &c., being pushed, &c., by me; ] in a strait, or narrow, [or crowded,] place: (Mgh:) [or pressed, crowded, or thronged, me: ] and muzaAHamapN is syn. with mudaAfaEapN : (TA in art. dfE :) ↓ AizodaHamahu in the place of zaHamahu is a mistake. (Mgh.) One says, zaHama Alqawomu baEoDuhumo baEoDFA The people straitened one another; syn. taDaAyaquwA ; [or pressed, crowded, or thronged, one another; ] in a sitting-place, or place of assembly: (Msb:) as also ↓ AzdHmwA , (Msb, K, * TA,) in whatever place it be; (Msb;) and ↓ tzAHmwA . (K, * TA.) One may also use the pass. form of zaHama , i. e. zuHima [meaning He was straitened, by pressure; &c.]; and that of zaAHama , i. e. ↓ zuwHima [meaning the same]. (Msb.) -A2- ↓ zaHima zuHomapF He gobbled a gobbet, or morsel, or mouthful: so in the “ Nawádir; ” as also zahimahaA . (TA.) 3: see above, in two places. ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, zaAHama EalaY Alr~iy^aAsapi waA^araAdahaA (assumed tropical:) [ He strove for headship, or command, and desired it ]. (IAar, TA in art. rA^s .) [And hence the prov. zaAHim biEawodK A^awo daEo : see art. Ewd .] ― -b3- [Hence, likewise,] zAHmhu also signifies (assumed tropical:) He treated him, or behaved towards him, with roughness, rudeness, hardness, harshness, or ill-nature. (TA. [I find this explanation noted down by me as taken from the TA, but without any reference to the art. from which I obtained it. It is not in the present art.]) ― -b4- zAHm Alxamosiyna He (a man, TA) approached, (K, TA,) and reached, or attained, (TA,) the [age of] fifty [years]; (K, TA;) as also zaAhamahaA . (TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb,) aor. , (Msb, MS, JM, [not mentioned in the S nor in the K, app. because well known,]) inf. n. zaEomN and zuEomN and zEomN , (S, Msb, K,) the first of the dial. of El-Hijáz, (Msb, TA,) the second of the dial. of [the tribe of] Asad, (Msb,) or Benoo-Temeem, (TA,) and the third of the dial. of some of [the tribe of] Keys; (Msb;) [generally best rendered He asserted; for it mostly relates to a thing not certainly known: or] he said; (S, Msb, K;) as in the phrases zaEamati AlHanafiy~apN [ The Hanafees said or asserted, or have said or asserted, ] and zaEama siybawayohi [ Seebaweyh said or asserted, or has said or asserted ]; (Msb;) [and zaEama A^an~ahu ka*aA He said, or asserted, that it was thus; ] either truly or falsely: (K:) mostly used in relation to a thing respecting which there is doubt, (Sh, Az, Msb, K,) and which is not certainly known: (Sh, Az, Msb:) or it is mostly used in relation to that which is false, or that respecting which there is doubt, or suspicion: (El-Marzookee, Msb:) or, as those skilled in the language of the Arabs say, in relation to a thing of which the speaker doubts, and does not know whether it may not be false: (Lth:) or zaEama zaEomFA means he related a piece of information not knowing whether it were true or false. (IKoot, Msb.) Hence the saying, zaEama maTiy~apu Alka*ibi [i. e. (assumed tropical:) zaEama is the conveyer, or vehicle, (properly the camel, or beast, that serves as the conveyer, ) of lying ]. (Msb.) It is said in a trad., biy^osa maTiy~apu Alr~ajuli zaEamuwA [(assumed tropical:) Very evil, or bad, is the man's conveyer zaEamuwA ]: i. e., when a man desires to journey to a country, or town, he mounts his camel, or beast, that serves to convey him, and journeys until he accomplishes the object of his want: therefore, that with which the speaker prefaces his speech, and by means of which he attains the object of his desire, when he says zaEamuwA ka*aA waka*aA , is likened to the camel, or beast, by means of which he attains the object of want: for zaEamuwA is [generally] said only in the case of a narration that has no authority whereon to rest, and that contains no proof. (TA.) IKh says that Alz~aEomu is used in relation to that which is discommended; and that its primary signification is said by some of the expositors of the Kur-án to be The act of lying: (TA: [this signification is also given in the K, as being contr. to the first:]) some say that it is metonymically used in this sense: (Msb:) and it is expl. as having this meaning in the Kur [vi. 137], where it is said, faqaAluwA h`*aA lil~`hi bizaEomihimo , i. e. [ And they have said, “ This belongeth unto God, ”] with their lying. (Lth, TA.) ― -b2- [Sometimes] zaEamahu signifies He described him, or it. (Har p. 204.) ― -b3- And sometimes zaEama signifies He promised: whence the saying of ' Amr Ibn-Sha-s, taquwlu halakonaA A_ino halakota waA_in~amaA EalaYA@ll~`hu A^arozaAqu AlEibaAdi kamaA zaEamo [ Thou sayest, or she says, “ We perish if thou perish: ” but verily upon God lie the means of subsistence of mankind, i. e. it lies upon Him to supply these, as He has promised ]. (TA.) ― -b4- Alz~aEomu is used also in the sense of AlZ~an~u : (Msb, TA:) one says, fiY zaEomiY ka*aA [ In my opinion it is thus ]. (Msb.) [Hence, likewise,] zaEamotaniY ka*aA , (K,) aor. tazoEumuniY , (TA,) Thou thoughtest me to be thus. (K, TA.) Aboo-Dhu-eyb says, faA_ino tuzoEumiyniY kunotu A^ajohalu fiykumu faA_in~iY $arayotu AlHiloma baEodaki biAljaholi [ And if thou think me such that I used to be ignorant, or to act ignorantly, among you, know that I have purchased intelligence since I was with thee ( baEodaki being for baEoda EahodiY biki ) in exchange for ignorance ]. (TA. [The meaning of tzEmynY is there indicated by the context.]) ― -b5- It is also used in the sense of AlAiEotiqaAdu : whence the saying in the Kur [lxiv. 7], zaEama A@l~a*iyna kafaruw A^ano lano yuboEavuwA [ They who have disbelieved our revelations have believed, or firmly believed, that they shall not be raised from the dead ]. (Msb.) ― -b6- Sometimes, also, zaEama is used in the sense of $ahida : as in the saying of En-Nábighah, zaEama AlhumaAmu biA^an~a faAhaA baAridN [app. meaning The magnanimous chief bore witness that her mouth was cool ]. (TA.) -A2- zaEama bihi , (S, Msb, K,) aor. (S, Msb) and , (Msb,) inf. n. zaEomN (S, Msb, K) and zaEaAmapN , (S, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) He was, or became, responsible, answerable, amenable, surety, or guarantee, for it; (S, Msb, K;) namely, property. (Msb.) ― -b2- And zaEama , like qatala , (Msb,) or zaEuma , like karuma , (TA,) aor. , inf. n. zaEaAmapN , He was, or became, chief, lord, master, or prince, (Msb, TA,) of a people, (TA,) or EalaY qawomK [ over a people ]; (Msb;) or spokesman of a people. (TA.) -A3- See also 4, in two places. -A4- zaEima , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. zaEamN (S, TA) and zaEomN , (TA,) He coveted, or eagerly desired. (S, K.) [Like its syn. TamiEa , it is trans. by means of fiY .] One says, ↓ zaEima fulaAnN fiY gayori mazoEamK , i. e. TamiEa fY gayori maToEamK [ Such a one coveted a thing not to be coveted; meaning, a thing of which the attainment was remote, or improbable: see art. TmE ]. (TA.) And ' Antarah says, Eul~iqotuhaA EaraDFA waA^aqotulu qawomahaA zaEamFA laEamoru A^abiyka layosa bimazoEami (S,) i. e. I became enamoured of her unintentionally, [or accidentally, ] while I was slaying her people; eagerly desiring her love: by the life of thy father, I swear, this is not a [ fit ] occasion for eager desire: i. e. I can not attain to holding communion of love with thee, [or with her,] any day, while there is this conflict and hostility between the two tribes: (EM p. 222:) layosa bimazoEamK meaning layosa bimaTomaEK : (S:) or, [as some relate it,] zaEomFA warab~i Albayoti layosa bimazoEami [ eagerly desiring: by the Lord of the House (i. e. the Kaabeh), &c.]. (TA. [ zaEomFA is there expressly said to be thus: but the measure does not require its being so.])

rawSourceText: , (S, Msb,) aor. , (Msb, MS, JM, [not mentioned in the S nor in the K, app. because well known,]) inf. n. zaEomN and zuEomN and zEomN , (S, Msb, K,) the first of the dial. of El-Hijáz, (Msb, TA,) the second of the dial. of [the tribe of] Asad, (Msb,) or Benoo-Temeem, (TA,) and the third of the dial. of some of [the tribe of] Keys; (Msb;) [generally best rendered He asserted; for it mostly relates to a thing not certainly known: or] he said; (S, Msb, K;) as in the phrases zaEamati AlHanafiy~apN [ The Hanafees said or asserted, or have said or asserted, ] and zaEama siybawayohi [ Seebaweyh said or asserted, or has said or asserted ]; (Msb;) [and zaEama A^an~ahu ka*aA He said, or asserted, that it was thus; ] either truly or falsely: (K:) mostly used in relation to a thing respecting which there is doubt, (Sh, Az, Msb, K,) and which is not certainly known: (Sh, Az, Msb:) or it is mostly used in relation to that which is false, or that respecting which there is doubt, or suspicion: (El-Marzookee, Msb:) or, as those skilled in the language of the Arabs say, in relation to a thing of which the speaker doubts, and does not know whether it may not be false: (Lth:) or zaEama zaEomFA means he related a piece of information not knowing whether it were true or false. (IKoot, Msb.) Hence the saying, zaEama maTiy~apu Alka*ibi [i. e. (assumed tropical:) zaEama is the conveyer, or vehicle, (properly the camel, or beast, that serves as the conveyer, ) of lying ]. (Msb.) It is said in a trad., biy^osa maTiy~apu Alr~ajuli zaEamuwA [(assumed tropical:) Very evil, or bad, is the man's conveyer zaEamuwA ]: i. e., when a man desires to journey to a country, or town, he mounts his camel, or beast, that serves to convey him, and journeys until he accomplishes the object of his want: therefore, that with which the speaker prefaces his speech, and by means of which he attains the object of his desire, when he says zaEamuwA ka*aA waka*aA , is likened to the camel, or beast, by means of which he attains the object of want: for zaEamuwA is [generally] said only in the case of a narration that has no authority whereon to rest, and that contains no proof. (TA.) IKh says that Alz~aEomu is used in relation to that which is discommended; and that its primary signification is said by some of the expositors of the Kur-án to be The act of lying: (TA: [this signification is also given in the K, as being contr. to the first:]) some say that it is metonymically used in this sense: (Msb:) and it is expl. as having this meaning in the Kur [vi. 137], where it is said, faqaAluwA h`*aA lil~`hi bizaEomihimo , i. e. [ And they have said, “ This belongeth unto God, ”] with their lying. (Lth, TA.) ― -b2- [Sometimes] zaEamahu signifies He described him, or it. (Har p. 204.) ― -b3- And sometimes zaEama signifies He promised: whence the saying of ' Amr Ibn-Sha-s, taquwlu halakonaA A_ino halakota waA_in~amaA EalaYA@ll~`hu A^arozaAqu AlEibaAdi kamaA zaEamo [ Thou sayest, or she says, “ We perish if thou perish: ” but verily upon God lie the means of subsistence of mankind, i. e. it lies upon Him to supply these, as He has promised ]. (TA.) ― -b4- Alz~aEomu is used also in the sense of AlZ~an~u : (Msb, TA:) one says, fiY zaEomiY ka*aA [ In my opinion it is thus ]. (Msb.) [Hence, likewise,] zaEamotaniY ka*aA , (K,) aor. tazoEumuniY , (TA,) Thou thoughtest me to be thus. (K, TA.) Aboo-Dhu-eyb says, faA_ino tuzoEumiyniY kunotu A^ajohalu fiykumu faA_in~iY $arayotu AlHiloma baEodaki biAljaholi [ And if thou think me such that I used to be ignorant, or to act ignorantly, among you, know that I have purchased intelligence since I was with thee ( baEodaki being for baEoda EahodiY biki ) in exchange for ignorance ]. (TA. [The meaning of tzEmynY is there indicated by the context.]) ― -b5- It is also used in the sense of AlAiEotiqaAdu : whence the saying in the Kur [lxiv. 7], zaEama A@l~a*iyna kafaruw A^ano lano yuboEavuwA [ They who have disbelieved our revelations have believed, or firmly believed, that they shall not be raised from the dead ]. (Msb.) ― -b6- Sometimes, also, zaEama is used in the sense of $ahida : as in the saying of En-Nábighah, zaEama AlhumaAmu biA^an~a faAhaA baAridN [app. meaning The magnanimous chief bore witness that her mouth was cool ]. (TA.) -A2- zaEama bihi , (S, Msb, K,) aor. (S, Msb) and , (Msb,) inf. n. zaEomN (S, Msb, K) and zaEaAmapN , (S, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) He was, or became, responsible, answerable, amenable, surety, or guarantee, for it; (S, Msb, K;) namely, property. (Msb.) ― -b2- And zaEama , like qatala , (Msb,) or zaEuma , like karuma , (TA,) aor. , inf. n. zaEaAmapN , He was, or became, chief, lord, master, or prince, (Msb, TA,) of a people, (TA,) or EalaY qawomK [ over a people ]; (Msb;) or spokesman of a people. (TA.) -A3- See also 4, in two places. -A4- zaEima , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. zaEamN (S, TA) and zaEomN , (TA,) He coveted, or eagerly desired. (S, K.) [Like its syn. TamiEa , it is trans. by means of fiY .] One says, ↓ zaEima fulaAnN fiY gayori mazoEamK , i. e. TamiEa fY gayori maToEamK [ Such a one coveted a thing not to be coveted; meaning, a thing of which the attainment was remote, or improbable: see art. TmE ]. (TA.) And ' Antarah says, Eul~iqotuhaA EaraDFA waA^aqotulu qawomahaA zaEamFA laEamoru A^abiyka layosa bimazoEami (S,) i. e. I became enamoured of her unintentionally, [or accidentally, ] while I was slaying her people; eagerly desiring her love: by the life of thy father, I swear, this is not a [ fit ] occasion for eager desire: i. e. I can not attain to holding communion of love with thee, [or with her,] any day, while there is this conflict and hostility between the two tribes: (EM p. 222:) layosa bimazoEamK meaning layosa bimaTomaEK : (S:) or, [as some relate it,] zaEomFA warab~i Albayoti layosa bimazoEami [ eagerly desiring: by the Lord of the House (i. e. the Kaabeh), &c.]. (TA. [ zaEomFA is there expressly said to be thus: but the measure does not require its being so.])

definition: He made a person to be such as is termed zaEiym ;
sourceDefinition: He made a person to be such as is termed zaEiym ; (Msb, TA;) as meaning responsible, answerable, amenable, surety, or guarantee. (Msb.) You say, A^azoEamotuka AlmaAla , (Msb,) or Al$~aYo'a , (TA,) I made thee, or have made thee, responsible, &c., (Msb, TA, *) [ for the property, or the thing; ] i. e. zaEiymFA bihi . (Msb, TA.) -A2- He made one to covet, or eagerly desire. (S, K.) You say, A^azoEamotuhu . (S.) [And A^azoEamotuhu fiY Al$~aYo'i I made him to covet, or eagerly desire, the thing; like as you say, A^aTomaEotuhu fiyhi . See zaEima .] -A3- He obeyed (K, TA) the zaEiym [i. e. chief, lord, or prince ]. (TA.) -A4- It (an affair) was, or became, possible. (K.) ― -b2- It (milk) began to become good, or pleasant; [or fit to be drunk; ] as also ↓ zaEama , (K,) inf. n. zaEomN . (TA.) ― -b3- AzEmt said of a young she-camel, or of one full-grown, She was thought to have fat in her hump. (IKh, TA. (IAar, K, TA.)

definition: [ Ginger; amomum zinziber; ] a certain plant growing in the country of the Arabs, in the land of 'Omán, (AHn, TA,) and in El-Yemen also; (TA;) well known: (S:) [or the root thereof; ] a certain root,...
sourceDefinition: [ Ginger; amomum zinziber; ] a certain plant growing in the country of the Arabs, in the land of 'Omán, (AHn, TA,) and in El-Yemen also; (TA;) well known: (S:) [or the root thereof; ] a certain root, or roots, (accord. to different copies of the K,) creeping beneath the ground; (K, TA;) burning, or biting, to the tongue; (TA;) growing like the stalks of the papyrus, (K, TA,) and the raAsan [mentioned below]: there is no wild sort of it; nor is it a tree that is eaten fresh like as herbs, or leguminous plants, are eaten; but it is used in a dry state; and its conserve is the best of conserves; and the best thereof is what is brought from the country of the Zinj and China: (TA:) it has a property that is heating, or warming, digestive, lenitive in a small degree, strengthening to the venereal faculty, (K, TA,) clearing to the phlegm, (TA,) sharpening to the intellect, (K * TA,) and exhilarating: (TA:) if mixed with the moisture of the liver of the goat, and dried, and pulverized, and used as a collyrium, it removes the film [ upon the eye ], and obscurity of the sight. (K, TA.) ― -b2- It is mentioned in the Kur, where it is said, [lxxvi. 17 and 18,] kaAna mizaAjuhaA zanojabiylFA EayonFA fiyhaA tusam~aY salosabiylFA [ The admixture whereof shall be znjbyl , a fountain therein named Selsebeel ]: i. e. it shall have the flavour of znjbyl [or ginger], which the Arabs esteem very pleasant: it may mean that znjbyl is [essentially] in the wine of Paradise: or that it is the admixture thereof: or that it is a name for the fountain whence this wine is taken, and which is named Selsebeel also. (Az, O, TA.) As some assert, (ISd, TA,) it means also Wine [absolutely]. (S, ISd, K.) ― -b3- zanojabiylu AlkilaAbi A certain herb, or leguminous plant, the leaves of which are like [ those of ] the xilaAf [or salix Aegyptia ], and the twigs are red: it clears the [ discoloration of the face termed ] kalaf , and the [ spots in the skin termed ] nama$ ; and it kills dogs; (K;) wherefore it is named in relation to them. (TA.) ― -b4- zanojabiylu AlEajami i. q. AlA^u$oturogaAzu [a word of Persian origin, now applied by Arabs to A species of carline thistle ]. (K.) [Accord. to Freytag, Horminum, or salvia silvestris: but this, I believe, is what is called in Pers. A^u$oturogaAn .] ― -b5- zanojabiylu Al$~aAmi i. q. Alr~aAsanu [ Inula helenium, common inula, or elecampane ]. (K.)

sourceDefinition: [ A piece of stick, or wood, for producing fire;; ] the upper one of the two pieces of stick, or wood, ( EuwdaAni , S, M, L, K, or xa$abataAni , L,) with which fire is produced [ in a manner described below ]; (S, M, L, K;) of the masc. gender; (Msb;) [or masc. and fem.: (see miyqaAdN , in art. wqd :)] and ↓ zanodapN is the appellation of the lower one thereof, (S, M, L, K,) in which is the notch, or hollow, ( furoDap , M, L, or faroD , A in art. frD ,) or in which is a hole ( vaqob , S), [ whence the fire is produced; ] and this is fem.: (S, M:) one end of the zanod is put into the faroD of the zanodap , and the zanod is then [ rapidly ] twirled round, in producing fire: (A in art. frD :) [the best kind of zanod is made of EafaAr ; and the best kind of ↓ zanodap , of marox : (see these two words:)] the dual zanodaAni is applied to the two together; (S, M, L;) [and so, very often, is the sing. zanodN :] one should not say zanodataAni ; (S, M, L, K;) for it is a well-known rule that predominance is to be attributed to the masc.: (MF:) the pl. sourceDefinition: A durojap (K, TA) consisting of a stone wrapped up in pieces of rag (TA) which is stuffed into a she-camel's vulva, when she is made to take a liking to the young one of another: (K:) it has a string attached to it; and when it distresses her, they pull it out, and she imagines that she has brought forth a young one: so say AO and others. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yazuwlu , (K,) and, accord. to the K, also yazaAlu , which is rare, on the authority of Aboo- 'Alee, but this is the aor. of zaAla like xaAfa , [which has a different meaning from the former verb,] (MF, TA,) inf. n. zawaAlN (K) and zuwuwlN (Lh, K) [which in all its senses except one mentioned below may app. be pronounced also zuw^uwlN , like Huw^uwlN for HuwuwlN , pl. of HawolN ,] and zawiylN and zawolN , (K, TA,) the last thus, with fet-h, accord. to a rule of the K, but in some of the copies zuwlN , with damm, (TA,) and zawalaAnN , (K,) It went away; passed away; departed; removed; shifted; (K, TA;) was, or became, remote, or absent; ceased to be or exist, or came to nought; (TA;) as also ↓ Aizowal~a , inf. n. AizowilaAlN ; (K;) or, accord. to the O, ↓ AizowaA^al~a , like AiTomaA^an~a . (TA.) [See also 7.] Hence, Ald~unoyaA wa$iykapu Alz~awaAli [ The world, or worldly enjoyment or good, is quick in passing away, or coming to nought ]. (TA.) And zAl zawaAluhu , and zawaAluhaA : see zawaAlN : and for the former see also zawiylN . And zAl zawiyluhu , and zawiyluhaA : see zawiylN . And zAl Al$~aYo'u Eano makaAnihi , (S, TA,) or mawoDiEihi , (Msb,) aor. yazuwlu , inf. n. zawaAlN (S, Msb, TA) &c., as above, (TA,) The thing removed, went away, [or ceased, ] from its place; it left, or quitted, its place. (TA.) And zulotu Eano makaAniY , inf. n. zawaAlN and zuwuwlN , [ I went away, &c., from my place. ] (K.) [And zAl Eanohu , said of any affection of the mind or body, It went away, passed away, or ceased, from him; it left him, or quitted him. ] And zaAluwA Eano makaAnihimo They turned away from their place; or returned, or went back, and fled, from it. (TA.) And zAl Eani Alr~aA^oYi , aor. yazuwlu , inf. n. zuwuwlN , [ He turned, or swerved, from the opinion, or judgment, or sentiment. ] (Lh, TA.) And zAl alone, aor. yazuwlu , He, or it, quitted his, or its, place. (AHeyth, TA.) And He removed from one town, or country, to another. (TA.) And zAlt Alxayolu birukobaAnihaA , (K,) inf. n. ziyaAlN , (TA,) The horses removed from their place with their riders. (K, TA. [Said in the TA to be tropical; but I see not why.]) ― -b2- Hence, zAlt Al$~amosu , inf. n. zawaAlN and zuwuwlN , without ' , (K,) as Th says, (TA,) and ziyaAlN and zawalaAnN , (tropical:) The sun declined from the meridian. (K, TA.) [And sometimes it signifies (assumed tropical:) The sun set: see 1 in art. dlk .] ― -b3- And hence, but not with zuwuwlN for an inf. n. in the senses expl. in this sentence and the next following it, (TA,) zAl Aln~ahaAru , (K, TA,) inf. n. zawaAlN (TA) [and app. ziyaAlN and zawalaAnN ], (tropical:) (tropical:) The day became advanced, the sun being somewhat high; syn. AirotafaEa : (K, TA:) or, as some say, went away; or departed. (TA.) And zAl AlZ~il~u , (TA,) or AlZ~il~i ↓ zAl zaAy^ilu , (K, TA,) (tropical:) (tropical:) The sun became high, and the shade contracted, or decreased, or went away, at midday. (K, * TA.) ― -b4- zAl ZEnhm , [thus in the TK (ed. of Boolák), i. e. ZaEonuhumo , thus in the K, and thus only, the verb being indicated by a preceding phrase; in the TA zAlt ZEnhm . which is an evident mistranscription;] inf. n. zayoluwlapN , (K,) like qayoluwlapN [an inf. n. of qaAla , aor. yaqiylu ; but more properly compared to dayomuwmapN , an inf. n. of daAma , aor. yaduwmu ]; (TA;) [a phrase which may be rendered Their journeying ceased for a while;] expl. as meaning Aiy^otawawoA makaAnahumo vum~a badaA lahumo [i. e. they abode in their place: then an opinion occurred to them different from their former opinion, so that it turned them therefrom, inducing them to remove]: (K:) in the K is added Eanohu ; but this should be omitted: the passage is taken from the M; in which Eanohu refers to Lh as the authority. (TA.) ― -b5- zAl [having for its inf. n., app., zawaAlN and zawiylN and zawolN (see the first of these below)] signifies also It moved; or was, or became, in a state of motion, commotion, or agitation; syn. taHar~aka : so in the saying, raA^ayotu $abaHFA vum~a zaAla [ I saw a bodily form or figure: then it moved, &c.]. (TA.) And one says, huwa yazuwlu fiYAln~aAsi , meaning He moves much among men, or the people, and does not remain still, or stationary. (TA.) ― -b6- zaAlato lahu ↓ zaAy^ilapN means $axaSa lahu $axoSN [ A figure seen from a distance rose to his view ]. (TA.) ― -b7- And zAl bihi Als~araAbu The mirage raised, or elevated, ( rafaEa ,) and made apparent, him, or it. (TA.) -A2- maA zaAla yafoEalu ka*aA &c.: see in art. zyl . -A3- zAl , aor. yazuwlu , also signifies He affected acuteness or sharpness or quickness of intellect, cleverness, ingeniousness, skilfulness, knowledge, or intelligence: or did so, not having it: syn. taZar~afa . (IAar, TA.) [See also 5.] -A4- [As a trans. verb, it belongs to art. zyl , and app. to the present art. also.] See 4. You say, zAl zawaAlahu , or zAl A@ll~`hu zawalahu ; and zAl zawaAlahaA : see zawaAlN . And ziyla zawiyluhu and zawiyluhaA and zawaAluhu : see zawiylN : and for the first, see also zawaAlN . ― -b2- And zAlhu He separated himself from him; (K;) as also zAylhu . (S and K in art zyl [to which the latter exclusively belongs.])

(K.) [Accord. to the TA, it seems to be used properly in relation to real things, and tropically in relation to ideal things. (S.) (TA.) And malilotu muzaAwalapa h`*aA AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) [ I loathed, or was averse from, striving, or seeking, to accomplish this affair ]. (TA.)

definition: (S, Msb, K) and ↓ zawiylN and ↓ zawolN (K) are inf.
sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K) and ↓ zawiylN and ↓ zawolN (K) are inf. ns. of zaAla [q. v.]. (S, Msb, K.) ― -b2- And all signify Motion, commotion, or agitation. (TA in explanation of the first and last, and K in explanation of the second.) [Hence,] ↓ zaAla zawaAluhu , or zawaAlahu ↓ zaAla , (accord. to different copies of the K,) or A@ll~`hu zawaAlahu ↓ zaAla , (S in art. zyl , and TA,) and A@ll~`hu zawaAlahu ↓ A^azaAla , (S in art. zyl , and K and TA,) are imprecations of destruction, or perdition, or death, (S, K,) and trial, or affliction, upon him to whom they relate: (S:) or such are the [second and] third and fourth of these phrases: but the first is a prayer for one's continuance where he is, [or his continuance in life; lit.] meaning May his motion cease; [and hence, may he continue where he is, or continue in life: ] and, as expl. by ISk, the [second and] third and fourth [lit.] signify May [ He i. e.] God cause his motion to cease; [and hence, may He, or God, put an end to his life; ] these phrases being similar to the saying A^asokata A@ll~`hu naAm~atahu . (TA.) [Thus all four have virtually the same lit. signification. And the first has also another meaning; as will be seen below.] El-Aashà says, h`*aA Aln~ahaAru badaA lahaA mino ham~ihaA zawaAlahaA ↓ maA baAluhaA biAll~ayoli zaAla (S, TA,) [app. meaning This is the day-time: an opinion has arisen in her mind such as to turn her from her former opinion and induce her to absent herself, ( badaA='N , I suppose, being understood after badaA lahaA , like as it is after badaA lahumo in the Kur xii. 35,) in consequence of her anxiety: what will be her case in the night? may it (her phantom) be absent, like as she is absent: for] the meaning is said to be, zaAla AlxayaAlu zawaAlahaA : IAar says, he disliked the phantom only because it roused his desire: or [ zaAla may be here syn. with A^azaAla , so that] the meaning may be A@ll~`hu zawaAlahaA ↓ A^azaAla [ may God make her motion to cease ]; and this is corroborated by the reading of AA, zawaAluhaA , in the nom. case, [i. e. zawaAluhaA ↓ zaAla may her motion cease; ] which makes this an instance of [the license termed] AlA_iqowaA=' : this, he says, is an old proverbial phrase of the Arabs, and El-Aashà has used it as he heard it: others than AA read [ zawaAlahaA ,] in the accus. case, without A_iqowaA=' , holding the meaning to be, may her phantom be absent from us in the night like as she herself is absent in the day-time. (TA.) ↓ zawiyluhu ↓ ziyla , likewise, means His motion ceased, or may his motion cease: or, accord. to Z, he became fixed, or motionless, from fear; or may he become so. (TA in art. zyl .) [See also another rendering of this phrase in the next paragraph.] One says also, waAlEawiylu ↓ A^axa*ahu Alz~awiylu Commotion, or agitation, (K, TA,) and disquietude of mind, (TA,) and wailing, or raising of the voice in weeping, overcame him. (K, TA.) -A2- See also the next paragraph, in three places.
