definition: Much, or abundant: applied in this sense to property.
sourceDefinition: Much, or abundant: applied in this sense to property. (Ham p. 593.) [See also gamorN .] -A2- [ In a state of immersion; immerged. (See A^ataAnN ; and see also a verse cited voce A^ano , p. 106, first col.)] ― -b2- And [hence, perhaps,] gaAmirapN signifies Palm-trees ( naxolN ) not requiring irrigation: (AHn, K:) but Az did not find this to be known. (TA.) [See also mugotamirN .] ― -b3- Applied to land, (S, Msb, TA,) and to a house, (TA,) [but written with p when A^aroDN is mentioned, or daArN ,] it signifies the Contr. of EaAmirN ; (S, TA;) and thus, (TA,) waste; desolate; in a state the contrary of flourishing; in a state of ruin; syn. xaraAbN : (Msb, K, TA:) [land to which this term is applied is thus called] because overflowed by water, so that it cannot be sown; or because it is covered with sand or dust; or because water generally exudes from it, so that it produces only reeds and the barodiY~ [i. e. papyrus or other rushes]: by gaAmirN is meant *uw gamorK ; like as one says ham~N naASibN , meaning *uw naSabK : (TA:) or any land that is not tilled ( lamo yusotaxorajo ) so as to be fit for sowing (K, TA) and planting: (TA:) or land that is unsown, but capable of being sown: so called because the water reaches it and comes over it: of the measure faAEilN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN ; (S, Msb;) like the epithets in sir~N kaAtimN and maA='N daAfiqN ; and made of the measure fAl only to correspond to EaAmirN as its opposite: (S, TA:) waste land which water does not reach is not called gaAmirN ; (S;) but such is called qaforN . (Msb.) It is said in a trad., [which shows that the last two explanations given above are correct,] that 'Omar imposed a tax of a diroham and a qafiyz upon every jariyb [of land], both EaAmir and gaAmir : and this he did in order that the people might not be remiss in sowing. (Az, TA.)

By God, thou wilt not cease remembering Joseph, ] accord. to all the grammarians and the expositors of the Kur-án: (TA:) for the oath that is not accompanied by the sign of affirmation denotes negation. (K.) -A2- fataA^a , as a complete [i. e. an attributive] verb, signifies He stilled, quieted, or made to cease, syn. sak~ana , or, as some say, (TA,) he abated, or allayed, syn. kasara , and extinguished: thus says Ibn-Málik, as on the authority of Fr; and it is correct: AHei has erred in charging him with having committed a mistake: (K, TA:) for he says that it is a mistranscription for favaA^a , with the three-pointed v : it is mentioned also by IKoot and IKtt: and Fr states that one says, fataA^otuhu Eani AlA^amori meaning I made him to cease ( sak~anotuhu ) from the affair: and fataA^otu Aln~aAra meaning I extinguished the fire. (TA.)

definition: It (fear, S, A, O) excited him to lightness and unsteadiness;
sourceDefinition: It (fear, S, A, O) excited him to lightness and unsteadiness; unsettled him. (S, A, O, K.) waA@sotafozizo mani A@sotaTaEta minohumo biSawotika , in the Kur [xvii. 66], is expl. by Fr as meaning And excite thou to lightness and unsteadiness, or unsettle thou, when thou canst, with thy voice. (O, TA.) And in like manner, waA_ino kaAduwA layasotafiz~uwnaka mina AlA^aroDi , in the same [xvii. 78], is expl. by him (O, TA) as meaning, And verily they were near to unsettling thee from the land: (TA:) but some say the meaning is, they were near to frightening thee so as to excite thee to promptness of flight from the land. (O, TA.) And Astfz~hu Eano raA^oyihi He incited him, or excited him, to ignorance, foolishness, or wrong conduct, and levity, or unsteadiness, so as to make him swerve from his right sentiment, opinion, or judgment; like Aisotaxaf~ahu En rA^yh . (Az and TA in art. xf .) ― -b2- He incited him, or excited him, to be promptly obedient and submissive to him and to that which he desired of him; like Astxf~hu . (Ksh in xliii. 54.) ― -b3- He expelled him (Jel in xvii. 105, and K) from the land, (Jel,) or from his abode, and disturbed, or disquieted, or unsettled, him, (K,) so as to excite him to lightness and unsteadiness. (TA.) [See also 1, latter half.] ― -b4- He, or it, deceived him, or beguiled him, so as to cast him into destruction. (TA.) ― -b5- He slew him: so the verb is expl. by some in the Kur xvii. 78, quoted above. (TA.)

definition: and fisoTaATN (S, M, Msb, K) and fus~aATN and fis~aATN and fusotaATN and fisotaATN , (S, M, K,) the t in the last two, as it is not found in the pl.
sourceDefinition: and fisoTaATN (S, M, Msb, K) and fus~aATN and fis~aATN and fusotaATN and fisotaATN , (S, M, K,) the t in the last two, as it is not found in the pl., being a substitute for the [former] T in fsTAT , or rather for the [latter] s in fs~AT , because it is more regular to change the latter of two identical letters than to change the former, and because the two identical letters in fs~AT are together, whereas the two identical letters in fsTAT are separated, (M,) and fusotaAtN and fisotaAtN , (K,) altogether eight different forms, but MF observes that Esh-Shiháb El-Kastalánee gives twelve, [which, however, he does not transcribe, the remaining four being probably with fet-h to the f ,] (TA,) A tent of hair [ -cloth ]: (S, Msb:) or a great tent: (Mgh:) or a kind of structure (M, Z) used in travelling, less than the suraAdiq : (Z:) or the kind of structure called suraAdiq : (K:) pl. fasaATiyTu ; (M, Msb, TA;) for which they did not say fasaAtiyTu . (M, TA:) ― -b2- Hence fusoTaATN is applied to A city: (Z, TA:) any city: and particularly a city in which is the general place of assemblage of people: (TA:) a populous, or comprehensive, city; accord. to some: (Msb:) the place of assemblage of the people of a kuwrap [which means a city, and a district, or region ], (Lth, Az, K,) around their general mosque: (Az, TA:) or you say, fusoTaATu AlmiSori , meaning the place of assemblage of the people of the mSr [or city ], around their congregational mosque. (M.) fusoTaATu [so in two copies of the S] is [a name of] The city of miSor [the metropolis of Egypt]: (S:) or AlfusoTaATu is also the proper name of miSoruAlEatiyqapu , (K, TA,) the city so called, (TA,) which was built by 'Amr Ibn-El- 'Ás; (K, TA;) the city of mSr in old times; as also AlfisoTaATu : (Msb:) and AlbaSorapu . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: : see the preceding paragraph, in two places. ― -b2- Also He went forth, (S,) or came, (TA,) to the faDaA=' [q. v.]. (S, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence] AfDY fulaAnN A_ilaY fulaAnK Such a one came to, or reached, such a one: (M, Mgh, TA:) originally, became in the space, or the place, or quarter, of such a one: (M:) or properly, became in the faDaA=' of such a one. (Mgh.) And in like manner, AfDY A_ilayohi AlA^amoru [ The thing, or event, came to, or reached, him ]. (M.) And A^afoDayotu A_ilaY Al$~aYo'i I came to, or reached, the thing. (Msb.) Accord. to IAar, (TA,) AlA_ifoDaA='u properly signifies AlAinotihaA='u [i. e. The coming at last, or ultimately, or the reaching, to a person or thing]. (IAar, T, Msb, TA.) Hence the saying [in the Kur iv. 25], waqado A^afoDaY baEoDukumo A_ilaY baEoDK i. e. When one of you hath come, and betaken himself, to the other; (TA;) in which the verb is made trans. by means of A_ilaY because having the meaning [of AinotahaY or] of waSala : (M:) or this means, when one of you hath become alone with the other, agreeably with the original derivation; or, accord. to some, it is an allusion to mutual contact, skin to skin: or to copulation. (Mgh.) You say, AfDY A_ilaY A@moraA^atihi [ He went in to his wife: or] he became in contact with his wife, skin to skin: (S, Msb:) or it signifies, (M, K,) or signifies also, (S, Msb,) (tropical:) he compressed his wife: (S, M, Msb, K:) or he was, or became, with her alone in private, whether he compressed her or not. (M, K.) ― -b4- AfDY bihimo He reached with them, or brought them to, a wide, or spacious, place. (TA.) And AfDY bihi AlT~ariyqu A_ilaY waEorK mina AlA^aroDi [ The road brought him to a rugged tract of land ]. (K * and TA in art. wEr ) ― -b5- AfDY biyadihi A_laY AlA^aroDi He touched the ground with the palm of his hand (IF, S, Msb, K) in his prostration [in prayer]. (S, K.) And A^afoDayotu A_ilayohi biyadiY mino gayori HaAy^ilK I put my hand to it without anything intervening; i. q. masasotuhu (Msb in art ms .) ― -b6- A^afoDayotu A_ilaY falaAnK bisiriY [ I communicated, or made known, to such a one my secret ]: (S;) or A^afoDayotu A_ilayohi biAls~ir~i I acquainted him with the secret. (Msb. TA.) ― -b7- AfDY also signifies (assumed tropical:) He became poor: so says IAar: as though he came to the ground. (TA.) -A2- laA yufoDiY A@ll~`hu faAka , occurring in a trad., is a phrase expressive of a prayer, meaning May God not make thy mouth wide and empty. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence the saying of IAar, AlA_ifoDaA='u A^no tasoquTa Alv~anaAyaA mino taHotu wamino fawoqu [app. meaning that AifoDaA='N is the inf. n. of A^ufoDiYa signifying His central incisors, below and above, fell out: or he was caused to lose them ]: and hence [the epithet] AlmufoDaApu [and therefore hence also what here follows]. (TA.) ― -b3- AfDY AlmaroA^apa He made the woman's masolakaAni (i. e. her vagina and rectum, Msb) to become one, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, TA,) in devirginating her, (Msb,) or in compressing her; (TA;) the intervening part becoming rent: (Mgh, TA:) and so A^afaADahaA : (M, in which it is mentioned in art. fDY :) the epithet applied to her is ↓ mufoDaApN , (M, Mgh, Msb, K,) which is syn. with $ariymN . (S.)

definition: [originally an inf.
sourceDefinition: [originally an inf. n.: see 1.] The burning, or heat, and boiling, of Hell. (TA.) And Intenseness, or vehemence, of heat; (TA;) as also ↓ faworapN . (S.) ― -b2- faworu Al$~afaqi The remains of the redness in the western horizon after sunset: as also vaworuhu . (TA.) [See also faworapN .] -A2- And A time: (TA:) [or rather] the present time in which is no delaying. (Msb.) Thus in the saying, Al$~ufoEapu EalaY Alfawori [ The right of pre-emption is to be had ] in the present time in which is no delaying. (Msb.) ― -b2- And hence, A state in which is no delay. (Msb.) You say, jaA='a fulaAnN fiY HaAjatihi vum~a rajaEa mino faworihi [ Such a one came for the object of his want, ] then returned immediately, or at once: or, as some say, with the same motion with which he came, not ceasing from motion after it; properly, conjoining what was before the coming with what was after it, without tarrying. (Msb.) And A^atawoA mino faworihimo , meaning mino wajohihimo [i. e., app., They came in a headlong manner; like the phrase maDaY EalaY wajohihi ]; (M, K, TA; but the M has jaAw^uwA instead of A^atawoA ;) and this is said by Zj to be the meaning of mino faworihimo in the Kur iii. 121: (M, TA:) or qabola A^ano yasokunuwA [ before their resting, or ceasing from motion ]: (K, TA:) or mino faworihimo in the Kur ubi suprà means in the commencement of their procedure: (O:) or in, or at, their instant of time; (Ksh, Bd;) i. e. [ in, or at, the same instant, or] immediately: (Bd:) and A^atayotu fulaAnFA mino faworiY , meaning qabola A^ano A^asokuna [i. e. I came to such a one before my resting, or ceasing from motion ]. (S, O.) And you say, faEalotuhu mino faworiY , meaning I did it at once, or instantly. (T, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (accord. to the K,) or ↓ fuw~aArapN , (accord. to a copy of the M,) A source, or spring, of water: (M, K:) [the latter word is app. the right in this case; for] IAar says that ↓ fuw~aArapN is applied to a wave: and to a birokap [i. e. watering-trough, or the like; or basin, pool, pond; &c.]: and faw~aArapN , to anything that is not water: and in one place he says that daw~aArapN and faw~aArapN are applied to anything that does not move nor turn round; and duw~aArapN and ↓ fuw~aArapN to such as moves and turns round. (T, TA.) ― -b2- faw~aArapu Alwariki , with fet-h and teshdeed, signifies The hole, or perforating aperture, of the wrk [or haunch ]: (S, O:) or the faw~aArap , (K,) or ↓ fuw~aArap , (so in a copy of the M,) is an aperture in the warik [or haunch ], to the belly, or interior of the body, not obstructed by bone: (M, K:) [these two explanations plainly apply to the sacroischiatic foramen: but what here follows is consistent with what precedes, though somewhat less clear:] or the faw~aArataAni , (K,) or ↓ fuw~aArataAni , (accord. to a copy of the M,) are [ two parts, in the region of the pelvis, described as being ] sik~ataAni [a word which I do not find to have any proper meaning that would be here apposite, but which seems to be applied in this case, by a kind of catachresis, to two parts through which a weapon or the like may pass, ] between [ each of ] the haunch-bones or hip-bones ( bayona Alwarikayoni ) and the quHoquH [or ischium ], towards the side of the warik [or hip-bone ], (M, K,) not intervening as obstacles in the way to the belly, or interior of the body; and they are what become in a state of commotion in the act of walking, or going along. (M.) [See also AlfaAy^ilu , in art. fyl ] And accord. to Lth, the term faw~aArataAni , (O, and so in a copy of the T,) or ↓ fuw~aArataAni , (so in another copy of the T,) is applied to Two appertenances of the kari$ [or stomach, properly of a ruminant animal ], having within them two small nodous lumps ( gud~ataAni ), which latter are not eaten, and each of which is a piece of flesh in the midst of red flesh. (T, O.)

definition: Pure, sheer, mere, unmixed, unmingled, unadulterated, or genuine;
sourceDefinition: Pure, sheer, mere, unmixed, unmingled, unadulterated, or genuine; (As, S, A, K;) in, or in respect of, (As, S, A,) or applied to, (K,) meanness, sordidness, or ignobleness, and generosity, liberality, or nobleness, (As, S, A, K,) and anything: (K:) fem. quH~apN : and pl. A^aqoHaAHN . (S, A.) One says lay^iymN quH~N [ One that is mean, sordid, or ignoble, ] in whom is nought of generosity, liberality, or nobleness. (A.) And EabodN quH~N A pure, or mere, slave; one that is of purely servile condition; (S;) or such as is termed qin~N [which means the same; or one born of slave-parents; &c.]. (A.) And EarabiY~N quH~N A pure, or genuine, Arabian; one of pure Arabian race; fem. Earabiy~apN quH~apN : (S, A, TA:) as also kuH~N and kuH~apN ; in which the k is a substitute for the q ; for they said A^aqoHaAHN , but not A^akoHaAHN : [i. e. kuH~u is not a dial. var. of quH~N , because the former has no pl.:] or A^akoHaAHN is used as a pl. of kuH~N . (L in art. kH .) And A^aEoraAbiY~N quH~N and ↓ quHaAHN (K, TA) A pure, or genuine, Arab of the desert: or one who has not entered the towns, nor mixed with their inhabitants: (TA:) pl. A^aEoraAbN A^afoHaAHN . (S, TA.) And fulaAnN mino quH~i AlEarabi (ISk, A, * TA) and kuH~ihimo , (ISk, TA) Such a one is of the pure, or genuine, of the Arabs. (ISk, A, * TA.) ― -b2- Also Coarse, rough, or rude, in make, or in nature or disposition; applied to a man; (Lth, S, K;) as though he were purely so; (S;) and to other than man. (Lth, K.) ― -b3- And (hence, TA) Unripe, applied in this sense to a melon, or water-melon, (Lth, A, K, TA,) because of its dryness: (A:) or one in its last state: but Az says that Lth has erred in explaining the word in the former of these senses, and that the correct word is fij~N . (TA.)

definition: The root, foundation, origin, or source, of a thing or an affair;
sourceDefinition: The root, foundation, origin, or source, of a thing or an affair; its essence, or very essence; or what is, or constitutes, its most essential, or elementary, part; the ultimate element to which it can be reduced or resolved; its utmost point or particular; or its principal, or best, part; syn. A^aSoluhu (Kr, L, K, TA) and faS~uhu (K, TA) and xaAliSuhu . (L, K, TA.) One says, SaAra A_ilaY quHaAHi AlA^amori He reached, or arrived at, the root, &c., of the affair. (L.) And laqad waqaEotu biquHaAHi qur~ika , as also waqaEotu biqur~ika , I have become acquainted with ( Ealimotu ) all that thou knowest, nothing thereof being hidden from me. (Ibn-Buzurj, TA.) And laA^aDoTar~an~aka A_ilY quHaAHika I will assuredly make thee to have recourse to thine utmost effort, or endeavour, i. e. A_ilaY jahodika : or, as IAar says, lA DTr~n~k AlY tur~ika waquHaAHika , i. e. A_ilaY A^aSolika . (L. [See A^aSolN .]) ― -b2- See also quH~N , latter half.

sourceDefinition: [The ischium; i. e.] the bone that surrounds the posterior pudendum, (S, K,) somewhat above the qib~ [or end of the rump-bone ]: (S:) or the part where the two hip-bones meet, internally: or [rather] what intervenes between the two hipbones, and surrounds the xaworaAn [or anus, or part in which is the anus ]; the xwrAn being between the quHoquH and the EuSoEuS : or the lower part of the Eajob [or rump-bone, or root of the tail ], in the integuments ( TibaAq ) of the two hip-bones; somewhat above the qib~ : or the bone upon which is the place wherein the penis is inserted, next, or near, to the lower part of the rakab [or pubes ]: it is said in the T that it is no part of the extremity of the backbone, and that its place of junction, or meeting, is outside the EuSoEuS : also, that the upper part of the EuSoEuS is the Eajob , and its lower part is the *anab : or the ESES is the internal extremity of the backbone, and the Ejb is its external extremity, and the xaworaAn is the dubur : (L, TA:) or, accord. to IAar, i. q. EuSoEuSN . (O voce EukodapN .)

definition: , (S, M, A, Msb,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, A, Msb,) aor. , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. qaroSN , (S, M, Msb, Mgh, K,) [ He pinched him, or it, ] with the two fingers: (S:) or it (a person's skin) with his fingers, so as to pain him: (A:) or he took, or took hold of, it (a man's flesh) with his two fingers, so as to pain him: (K:) or he twisted round two fingers upon it, namely, a thing; or the extremities of the fingers, only: (Msb:) or he scratched him, or it, with his nails: and he pressed, or squeezed, or pinched, him, or it, with the fingers, so as to pain: (M:) or he took it with the ends of his fingers: (Mgh, CK: [one of the explanations of AlqaroSu in the latter being AlqaboSu :]) or he seized it (so accord. to a MS. copy of the K, [the inf. n. being there rendered by AlqaboDu ; in the place of which I find in the TA, AlqrD ; but this I think a mistranscription;]) with the two fingers, (so in some copies of the K, and in the TA,) so as to pain. (TA.) You say also, qaraSahu biZuforayohi He took [or pinched ] his skin with his two nails. (Z, Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (tropical:) It (a flea) bit him: (S, K:) also said of a gnat; (A, TA;) and of a serpent. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, (tropical:) [as meaning It pinched him, or pained him, ] said of the cold. (A, TA.) ― -b4- And qaraSa , aor. and inf. n. as above, [and quruwSapN seems to be another inf. n. of the same,] (tropical:) It (beverage) bit the tongue. (M.) You say also of [the beverage called] nabiy* , fiyhi quruwSapN (tropical:) In it is a biting quality, affecting the tongue. (A, TA.) ― -b5- Also, qaraSahu bilisaAnihi , (M, Msb,) inf n. qaroSN , (Msb,) (tropical:) He hurt him with his tongue, by saying something which gave pain. (M, * Msb.) And laA tazaAlu taqoruSuniY minoka qaAriSapN (tropical:) [ A hurtful saying proceeding from thee does not cease to hurt me ]. (A.) ― -b6- qaraSahu also signifies He took it, (M, TA,) or cut it in pieces, namely, anything, (TA,) between two things; (M, TA;) as also ↓ qr~Shu : (Msb:) or the former signifies [simply] he cut it: (K:) and the latter, he cut it in pieces. (A.) Hence, (TA,) A^uqoruSiyhi biAlmaA'i , (S, Mgh, * Msb, * TA,) or bAlmA' ↓ qar~iSiyhi , (S, M, TA,) said in a trad., (S, M, Msb,) respecting the menstrual blood, (S, M,) accord. to different relations: (S, TA:) the latter means, Separate thou its particles [so I here render qaT~iEiyhi ] with water; (A'Obeyd, S, TA;) and the former has a similar [but less intensive] meaning: (TA:) or the former means, wash it with the ends of thy fingers; (S, Msb;) and remove it with the nail or the like: (Msb:) or take it [ off ] with the ends of the fingers: (Mgh:) or rub it hard with the ends of the fingers and the nails, and pour upon it water, so as to remove it and the mark of it. (Az, in Msb, art. Ht ; and IAth, * in TA, in the present art.) ― -b7- You say also, qaraSa AlEajiyna , (A,) inf. n. qaroSN ; (K;) or ↓ qr~Shu ; (M;) He cut the dough to spread it out: (M, A:) or the former, [simply,] he spread out the dough: (K:) or qaraSati AlEajiyna , aor. , inf. n. as above, (S, TA,) she cut the dough, (S,) or spread it out and cut it, (TA,) into pieces, each such as is termed quroSap : (S, TA:) and ↓ qur~Sthu , (S, Msb,) inf. n. taqoriySN , (S, K,) she cut it into many pieces, (S, Msb, K,) each such as is termed quroSap , (S,) or quroS . (Msb.) -A2- qariSa , aor. , (K,) inf. n. qaraSN , (TK,) signifies daAma EalaY AlmunaAfarapi waAlgiybapi (tropical:) [ He continued in a course of mutual aversion and defamation ]. (K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ Cauliflower; ] the thickest species of kurunob ; (K;) called in the dial. of Egypt qaronabiyTN ; mentioned in the S in art. qbT ; [but only as a thing well known;] the author of the S regarding the n as augmentative: (TA:) it renders the breath stinking; and causes a thickness, or grossness, [app. of the humours; ] and she who uses its seed in the manner of a suppository in the vagina will not become pregnant: (K:) so say the physicians. (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b2- And qanaHa AlbaAba He hewed, or cut out, a wooden implement, ( called a qun~aAHap [q. v.], L,) and with it raised [ and opened ] the door; as also ↓ AqnHhu : (T, L, K, TA:) or [simply] he raised [ and opened ] the door with the wooden implement called a qun~aAHap ; and so ↓ qn~Hhu : (A:) [or] AlbAlba ↓ qn~H , (S, K,) inf. n. taqoniyHN , (K,) He adjusted ( A^aSolaHa ) a qun~aAHap to the door. (S, K.) -A2- And qanaHa , (K, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) said of one drinking, He satisfied his thirst, and, by reason thereof, raised his head; and showed, or expressed, dislike of drinking ( takaAraha EalaY Al$~urobi ); like ↓ tqn~H ; (K, TA;) which is the more approved [and to which, as well as to the former verb, both of the clauses of the explanation above relate, as will be shown by what follows]: in some of the copies [of the K] like ↓ qn~H : accord. to AHn, one says, qanaHa mina Al$~araAbi , aor. and inf. n. as above, meaning he sipped [ of the wine or beverage ]; and accord. to Az, ↓ taqan~aHotu mina Al$~araAbi , which, he says, is the prevailing expression: hence the saying of Umm-Zara, A^a$orabu ↓ faA^ataqan~aHu , i. e. I [ drink, and ] stop, or interrupt, drinking, and proceed leisurely therein: or, I drink after the satisfying of thirst: which latter explanation, mentioned on the authority of AZ, is that which is approved by Sh and Az, in opposition to Aboo-'Abd-Allah Et-Tuwál, who thought it to mean I drink by little and little. (TA. [See also this saying of Umm-Zara, with another reading of it, in the last sentence but one of art. qmH .])

sourceDefinition: A ram, or male sheep, whatever be his age: (M, TA:) or a male sheep [ that has entered his third year, ] when he has cast his central incisors: or when his tooth that is next to the central pair of incisors has come forth: (Lth, K:) [also applied in the present day to the wild sheep of the Arabian and Egyptian deserts and mountains; ovis tragelaphus: ] pl. [of pauc.] A^akobu$N and A^akobaA$N (K) and [of mult.] kibaA$N (S, A, K) [and app. kubuw$N ] and kubuw$apN , like SuquwrapN from SaqorN . (TA.) The female is not called kabo$apN , but naEojapN . (IJ. [See raAjilapN .]) ― -b2- [Hence,] (tropical:) The chief, or lord, of a people, or company of men; (S, K;) their leader: (K:) or their strenuous defender, or protector, and the one of them to whom others look. (TA.) You say, huwa kabo$u Alkatiybapi (A, TA) (tropical:) He is the leader of the army, or troop: (TA:) and humo kibaA$u AlkataAy^ibi (tropical:) [ They are the leaders of the armies, or troops ]. (A, TA.) And kibaA$N also signifies (tropical:) Heroes, or brave men. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) Aged and learned persons. (TA in art. xrf .) ― -b3- [Hence also, (tropical:) A buttress: and a corbel which juts out from a wall to support a superstructure: so in the present day: pl. kubuw$N .] You say, banawoA suwrFA HaSiynFA wawav~aquwhu biAlkubuw$i (tropical:) [ They built a strong town-wall, and made it firm with the buttresses ]. (A, TA.) [See also another ex. voce faSiylN .]

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (L,) inf. n. kad~N , (S, L, K,) He toiled; or was, or became, vehement, or severe, (S, A, L, K,) in work; (S, A, L;) he worked laboriously; (TA;) he fatigued himself, and hastened, in his work. (L.) [You say] bijad~ika laA bikad~ika By thy good fortune, not by thy toil, are things attained. A proverb. (L.) And laA tajoEalo Eayo$ahumaA kad~F Make not the life of them two a toil. (L, from a trad.) ― -b2- AlmasaAy^ilu kad~N yakad~u bihaA Alr~ajulu wajohahu Petitions are [ a cause of ] dispiriting: a man thereby impairs the brightness of his countenance. (L, from a trad.) -A2- kad~ahu , (L, K, aor. , inf. n. kad~N , (L,) He required of him toil, or vehemence, or severity in work, or persevering or constant exertion in striving to do a thing or in seeking a thing; as also ↓ Aktd~hu , and ↓ Astkd~hu : (L, K:) he fatigued or wearied or jaded him; (S, * L;) namely, a beast, and a man, &c.: (L;) [like dak~ahu ;] he plied, or pressed him, plied or pressed him hard, or harassed him, in constant work which he imposed upon him, so as to fatigue or weary him. (Az, L.) See also kad~N . ― -b2- kad~a (tropical:) He fatigued his tongue with speaking and his heart with thinking. (A, L.) ― -b3- kad~a , aor. , (L,) inf. n. kad~N , (L, K,) He exerted himself perseveringly, assiduously, constantly, or incessantly, (L, K,) in striving to do, effect, or accomplish, a thing, (L,) or in seeking [ a thing ]. (K.) ― -b4- kad~a , aor. , (L,) inf. n. kad~N , (S, L,) He sought (S, L) gain, (S,) or, sustenance, or the means of subsistence. (L.) -A3- kad~a , aor. , (L,) inf. n. kad~N , (S, L, K,) He pointed, or made a sign, with the finger, (S, L, K,) like as the beggar does. (S.) [It is also trans.] El-Kumeyt says, ganiytu falamo A^arodudokumu Einoda bigoyapK waHujotu falamo A^akodudokumu biAlA^aSaAbiEi [ I was rich, and I did not repel you on an occasion of exigency; and I was in want, and I did not point at you with the fingers ]. (S, L.) ― -b2- ↓ kud~uwniY faA_in~iY mukid~N (tropical:) Ask ye of me; for I give [ only ] when asked. Said by Ibn-Hubeyreh. (A [but in my copy of that work, the first word is written kid~uwniY .]) -A4- kad~a , [aor. .] (tropical:) He scratched, or scraped: (L:) he scraped off a soil from a garment: (TA:) he scratched perseveringly his head, and his skin, with his nails. (A.) ― -b2- kad~a , (TA,) [aor. ,] inf. n. kad~N , (K,) (assumed tropical:) He combed his head. (K, TA.) ― -b3- kad~a , [aor. ,] (tropical:) He (a beast) trod the ground with his hoofs. (A, * L.) -A5- kd~hu , (aor. , L,) He pulled or drew it out (i. e. a solid or a fluid thing) with his hand; as also ↓ Aktd~hu . (L, K.)

sourceDefinition: A nawarodjap (in the TA, nawarodaHap , with H unpointed,) made of myrtle, and of the branches of the [ kind of willow called ] xilaAf ( spread out, TA), upon which sweet-smelling plants are arranged, or disposed, in regular series, and which is then folded: (Lth, K:) the Nabathean word is knvA . (L.) It is a circular thing ( daAy^irap ) of myrtle, and of branches of willow, upon which sweet-smelling plants are disposed, or arranged, and which is then folded like a volume, or roll, and made in the form of a basket: the damsels prepare this for ornament in the days of the springseason, and amuse themselves with it. nwrdjp is an arabicized word, from the Persian nawarodho , pass. part. n. of nawarodiydano , and meaning “ folded, ” or “ twisted ” (TK, [as explained to me by a very learned Turk, who, however, thinks the words not very clear.])

sourceDefinition: Treasure; property buried (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) in the earth: (TA:) an inf. n. used as a subst.: pl. kunuwzN . (Mgh, Msb.) ― -b2- Hence, (TA,) it is applied in a trad. to (tropical:) Any property whereof the portion that should be given in alms is not given. (S, TA.) ― -b3- Property that is preserved in a receptacle. (TA.) ― -b4- Anything abundant, collected together, that is desired with emulation. (Sh, TA.) ― -b5- Gold: and silver. (K.) It is said in a trad., A^uEoTiytu Alkanozayoni mina AlA^aHomari waAlA^aboyaDi I have been given gold and silver. (TA.) ― -b6- (tropical:) [ A treasure of knowledge or science ]. You say, maEahu kanozN mino kunuwzi AlEilomi (tropical:) [ With him is a treasure of the treasures of knowledge or science ]. (A, TA.) In the Kur, xviii. 81, it is said to be used in a similar manner, as signifying not gold nor silver, but (tropical:) Science and books. (TA.) And it is said in like manner in a trad., A^alaA A^uEal~imuka kanozFA mino kunuwzi Aljan~api laA Hawola walaA quw~apa A_il~aA biA@ll~`hi (tropical:) [ Ho! I will teach thee a treasure of the treasures of paradise: There is no power nor strength but in God ]: meaning, that a reward is stored up [in paradise] for him who says this, and who describes himself thereby, like as a treasure is stored up. (TA.) ― -b7- Aboo-'Alee El-Kálee says, that it is used in a verse of 'Alkamah, which he does not quote, as signifying (tropical:) Fat; as a subst.; and adds, that it is the only instance known to him of its being thus used. (TA.) -A2- Also, That in which property is preserved, or guarded: (K, * TA:) and ↓ makonizN [or rather both] that in which property is buried, treasured, hoarded, laid up, reposited, or stored, in secret: pl. of the latter, makaAnizu . (A, TA.)

sourceDefinition: and yalanojajN and A^alanojajN , (S, L,) or yalanojuwju and yalanojaju and A^alanojaju , [all three imperfectly declinable, as being generic proper names and of foreign origin, borrowed from the Persian language,] and A^alanojuwjN and yalanojajN and yalanojuwjN [which last is omitted in the CK] and yalanojuwjiY~N (K) and A^alanojajN and A^alanojiyjN , (TA,) Aloes-wood; syn. Euwdu AlT~iybi , (L,) or Euwdu Albaxuwri : (K:) or the wood of another tree with which one fumigates: (L:) a certain wood with which one fumigates. (S.) The A and Y in Alnjj and ylnjj [&c.] are augmentative letters added to make these words quasi-coordinate to the class of quinqueliteral-radical words: an augmentative letter is not used for such a purpose at the beginning of a word unless there is also with it another augmentative letter: and such, here, is the n . (IJ.) Lh uses ylnjwj and Alnjwj and Alnjyj as epithets, writing EuwdN ylnjwj &c. (TA.) The wood thus called has a very beneficial effect upon a relaxed stomach, (K,) when eaten; and of the beneficial effects for which it is most celebrated are those which it produces upon the brain and the heart, when used for fumigation and when eaten. (TA.)

definition: The people warned, or cautioned, one another, or put one another in fear, (M, K,) of a terrifying evil.
sourceDefinition: The people warned, or cautioned, one another, or put one another in fear, (M, K,) of a terrifying evil. (TA.) (T, S, TA.)

definition: A vow, which a man makes to be binding, or obligatory, on himself;
sourceDefinition: A vow, which a man makes to be binding, or obligatory, on himself; (T, M, * K, * TA;) [either absolutely, or conditionally: (see na*ara :)] pl. nu*uwrN : (S, M, K: *) and in the following verse of Ibn-Ahmar, some say that nu*ur is pl. of na*orN , like as ruhunN is pl. of rahonN ; but others say that it is pl. of na*iyrN in the sense of mano*uwrN : kamo duwna layolaY mino tanuwfiy~apK lam~aAEapK tuno*aru fiyhaA Aln~u*uro [ How many a waterless desert glistening with the mirage, in which vows, or things vowed, are vowed, lie in the way to Leylà! ]. (S.) ― -b2- Also, (tropical:) The mulct for an intentional wound; used in this sense by Esh-Sháfi'ee, (T, TA,) and of the dial. of El-Hijáz; (TA;) i. q. A^aro$N , (T, A, K, TA,) which is of the dial. of the people of El-'Irák: (T, TA:) pl. nu*uwrN : (T, A, K:) said by Aboo-Nahshal to be only for wounds, small and great. (T, K. *) You say, liY qibala fulaAnK na*orN , (T, TS, L,) or Einoda fulaAnK , (K,) (tropical:) A mulct for a wound is owed to me. (T, K, &c.) And A^aEoTayotuhu na*ora juroHihi (tropical:) I gave him the mulct for his wound. (A.) Aboo-Sa'eed Ed-Dareer says that it is thus called liA^an~ahu nu*ira fiyhi , i. e., because it is made binding, or obligatory, for it; [namely, for the wound;] from the phrase na*arotu ElaY nafosiY . (T, TA.) ― -b3- [ A votive offering ]. -A2- See also nu*orN .

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, K,) and , (Msb, MF,) inf. n. naDoHN , (S,) He sprinkled a house, or chamber, [with water]: (S, K:) or he sprinkled it lightly: (TA:) naDoHN is like naDoxN ; and sometimes these two words agree, and sometimes they differ: (Lth:) some say that they both signify any sprinkling: (TA:) or the former signifies what is intentional; and the latter, what is unintentional. (IAar.) [See naDaxa .] ― -b2- naDaHotu Ealayohi AlmaA='a , inf. n. naDoHN , [ I sprinkled water, or the water, upon him ]. (As.) ― -b3- naDaHa , aor. , and , inf. n. naDoHN , He moistened, or sprinkled, a garment, or piece of cloth. (Msb.) ― -b4- A^aSaAbahu naDoHN mino ka*aA [ A sprinkling of such a thing came upon him ]. (TA.) ― -b5- naDaHato biyawolihaA She (a camel) sprinkled her urine. (TA.) ― -b6- naDaHa EaTa$ahu , (S, K,) aor. inf. n. naDoHN , (S,) (tropical:) It (water, TA,) moistened [or allayed ] his thirst, (S, TA,) and allayed it: (K. TA:) took it away: or almost took it away: (TA;) also (K) or naDaHa Alr~iYa , (TA,) he satisfied his thirst with drink: (K:) or he drank less than what would satisfy his thirst. (S, K.) ― -b7- naDaHa AlmaA='u AlmaAla The water took away the thirst of the camels &c.: or nearly did so. (T.) ― -b8- naDaHa AlmaA='a He (a camel) carried water from a river or canal or well to irrigate standing corn or the like. (Msb.) ― -b9- naDaHa He moistened a skin, in order that it might not break. ― -b10- naDaHa Aljul~apa , aor. , inf. n. naDoHN , He sprinkled the palm-leaf date-basket with water, in order that its dates might stick together: (L:) or he scattered forth its contents. (L, K.) ― -b11- naDaHa (inf. n. naSoHN , S,) He watered palm-trees, (K,) and standing corn &c., (TA,) by means of a camel carrying the water. (K.) ― -b12- suqiY Alz~aroEu naDoHA The standing corn &c. was watered by means of buckets, ( dilaA='a and guruwb ,) and camels carrying the water; not by means of a channel opened for that purpose. (TA.) ― -b13- h`*ihi naxolu tunoDaHu These are palm-trees that are watered [ by the means above mentioned ]. (S.) ― -b14- fulaAnN yasoqiY biAln~aDoH [ Such a one waters palm-trees &c. by the means above mentioned ]. (S.) ― -b15- yanoDiHu EalaY AlbaEiyri He drives the camel that carries the water for irrigation, watering palm-trees [ &c. ] (S) ― -b16- naDaHuwhumo biAln~aboli , (inf. n. naDoHN , TA.) (tropical:) They shot at them [or sprinkled them ] with arrows: (S, K:) they scattered arrows among them. like as water is sprinkled. (TA.) Mohammad said to the archers at the battle of Ohod, AinoDiHuwA Ean~aA Alxayola (tropical:) Shoot ye at the horses and their riders with arrows [ and so repel them from us ]. (S, * TA.) ― -b17- naDaHa farojahu , aor. and , (TA;) and ↓ AntDH and ↓ AstnDH [both of which are thus used as intrans.]: (K;) He sprinkled some water upon his pudendum after the ablution called AlwuDuwo' : (K:) as also AinotafaDa . (TA.) ― -b18- naDaHa biAlbawoli EalaY faxi*ayohi He made [ a little sprinkling of ] urine to fall upon his thighs. (K.) Hence the saying in a trad., Aln~aDoxu mina Aln~aDoHi , meaning, that he upon whom falls a little sprinkling of urine, like the heads of needles, as explained by Z, must sprinkle the part with water, and is not required to wash it. (TA.) ― -b19- naDaHatonaA Als~amaA='u The sky rained upon us. (L.) ― -b20- naDaHa , [aor. ,] He (a horse) sweated. (Msb.) naDaHa biAlEaraqi , inf. n. naDoHN and naDaHaAnN , He (a man, and a horse,) broke out with sweat: and in like manner, the protuberance behind a camel's ear ; and the arm-pit or the like. (L) [See an ex. in a verse cited in art. Edw , conj. 3.] ― -b21- yanoDaHu TybFA He diffuses the odour of perfume: lit., sweats it. (L, from a trad.) ― -b22- naDaHa It (sweat) exuded, or came forth. (Msb.) ― -b23- naDaHati Alqrobapu . (S, K,) and AlxaAbiyapu , (S,) aor. , inf. n. naDoHN and tan~aDaAHN , (S, K,) [the latter of an intensive form, The water-skin, and the jar. ( being thin, TA,) sweated, (ISk, S, K,) or exuded its water. (TA.) ― -b24- naDaHa Aljabalu The mountain sweated water between its masses of rock. (TA) ― -b25- naDaH Al$~ajaru , inf. n. naDoHN , TA,) (tropical:) The trees began to break out with leaves. (As, S, K.) ― -b26- naDaHa Alz~aroEu , and ↓ AnDH , (assumed tropical:) The standing corn became thick in its body, (TA,) and began to have the farinaceous substance in its grains, yet moist, or succulent, or tender. (K.) ― -b27- taDaHati AlEayonu , (L, K,) aor. , inf. n. naDoHN : (L.;) and ↓ AntDHt , (L, K,) and ↓ nnD~Ht ; (K;) The eye overflowed with tears: (L, K:) the eye filled with tears and the overflowed without stopping. (L.) ― -b28- naDaHa , aor. It (a sea, or great river,) flowed. (TA, art. tbr .) ― -b29- AinoDaHuwA Alr~aHima bibilaAlihaA : see bilaAlN . -A2- naDaHa Eano fulaAnK , (S, K,) aor. ; (S;) and Eanohu ↓ bADH , (K,) inf. n. munaADaHapu and niDaAHN ; (TA;) (tropical:) He repelled from, and defended, such a one: (S, K:) as also maDaHa : (Shujáa:) and naDHa Alr~ajula he repelled from the man. (Kr.) ― -b2- naDaHa Eano nafosihi (tropical:) He defended himself with an argument. a pled. or an allegation. (S.)

definition: (tropical:) A camel (S) or an ass or a bull (TA) upon which water is drawn ( yasotaqaY Ealayohi ) [ from a well &c.
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) A camel (S) or an ass or a bull (TA) upon which water is drawn ( yasotaqaY Ealayohi ) [ from a well &c. ]: (S, TA:) a camel that carries water ( yaHomilu AlmaA='a ) from a river or canal or well to irrigate seed-produce; so called because it is a means of moistening [or allaying] thirst by the water which it carries: (Msb:) the female is called naADiHapN (S, Msb) and saAniyapN [q. v.]: (S:) pl. nawaADiHu . (Msb.) ― -b2- Afterwards applied to Any camel: as in the following instance, occurring in a trad., A^aToEimohu naADiHaka Give him thy camel to eat. (Msb.) ― -b3- See naDoHN .

(L.) ― -b3- nafa*a Als~ahomu , aor. , inf. n. nufuw*N and nafaA*N , The arrow perforated, transpierced, or pierced through, the animal at which it was shot, and went forth from it: (Msb:) or nafa*a Als~ahomu Alr~amiy~apa , (M, L,) and nafa*a minohaA , (S, L,) and fiyhaA , (M, A, L,) aor. , (M, L,) inf. n. nafaA*N (M, A, L, K) and nufuw*N (A) and nafo*N , (M, L, K,) the arrow penetrated into the inside of the animal at which it was shot, and its extremity went forth from the other side, or protruded from it, the rest remaining therein; the extremity of the arrow passed through the animal at which it was shot, the rest remaining therein; (M, L, K;) a part of the arrow passed through, or went forth or protruded from, the animal at which it was shot. sourceDefinition: i. q. TaEonapN naAfi*apN ; (S;) A wound having a passage through the other side; by nafa*N being meant manofa*N , or nufuw*N : (T, L:) pl. A^anofaA*N . (A.) Keys Ibn-El-Khateem says (see Ham. p. 85), TaEanotu A@bona Eabodi Alqayosi TaEonapa vaAy^irK lahaA nafa*N lawolaA Al$~aEaAEu A^aDaA'ahaA (T, S, L) I pierced the son of 'Abd-El-Keys with the wound of one making an angry assault, that had a passage through, which, but for the spirtling blood, would have made it show the light through him. (T, L [See also $uEaAEN .]) See also manofa*N . ― -b2- nafa*N (tropical:) A place, or way, or means, of exit, escape, or safety; syn. maxorajN (T, S, A, L, K.) So in the saying A^ataY binafa*i maA qaAla (tropical:) He effected a means of escape from [ the natural consequences of ] what he had said; i. e., biAlmaxoraji minohu . (T, S, A, L, K.) It occurs in a trad., where it is said, that unless a man who has published against a Muslim a charge of which he is clear do this, he is to be punished. (T, A, L.)

definition: and ↓ naharN (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) A channel in which water runs: (A, K:) so most say: or the water itself [ that runs therein;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ naharN (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) A channel in which water runs: (A, K:) so most say: or the water itself [ that runs therein; i. e., a river; a rivulet; a brook; a canal of running water ]: (TA:) or a wide channel in which water runs: originally, the water [ that runs therein ]: (Mgh:) or properly, wide running water: and by a secondary application, which is tropical. (tropical:) the trench or channel [ in which it runs ]: (Msb, TA *:) pl. [of pauc.] A^anohurN , (Msb, K,) a pl. of the former, (Msb,) and A^anohaArN , (S, Msb, K,) a pl. of the latter, (Msb,) [but used as a pl. of either, both of pauc. and of mult. and the most common of all the pls.,] and nuhurN , (Msb, and so in some copies of the K,) with two dammehs, a pl. of the former, (Msb,) or nuhorN , (as in some copies of the K and in the TA,) and nuhuwrN , (IAar, K.) You say, jaraY Aln~ahoru [ The river ran, or flowed ]; like as you say, jaraY AlmiyzaAbu . (Msb.) And nahorN kaviyr AlmaA='i [ A channel of running water having much water ]. (A.) And ↓ naharN is also used in a pl. sense: as in the Kur, [liv. 54], fiY jan~aAtK wanaharK [ In gardens and among rivers ], i. e., A^anohaAri ; like the phrase in the Kur, (same chap. verse 45,] wayuwal~uwna Ald~ubora , (Fr, S.) meaning AlA^adobaAra , (Fr, TA:) but it is otherwise explained. (S.) See naharN below.

definition: Day; or day-time; contr. of layolN : (S, TA:) or broad daylight, (Mgh,) from sunrise to sunset: (Mgh, Msb, K:) this is the original signification: (TA;) or this is the signification in the vulgar...
sourceDefinition: Day; or day-time; contr. of layolN : (S, TA:) or broad daylight, (Mgh,) from sunrise to sunset: (Mgh, Msb, K:) this is the original signification: (TA;) or this is the signification in the vulgar conventional language: but in the classical language it signifies the time from the rising of the dawn to sunset: (Msb:) or the light between the rising of the dawn and sunset: (K:) and so accord. to the lawyers: (TA:) in the trads., it is the whiteness of the nhAr , and the blackness of the lyl ; and there is nothing intervening between the lyl and the nhAr : but sometimes the Arabs amplified, and applied nhAr to the time from the clear shining of the dawn to the setting [ of the sun ]: (Msb.) or (so accord. to the TA. but in some copies of the K, and the spreading of the light [ which is a cause ] of sight and its dispersion: (K:) in this explanation in the L, in the place of waA@fotiraAquhu we find waA@jotimaAEuhu [and its collecting together ]: (TA:) it is also syn. with yawomN ; and is so when used without restriction in the non-fundamental sciences of religion, ( AlfuruwE ,) as in the phrases Sumo nahaArFA [ fast thou a day ] and A_iEomalo nahaArFA [ work thou a day ]: and it may be so used, or in its proper classical sense, when prefixed to yawom , governing the latter in the gen. case: (Msb:) it has no proper dual, (Mgh, Msb,) and no proper pl., (S, Mgh, Msb, K, (like Ea*aAbN and saraAbN ; (S, K;) the former of which, however, has a pl. assigned to it [by Zj and] in the K, namely, A^aEo*ibapN ; (MF;) [and respecting the latter see $araAbN , with $ ;] [for] nhAr is a name applied to every yawom [or day ]; and layolN , to every layolap [or night]: one does not say nahaArN wanahaAraAni , nor layolN walayolaAni : but the sing. of nhAr is yawomN (TA.) and the dual, yawomaAni , (Msb, TA:) and the pl., A^ay~aAmN . (Msb:) and the contr. of ywomN is layolapN , so says Az, on the authority of AHeyth (TA:) or it has pls.: namely, A^anohurN , (IAar, S, K,) a pl. of pauc., (S,) in some lexicons A^anohirapN , (TA,) also a pl. of pauc.,] and nuhurN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) a pl. of mult. (S) [See also naharN .] Ibn-Keysán cites the following ex., lawolaA Alv~ariydaAn lamutonaA biAlD~umuro variydu layolK wavriydN biAln~ahuro [ Were it not for the two thereeds (or messes of crumbled bread moistened with broth ), we had died of leanness: the thereed of night, and thereed in the day-times ]. (S.)

definition: One in whom is sudden fright, or terror.
sourceDefinition: One in whom is sudden fright, or terror. and a shrinking ( talab~u* ) [ by reason of fear ]. (L.) ― -b2- habiytN and ↓ mahobuwtN A cowardly man, whose intellect is quitting him: (S, K:) a man without intellect. (TA.) ― -b3- In the saying of a poet, na$owatuhaA habiytu , quoted, limit not expl., by Th, hbyt is thought by ISd to be of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure faAEilN . and to signify, $aYo'N yahobitu , i. e. A thing that stupefies, or renders foolish, and confounds, perplexes, or amazes, and thus stills, or quiets and causes to sleep. The poet says, turiyka qa*FY bihaA A_ino kaAna fiyhaA buEayoda Aln~awomi na$owtuhaA habiytu [he is app. describing clear and strong wine, and says, It will show thee a mote in it, if it be therein: a little after sleep, (even,) the intoxication (which is the result) thereof is a thing that stupefies, &c. ]. (TA.)

definition: It (a place, A, Msb, or a place of alighting or abode, S, K) was, or became, desolate, deserted, or destitute of human beings;
sourceDefinition: It (a place, A, Msb, or a place of alighting or abode, S, K) was, or became, desolate, deserted, or destitute of human beings; (S, A, Msb, K,) the people having gone from it; (S, K;) as also ↓ twH~$ . (A, Msb, K.) And [in like manner you say of a land,] AlA^aroDu ↓ twH~$t , [and ↓ AstwH$t , (see A^aroDN waHo$apN , voce waHo$N ,)] The land was, or became waHo$ap (S, TA) [i. e. desolate, deserted, &c.] ― -b2- He (a man) was, or became, hungry; (S, A, K, TA;) not having eaten anything, so that his inside was empty; (TA;) as also ↓ twH~$ : (A:) or the latter signifies his belly became empty by reason of hunger. (S, K.) Also the former, His provisions became spent, or exhausted. (S, K.) You say, qado A^awoHa$onaA muno*u layolatayoni Our provisions have been spent for two nights. (S.) You say also, ↓ twH~$ lild~awaA='i (S, A, K *) He made himself hungry; (A;) or made his inside, (S,) or his stomach, (K,) empty of food (S, K) and beverage; (K;) for the purpose of drinking medicine. [See also an ex. from a poet, voce A^unosN : And see its quasi-pass., 10.]

definition: He put himself in an upright posture, not at his ease, in his manner of sitting;
sourceDefinition: He put himself in an upright posture, not at his ease, in his manner of sitting; he sat erect, not at his ease: (S, Mgh, K:) or he put down his knees [ upon the ground ] and raised his buttocks: (Aboo-Mo'ádh, K:) or he raised himself upon his legs, or feet, without having yet set himself firmly in a standing posture, but having prepared himself to leap, or spring, (Lth, K, TA,) or to go away: (Lth, TA:) or he sat in a posture as though he desired to rise and stand up; whether in the manner termed A_iqoEaA=' [i. e. sitting upon the ground with the shanks erect], or otherwise. (MF.)

definition: I made it to face the thing: (S, K:) and Al$~aYo'a ↓ qaAbalotuhu app.
sourceDefinition: I made it to face the thing: (S, K:) and Al$~aYo'a ↓ qaAbalotuhu app. signifies the same: see a verse of El-Aashà voce AirotisaAmN . ― -b2- A^aqobala bihi [ He turned it forward; contr. of A^adobara bihi ]. (S, K, art. dbr .) ― -b3- A^aqobala He came, facing; (JK, S, * K; *) came forward; came on; advanced; contr. of A^adobara . (S, K.) ― -b4- A^aqobalotu qibalaka [not qubolaka ] I advanced, or came, toward thee. Like qaSadotu qaSodaka . (L, art. Hrd .) See also Kur, ii. 172. ― -b5- A^aqobala Ealayohi He advanced, or approached, towards him, or it. ― -b6- A^aqobala EalaY A_inosaAnK , as though he desired no other person. (JK.) ― -b7- AqobaAlN The advancing of fortune; contr. of A_idobaArN . ― -b8- AlA_iqobaAlu fiY Ald~unoyaA [ Advance in the world, or in worldly circumstances ]. (Mgh in art. jd .) A_iqobaAlN signifies The being fortunate. (KL.) ― -b9- A_iqobaAlN i. q. dawolapN [ Good fortune; &c.; see tAmiku ]: and Eiz~apN [ might; &c.]. (Kull, p. 64.) ― -b10- A^aqobala Ealayohi He showed favour to him: or, more properly, he presented a favourable aspect to him; or, accord. to general usage, he met him kindly; see ba$~a lahu . ― -b11- A^aqobalato Ealayohi Ald~unoyaA , (A, art. ftH ,) The world favoured him. ― -b12- A^aqobala EalaY $aYo'K He set about, or commenced, doing a thing. (K, &c.) ― -b13- See taSad~ada . ― -b14- A^aqobala Ealayohi He clave to it: and he took to, set about, began, or commenced it; as also Elyh ↓ qabala . (K.) ― -b15- [ A^aqobala Ealayohi biAls~ayofi , and biAlEaSaA , and biAls~awoTi He advanced against him, or set upon him, with the sword, and with the staff or stick, and with the whip. ] ― -b16- You say, A^aqobala Ealayoh biAls~awoTi yaDoribuhu [ He advanced against him, or set upon him, with the whip, striking him ]. (S in art. Hwl .) ― -b17- See qabalN . ― -b18- yuqobilu biAld~alowi A_ilaY Albiy^ori and A^amoru fulaAnK AlaY A_iqobaAlK : see A^adobara . ― -b19- A^aqobal Ealayohi biAlt~aEoniyfi : see Har, p. 165 ― -b20- A^aqobilo EalaY nafosika [ Betake, or apply, thyself to thine own affairs ]. (T, voce A_ilaY .) ― -b21- dabarato lahu Alr~iyHu baEoda maA A^aqobalato : see dbr . ― -b22- A^aqobala [ He recovered, or regained, health; ] occurring in the K, as the explanation of vaAba jisomuhu . (K, art. vwb .) A^aqobala baEoda huzaAlK . (K, voce Ha$ama .) ― -b23- A^aqobala , with reference to the slit ear of a she-camel: see A^adobara . ― -b24- A^aqobilonaA bi*im~apK , app. a mistranscription for A^aqolibonaA : see *im~apN .

definition: He faced him, or it.
sourceDefinition: : see Aisotadobarahu . He faced him, or it. (TA) He turned his face towards him, or it. ― -b2- He came before his face. ― -b3- He went to meet him; he met him, or encountered him. He saw it before him: he looked forward to it: he saw it, or knew it, beforehand. He saw, or knew, at the beginning of it what he did not see, or know, at the end thereof. ― -b4- Astqblhu biA^amorK (T, S, K, &c., in art. bdh ) He met him, or encountered him, with a thing. or an affair, or an action. (TK in art. bdh .) ― -b5- Astqblhu bimaA yakorahu (A, K, in art. bkt , &c.) He encountered him with, or, as it often means, he accused him, to his face, of a thing that he disliked, or hated: see bak~atahu ; and the phrases Aalbohtu A@sotiqobaAluka A^axaAka bimaA layosa fiyhi and biAlka*bi ↓ qaAbalahu , voce bahatahu ; and Astqblhu biAlHaq~i , voce qaraHahu ; in both senses like laqiyahu bimakoruwhK . ― -b6- Aisotaqobalotuhu bikalaAmK fiyhi giloZapN [ I encountered him, or confronted him, with speech in which was roughness ]. (JK, M, TA, art. jbh .) ― -b7- Aisotaqobalahu He anticipated it; namely, Ramadán, by fasting before its commencement. (TA.) ― -b8- See 8.

definition: He was, or became, still, or stationary;
sourceDefinition: He was, or became, still, or stationary; (Msb;) [ he stood still; ] he continued standing: (K:) and [simply] he stood; contr. of jalasa . (TA.) ― -b2- waqafa Ald~aAb~apa , inf. n. waqofN , He made the beast to be, or become, still, or motionless. (Msb.) ― -b3- waqafa Ealayohi He stopped, or paused, upon coming to him, or it; he stopped, or paused, at it; or where he, or it, was. ― -b4- waqafa EalaY $aYo'K He paused at, and paid attention to, a thing. ― -b5- waqafa Ealayohi He comprehended it, namely, a meaning: he understood it. (TA. [Or, correctly, wuqifa , for it is there altered.]) ― -b6- He met with it; namely, a word or the like, in reading: often occurring in this sense. ― -b7- wuqifa Ealayohi He saw it: and he was introduced into it, and knew what was in it. (TA.) He was made to know it surely. See Bd, vi. 27 and 30. ― -b8- waqafotuhu ElY *anobihi I made him acquainted with, or made him to know, his crime, sin, fault, or the like; (S, K:) and so Ealayohi ↓ A^awoqafahu , q. v. (Mgh.) ― -b9- waqafa , aor. , inf. n. wuquwfN , He withstood, resisted: governing by Eano . ― -b10- waqafahu and ↓ A^awoqafahu and ↓ waq~afahu [ He bequeathed it, or gave it, unalienably: ] the first of these is the most chaste: the last is disapproved and rare. (TA, art. Hbs .) See muw^ab~adN .

definition: [ He made him to pause, or wait, at the thing, or affair ].
sourceDefinition: [ He made him to pause, or wait, at the thing, or affair ]. (K, TA, in art. vbT .) See the quasi-pass. tawaq~afa : and see vab~aTahu . ― -b2- waq~afahu , inf. n. tawoqiyfN He taught him the places of pausing, in reading. (Mgh.) And hence, He made him to know a thing. (Mgh.) ― -b3- waq~afahu EalaY Al$~aYo'i , meaning Ear~afahu A_iy~aAhu , He made him acquainted with the thing; informed him of it; gave him notice of it; though often occurring, for waqafahu Ealayohi , seems to be post-classical. It is used in this sense, or as meaning He (God) revealed to him the thing, in many places in the Mz, 1st nwE : as, for ex, in the following instance, cited from IF, waq~afa A@ll~`hu A=dama EalaY maA $aA='a A^ano yuEal~imahu A_iy~aAhu [ God taught, or revealed to, Adam what He pleased to teach him ]. ― -b4- waq~afa AlHadiyva , (JK,) inf. n. tawoqiyfN , (K,) He explained the tradition; syn. bay~anahu . (JK, K. *) ― -b5- tawoqiyfN , as a legal term: see naS~a EalaY $aYo'K m~aA . ― -b6- See 1

definition: (tropical:) He paused, or waited, at the thing;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) He paused, or waited, at the thing; syn. talab~ava . (IDrd, K, TA.) (Accord. to some copies of the K, tavab~ata .] You say, tawaq~afotu EalaY h`*aA AlA^amori (tropical:) I paused, or waited, at this thing, or affair. (TA.) And tawaq~afa EalaY jawaAbi kalaAmihi (tropical:) [ He paused, or waited, at the reply to his speech ]. (TA.) And hence, tawaq~afa EalaY Als~amaAEi He limited, or restricted, himself to what had been heard [from the Arabs, with respect to a construction, &c.]; did not transgress it, or overstep it. See mutawaq~afN . ― -b2- tawaq~afa fiyhi (assumed tropical:) He paused upon it; he hesitated, or deliberated, respecting it. Of very frequent occurrence. ― -b3- tawaq~afa Eani AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) He held, refrained, or abstained, from the thing, or affair. (Msb.) ― -b4- tawaq~afa EalaY ka*aA It (for instance, an opinion or a judgment, and the truth of an evidence or a demonstration, and the result of an inquiry or investigation) rested, was founded or grounded, depended, or was dependent, upon such a thing. You say, of knowledge, yatawaq~afu HuSuwluhu EalaY ka*aA Its origination rests upon such a thing; as, for instance, speculation.
